The platform offers a seller authentication program, curated collections and trending edits, buyer protection with returns and refunds, and integrated payments and shipping, operating primarily in Mexico. Gloset is backed by 500 Global. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, API reference, or technical documentation surface — it is a consumer marketplace web/app product.

providers.name: Greentoe
providers.description: Greentoe is a name-your-price e-commerce marketplace where shoppers make an offer on brand-new electronics, cameras, TVs and home theater, appliances, baby gear, watches, and optics, and manufacturer-authorized retailers compete to fulfill the order at the buyer's price. Built to bring the negotiation model of big-ticket purchases online, Greentoe reports more than $100M saved by its customers, backs every order with manufacturer warranties and a 30-day return policy, and is backed by 500 Global and Y Combinator. Greentoe operates as a consumer-facing web application and does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public web and security surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Haus Laboratories
providers.description: Haus Labs by Lady Gaga (formerly Haus Laboratories) is an American clean-beauty cosmetics brand founded by Lady Gaga. It first launched in September 2019 and relaunched in June 2022 with Sephora as its exclusive retail partner. The brand makes skincare-infused, high-performance color cosmetics and makeup — including its Triclone Skin Tech Foundation plus lip, eye, and complexion products — that are always vegan and cruelty-free. It sells direct-to-consumer through hauslabs.com and through Sephora. Haus Labs is a consumer packaged goods / beauty company with no public developer API; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record surfaced from the Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio.

providers.name: Jane (iHeartJane)
providers.description: Jane Technologies (iHeartJane) is a cannabis ecommerce and marketplace platform that powers real-time online menus, point-of-sale and kiosk checkout, order and reservation flows, and the Jane Universal Product Catalog for 2,500+ dispensaries and brands across the United States and Canada. Jane exposes a documented HTTP API (the Jane API, published as Swagger at api.iheartjane.com/jane-api-docs) for retrieving live store menu products and generating access tokens, and a partner Digital Merchandising SDK (Jane DM SDK) for embedding MyHigh-powered personalization and sponsored-product widgets into a retailer's own menu. Both surfaces are partner-gated - access requires approval and credentials from a Jane account representative - so the endpoints listed here are modeled from Jane's public documentation rather than exercised against a live, open, unauthenticated API.

providers.name: Kendra Scott
providers.description: Kendra Scott is an American jewelry and accessories retailer founded in 2002 in Austin, Texas, offering personalized jewelry, watches, home goods, and gifts through customization options such as initials, birthstones, and engraving. The brand operates a direct-to-consumer ecommerce storefront alongside a network of retail stores, and pairs its Color Bar customization experience with a philanthropic giving model tied to purchases. Surfaced as a portfolio company of norwest-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network; the company publishes a consumer ecommerce site but no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time. This profile captures its public identity and web-property surface pending any future developer program.

providers.name: KeyMe
providers.description: KeyMe is a nationwide locksmith and key-duplication company that pairs mobile locksmith technicians with a network of self-service key-copying kiosks located inside thousands of retail stores across the United States. Customers can copy residential, commercial, and automotive keys, RFID fobs and access cards at a kiosk, order duplicates online, or request 24/7 mobile locksmith help for home, auto, and business lockouts, transponder and ignition key programming, lock installation, re-keying, and access-control and master-key systems. KeyMe is backed by Battery Ventures. As of this profile the company operates as a consumer-facing locksmith and kiosk service and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this record captures its public web identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: La-Z-Boy
providers.description: La-Z-Boy is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The La-Z-Boy API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Magic Spoon
providers.description: Magic Spoon is a direct-to-consumer breakfast brand selling high-protein, low-sugar cereal, oatmeal, granola, treats, and toaster pastries through its Shopify-powered online store and major retailers including Whole Foods, Target, Costco, Walmart, Kroger, and Sprouts. The company reformulates childhood-classic cereals to be keto-friendly and gluten-free, offering a subscribe-and-save model. Magic Spoon is a consumer packaged goods (CPG) ecommerce company backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners; it operates a retail storefront rather than a public developer platform, and this profile was surfaced as a VC portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Magicpin
providers.description: Magicpin (operated by Samast Technologies Private Limited) is India's hyperlocal savings and discovery platform, connecting consumers with deals, cashback, and vouchers across restaurants, food delivery, fashion, grocery, beauty, fitness, and electronics merchants in cities throughout India. The company operates a consumer savings app alongside a merchant/brands portal and corporate voucher solutions. As of this enrichment pass Magicpin publishes a consumer web and mobile experience plus partner and brand onboarding portals, but exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Outdoor Voices
providers.description: Outdoor Voices is an Austin-founded direct-to-consumer activewear and athletic apparel brand designing clothing for everyday recreation — running, hiking, studio workouts, and rest days — for women and men. The company sells exclusively through its own Shopify-hosted e-commerce storefront and retail presence rather than a public developer platform. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and added to the API Evangelist network. An enrichment pass found no first-party public API, SDK, webhook, or developer surface: the site runs on Shopify commerce infrastructure with only consumer-facing help, privacy, and terms pages.

providers.name: Public Goods
providers.description: Public Goods is a direct-to-consumer e-commerce retailer selling household essentials, personal care, and home products under its own private label, with an emphasis on natural formulations, simplified ingredient lists, minimalist packaging, and sustainable sourcing. The company operates a membership model (an annual fee unlocking member pricing, free shipping, and store credit) and a wholesale channel. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As a consumer retail brand it publishes no developer API, SDK, or technical documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Savage X Fenty
providers.description: Savage X Fenty is a direct-to-consumer lingerie, intimates, sleepwear and loungewear brand co-founded by Rihanna in 2018 and operated as part of TechStyle Fashion Group. It sells through savagex.com and its own iOS and Android shopping apps on a membership model — Savage X Rewards — where members unlock member pricing and store credits, or "skip the month" between the 1st and 5th to avoid the charge. The commerce stack is a custom TechStyle backend fronted by Next.js and Builder.io, behind a Cloudflare edge, with an AWS API Gateway at gateway.savagex.com. Savage X Fenty publishes no public developer program, no API reference, and no machine-readable contract; its first-party API gateway and its engineering docs site are both closed to the public.

providers.name: Scondoo
providers.description: Scondoo is a German consumer cashback and coupon platform, operated by acardo group AG, that lets shoppers earn money back on everyday grocery and drugstore purchases. Users browse exclusive cashback deals in the scondoo iOS and Android apps, buy the qualifying products at any supermarket or drugstore (Kaufland, REWE, EDEKA, Netto, Aldi, Lidl, dm, Rossmann and many more), then snap a photo of the receipt to have the cashback credited to their balance and paid out via bank transfer or PayPal. The service is consumer-facing and mobile-only; it publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or partner integration surface.

providers.name: The Scotts Miracle-Gro Company
providers.description: The Scotts Miracle-Gro Company is the world's largest marketer of branded consumer lawn and garden products, with brands including Scotts, Miracle-Gro, Ortho, Roundup and Tomcat. It is a physical consumer-goods manufacturer and retailer: its digital surface is a Salesforce Commerce Cloud storefront and corporate site at scottsmiraclegro.com, plus end-user mobile apps. It publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable contract. The one developer-facing surface it ever marketed — the open API for the GRO connected smart-watering platform (Gro 7 Zone Controller, Gro Water Sensors) — had its cloud service discontinued on 2021-12-30 and its hosts no longer resolve. The Hawthorne Gardening Company subsidiary was divested to Vireo Growth in April 2026 and is no longer part of this company's surface.

providers.name: Theretailequation
providers.description: The Retail Equation (TRE) is an Irvine, California software and analytics company that helps retailers detect and prevent fraudulent transactions and reduce return/exchange policy abuse. Its core Transaction Authorization service analyzes a shopper's linked purchase, return, and exchange history in real time and returns an approve, warn, or deny recommendation at the point of return — scoring transaction frequency, value, and receipt status while explicitly excluding demographic factors. TRE is part of Appriss Retail. The public web presence is a marketing and consumer-inquiry site plus an authenticated retailer Return Activity Report (RAR) portal; no public developer program, API documentation, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface is published.

providers.name: This Is L.
providers.description: This Is L. (L. Inc.) is a personal-care company making certified-organic cotton menstrual products — tampons, pads, and liners — sold through major U.S. retailers including Target, Walmart, Walgreens, CVS, and Kroger as well as direct-to-consumer at thisisl.com. Founded as a social enterprise and public-benefit corporation with a one-for-one give-back model, L. was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global and is now a Procter & Gamble brand (its legal, privacy, and vulnerability-disclosure surfaces resolve to pg.com). This is a consumer packaged-goods e-commerce business with no public developer API, SDK, or technology platform; enrichment captured its identity, web link-properties, and security posture.

providers.name: Villoid
providers.description: Villoid is a Norwegian online fashion retailer (villoid.no, redirected from villoid.com) operating a Shopify-hosted boutique that curates over 250 designer and contemporary womenswear brands such as Ganni, Isabel Marant, Stella McCartney and ROTATE Birger Christensen. The store sells dresses, shoes, bags, accessories, sportswear and home goods, offering same-day delivery in Norway, easy returns, gift cards and payment via Klarna, Vipps, Visa and Mastercard. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global, Villoid exposes a consumer storefront and publishes no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Crave Retail
providers.description: Crave Retail, Inc. builds in-store retail technology that connects shoppers, store associates, and product data across physical touchpoints. Its platform spans Crave Engage (customer-facing digital shopping assistants in fitting rooms, on the sales floor, and on mobile), Crave Assist (store-associate tools for floor visibility, service routing, and item lookup), and Smart Fitting Rooms, the RFID-based connected fitting-room product it started with. Crave reports 3,000+ live touchpoints, 27M+ shopper sessions, and operations across 10+ countries. The company is Techstars-backed. As of this enrichment pass it publishes a marketing and legal web presence but no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or documentation.

providers.name: Goop
providers.description: Goop is a modern lifestyle and wellness brand founded in 2008 by Gwyneth Paltrow, launched from her kitchen as a weekly email newsletter and grown into a content-and-commerce company spanning editorial journalism, e-commerce, and its own product lines across beauty, skincare, supplements, food, fashion, home, and travel. Goop operates goop.com as a curated online shop and digital magazine, publishes wellness and beauty guidance, and sells goop-branded product lines (including goopglow and goop Beauty) alongside a curated marketplace of third-party brands. It is a privately held company backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners (Series C, 2017) and other investors. Goop does not currently operate a public developer program or API; this profile captures its company identity and public web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Sleep Number
providers.description: Sleep Number Corporation (NASDAQ: SNBR) designs, manufactures, and retails smart adjustable-firmness beds and sleep-wellness products, sold through an omnichannel US retail model. Its Sleep Number 360 smart beds run the proprietary SleepIQ operating system, which captures biometric sleep data each night and returns actionable insights to improve sleep health. Sleep Number does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; the SleepIQ platform is a closed, undocumented backend consumed only by the first-party mobile and web apps. The community has reverse-engineered unofficial SleepIQ client libraries (Python, Go, PHP), but these are not first-party and are not endorsed by Sleep Number. This profile was surfaced as a legacy portfolio lead of Norwest Venture Partners and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: STAND+
providers.description: STAND+ is a Techstars-backed footwear company making biomechanically engineered "energy-recovery" shoes for people who spend long hours standing or walking - healthcare workers, frontline and workforce professionals, athletes, and everyday movers. Its proprietary midsole is designed to dissipate and disperse impact energy outward rather than returning it into the joints, which the company markets for fatigue and pain reduction. The product lineup includes the AntiGrav1, AntiGrav2, and AG3 recovery shoes, the Gales Pro and Gales Frontline workforce and healthcare lines, and standalone recovery insoles. STAND+ is APMA (American Podiatric Medical Association) certified and HSA/FSA eligible through a Truemed partnership. This is a direct-to-consumer e-commerce brand (standshoes.com) with no public developer API, SDK, or integration surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Welly
providers.description: Welly is a health and wellness brand and Certified B Corporation that designs first aid and personal care products, best known for its patterned Flex Fabric adhesive bandages, first aid kits, hydrocolloid blemish and bug-bite patches, and antiseptic wipes. Founded to make caring for everyday cuts, scrapes, and playtime injuries more joyful, Welly sells direct-to-consumer through a Shopify storefront at getwelly.com and via national retail partners. As a consumer packaged-goods company it publishes no public developer API or documentation; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record enriched from its public web presence.

providers.name: Circle K
providers.description: Circle K is a global convenience store and fuel station chain operating more than 14,800 stores worldwide including 9,799 locations in North America and 2,697 in Europe across 48 U.S. states and over 30 countries. A subsidiary of Alimentation Couche-Tard, Circle K operates the Inner Circle Rewards loyalty program, the Easy Pay fuel payment system, an EV charging network, and the Circle K PRO Business Fleet Card.

providers.name: Joko
providers.description: Joko is a French fintech company operating a consumer cashback, rewards, and savings application that connects shoppers with more than 3,500 partner brands online and in physical stores. Users earn cashback and automatically apply promo codes through the Joko iOS and Android apps and browser extensions (Chrome, Firefox, Safari), while also managing budgets, loyalty cards, gift cards, and split (3x installment) payments. Joko also runs a business solution offering brand partnerships and consumer market research. Backed by Partech, Joko is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation at this time.

providers.name: Juleb
providers.description: Juleb is a Saudi Arabia-based pharma-tech and retail software company providing an integrated cloud platform for the health, retail, and distribution sectors. Its suite spans accounting and financial management, inventory and warehouse management, sales force automation (SFA), point of sale (POS), Rx e-prescription, e-commerce, and DSCSA regulatory compliance. Juleb connects to Saudi compliance systems (ZATCA/Fatoora, RSD, GS1, Wasfaty), e-commerce channels (Salla, Shopify, HungerStation), payment providers (Geidea, Alhamrani), and ERPs (Microsoft Dynamics). Founded by Yousuf Jamjoom and backed by 500 Global, Juleb exposes a REST API (documented at docs.juleb.com) covering inventory, point of sale, prescriptions, and partner/company resources.

providers.name: Beautylish
providers.description: Beautylish is a San Francisco based online beauty retailer and community, founded in 2010 by Nils Johnson, Vu Nguyen and Sameer Iyengar. It began as a community where beauty enthusiasts shared tutorials, reviews and product knowledge, and launched its own e-commerce storefront in 2012. Beautylish curates makeup, skincare, hair, fragrance, nails, bath and body, wellness and tool brands from around the world, pairs them with editorial content and makeup-artist guidance, and operates its own fulfillment, rewards (Beautylish Rewards), flexible payments and Zero Day Delivery programs. The company runs a first-party storefront rather than a developer platform: as of this profile it publishes no developer portal, no public API reference, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, and no SDKs. Its public partner surface is a ShareASale/Awin affiliate program rather than an API.

providers.name: Clicktivated
providers.description: Clicktivated is a video technology platform that turns existing video content into interactive, shoppable experiences without re-shooting or re-editing. Its "Activate, Distribute, Optimize" workflow makes any video clickable the same day, deploys it programmatically across DSPs, SSPs, publishers, and direct site embeds, and captures first-party intent signals - item-level and place-level - to improve targeting, measure lift, and drive better performance. The company serves retail brands closing the gap between inspiration and purchase, and tourism brands converting inspiration into itineraries. Founded as Clicktivated Video, Inc. and backed by Techstars, with offices in Detroit, New York, Dubai, and Sydney.

providers.name: Vekia
providers.description: Vekia is a French supply-chain software vendor founded in 2008 in Lille by Manuel Davy (Vekia SAS, 143 rue d'Athènes, 59800 Lille, RCS Lille Métropole 503 225 716). Its platform, Vekia Engine, applies probabilistic artificial intelligence and machine learning to demand and stock forecasting, then generates optimised purchase-order proposals that are pushed back into the customer's existing ERP rather than replacing it, alongside shortage-risk alerting and a logistics control tower. Vekia Disrupt covers disruption and shortage management. The platform is hosted on Microsoft Azure in Europe and marketed to retail and specialised distribution, e-commerce, industry, energy and telecom, with published case studies at ENGIE, Mr Bricolage and Okaïdi. Vekia publishes no public API, no developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable contract; ERP, WMS and TMS integration is delivered as a project by Vekia rather than through a self-serve developer surface.

providers.name: Bailey44
providers.description: Bailey 44 (stylized Bailey/44) is a contemporary womenswear brand selling direct-to-consumer through a Shopify storefront at bailey44.com. The label offers women's apparel — dresses, tops, knits, and separates — around a brand voice of optimism and self-expression ("The Future is Female"). Bailey44 was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. It does not publish a public developer API; its only machine-readable surfaces are the Shopify Customer Account API discovery documents (OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0 authorization-server metadata, issuer shopify.com/authentication/8596750398) served at bailey44.com/.well-known/, a standard Shopify sitemap, and an RSS-backed news blog. This profile is a lead enriched by the pipeline; no first-party API artifacts were found.

providers.name: Beyond Meat
providers.description: Beyond Meat, Inc. is a Los Angeles-based producer of plant-based meat substitutes founded in 2009 and publicly traded on Nasdaq (BYND). The company makes plant-protein versions of beef, pork, and poultry products, including the Beyond Burger, Beyond Sausage, Beyond Beef, and Beyond Chicken, distributed across grocery retail and foodservice channels worldwide. Beyond Meat operates as a consumer packaged-goods brand rather than a technology or developer-platform company; it publishes a marketing and e-commerce website, product and recipe catalogs, a newsroom, and an investor-relations presence, but does not offer a public developer API. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Kleiner Perkins and Obvious Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Bukalapak
providers.description: Bukalapak is one of Indonesia's largest online marketplaces and all-commerce platforms, connecting millions of individual sellers, small warungs (kiosks), and buyers across the archipelago, alongside virtual products, financial services, and online-to-offline retail. Originally added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub (backed by 500 Global), this profile has been enriched from Bukalapak's real public developer surface: a public REST API at api.bukalapak.com secured with OAuth2 via accounts.bukalapak.com, a first-party JavaScript SDK (bukalapak.js), and a large public GitHub organization. No OpenAPI/Swagger specification is currently published by the provider, so the captured artifacts (authentication, packages, domain security) are sourced from first-party repositories and live domain probes rather than derived from a spec.

providers.name: Datasembly
providers.description: Datasembly is a real-time retail intelligence platform that collects hyperlocal pricing, promotion, and assortment data from physical and online retail locations. The company reports gathering 12+ billion weekly prices across 150K+ stores from 230+ retailers, building a dataset of more than 2 trillion observations that consumer packaged goods (CPG) brands and retailers use to optimize pricing strategy, measure trade-spend effectiveness, monitor competitors, evaluate key value items, and plan seasonal launches. Datasembly delivers this competitive intelligence as fully shareable data and analytics rather than a public developer API. The company was acquired by SPINS. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; no public API, developer portal, or API documentation was found on the provider's surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Fabletics
providers.description: Fabletics is an American athleisure and activewear brand co-founded in 2013 by actress Kate Hudson with Adam Goldenberg and Don Ressler under the TechStyle Fashion Group in El Segundo, California. It sells women's and men's (FL2) activewear, leggings, sports bras, accessories, the Yitty shapewear line, and Fabletics Scrubs through a VIP membership subscription model that gives members monthly credits and member pricing, operating omnichannel across its e-commerce site and a growing footprint of brick-and-mortar retail stores. As a direct-to-consumer retailer, Fabletics does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity and public web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: First Club
providers.description: FirstClub is a member-exclusive quick-commerce grocery platform operating in Bengaluru and Hyderabad, India, delivering curated, quality-inspected groceries in as little as 30 minutes from physical "ClubHouses" rather than traditional dark stores. The company targets India's top-tier consumers with only trusted, tasted, and tested products, screening out a published list of banned ingredients across categories including fruits and vegetables, dairy and eggs, bakery, staples, kids nutrition, packaged foods, snacks and beverages, health supplements, and cleaning essentials. FirstClub also offers a subscription model, "FirstClub Mornings." Founded by ex-Flipkart executive Ayyappan R, the company is backed by Accel and RTP Global. It surfaces here as an API Evangelist network profile; FirstClub is a consumer mobile-app business and currently publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation.

providers.name: In Your Shoe
providers.description: In Your Shoe is an Egyptian streetwear and apparel brand, founded in 2018 and based in Cairo, Egypt, that designs and sells playful, statement-driven ready-to-wear pieces — oversized and boxy tees, shirts, jeans, jorts, loungewear, kids' lines, and accessories — letting Millennials and Gen-Z express themselves through high-quality, self-expressive fashion. The company sells direct-to-consumer through a Shopify storefront and is backed by 500 Global and the Misk 500 MENA Accelerator. It publishes no first-party developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures its identity and public web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: InfoScout (acquired by Numerator in 2017)
providers.description: InfoScout (acquired by Numerator in 2017) is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: commerce. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Otrium
providers.description: Otrium is an online designer fashion outlet, headquartered in Amsterdam, that connects shoppers across Europe with end-of-season and overstock apparel, footwear, and accessories from designer and premium brands at reduced prices. A Certified B Corporation, Otrium operates a curated marketplace model with dedicated brand storefronts, native iOS and Android apps, and multi-market localization across the Netherlands, Germany, Belgium, France, Italy, the United Kingdom, Spain, Poland, and the rest of Europe. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bond Capital and Index Ventures. No public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface is currently published; this profile captures the company identity and its verified public web properties.

providers.name: Port of Mokha
providers.description: Port of Mokha is a specialty coffee company founded by Mokhtar Alkhanshali that sources rare, high-scoring single-origin coffee from Yemen and brings it to the international specialty market. Known for record-setting Coffee Review scores and curated offerings such as the Timeless Mokha Blend and The Yemen Trilogy, it also runs a wholesale program and publishes brewing guides. The business operates as a direct-to-consumer Shopify storefront; it exposes no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched as a retail (non-API) company record.

providers.name: RS Legacy
providers.description: RS Legacy Corporation is the post-bankruptcy successor entity of RadioShack Corporation, the iconic American consumer electronics retailer founded in 1921. RadioShack filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2015, with RS Legacy Corp assuming the remaining obligations. The RadioShack brand was subsequently acquired by Unicomer Group (El Salvador-based) in 2023, which now operates the brand globally in approximately 70 countries including the United States, Canada, Europe, and Latin America. RadioShack continues to sell consumer electronics, components, batteries, cables, and accessories online at radioshack.com and through franchise locations. No public developer API is currently documented.

providers.name: Bloom & Wild
providers.description: Bloom & Wild is a British direct-to-consumer online florist and gifting brand founded in 2013 by Aron Gelbard and Ben Stanway, best known for pioneering letterbox flowers — bouquets packed flat so they fit through a UK letterbox — alongside hand-tied bouquets, plants, gift sets, gift cards and recurring flower subscriptions. Bloom & Wild Group trades as Bloom & Wild in the United Kingdom, Ireland, Germany and Austria, and operates the sister brands bloomon (Netherlands, Belgium, Denmark) and Bergamotte (France) on separate storefronts. The group is a certified B Corp and runs its own commerce platform — a Ruby on Rails backend fronted by Kong, an Angular multi-brand web app and native iOS and Android clients, on AWS and GCP. Bloom & Wild publishes NO public developer portal, no API documentation, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable API description, and no partner or corporate-gifting API: business and bulk gifting is transacted through a contact form, an account manager and invoicing, not through a programmatic surface. The application backends at api.bloomandwild.com and capi.bloomandwild.com are live but private to the brand's own clients and undocumented. What the group does publish for machines is narrow but real: an llms.txt on the UK and German storefronts that routes assistants to the correct market by delivery destination and even ships an optional agent widget specification, and an RFC 9116 security.txt served across every group storefront.

providers.name: KWI
providers.description: KWI is a retail technology company founded in 1985 and headquartered in Melville, New York, that delivers a cloud-based, unified commerce platform for specialty and department retailers. The platform combines an iOS mobile point-of-sale, merchandising and inventory optimization, order management with buy-anywhere / fulfill-from-anywhere fulfillment, CRM, clienteling and loyalty, the Snapshot real-time sales analytics application, and AI product image search, all operated as a SaaS managed service with helpdesk, hardware, and payments support. KWI describes an API layer in its platform architecture used to export data to third-party systems and channels --- CRMs, ERPs, SRPs, and supply chains --- alongside packaged connectors such as Shopify Connect and a Klaviyo connector. As of this profile KWI publishes no public developer portal, API reference, machine-readable specification, or SDKs; integration is delivered through its professional-services organization under customer contract.

providers.name: Photobox
providers.description: Photobox is Europe's leading e-commerce retailer of personalised photo products and gifts, serving tens of millions of customers across the UK and continental Europe. Its consumer web and mobile apps let people upload photos and create photo books, wall art, canvas prints, calendars, cards, mugs and other personalised gifts for home delivery. Backed by Insight Partners. As of this enrichment pass Photobox publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDKs, or partner API surface; its verified GitHub organization contains only two forked operations utilities. This profile therefore captures company identity and public web properties rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Ralph Lauren
providers.description: Ralph Lauren is a global leader in the design, marketing, and distribution of premium lifestyle products across apparel, footwear, accessories, home, fragrances, and hospitality. The company operates ralphlauren.com, Polo Ralph Lauren, Lauren, Club Monaco, and other brands. No public developer API has been verified; the company participates in affiliate programs via Rakuten and Sovrn Commerce, and uses Microsoft Azure OpenAI for the Ask Ralph AI shopping assistant launched in 2025.

providers.name: Sunoco LP
providers.description: Sunoco LP (NYSE: SUN) is a master limited partnership and the premier independent fuel distributor in the United States, distributing over 15 billion gallons of fuel annually to approximately 11,000 Sunoco and partner-branded retail locations and operating more than 160 terminals. Sunoco LP is affiliated with Energy Transfer (parent of Sunoco GP, the general partner). On November 3, 2025 Sunoco closed its $9.1 billion acquisition of Parkland Corporation (announced May 5, 2025), creating SunocoCorp LLC, which began trading on the NYSE under ticker "SUNC". The Parkland acquisition substantially expands Sunoco's footprint into Canada and additional international markets, adding Parkland's refining, retail, and commercial fuels businesses to Sunoco's North American distribution network.

providers.name: LYST
providers.description: Lyst is a global fashion aggregation and shopping platform that consolidates products from more than 27,000 brands and retailers, connecting roughly 160 million annual shoppers with clothing, shoes, bags, accessories and jewelry across a single personalized, AI-driven catalog. Rather than a public developer API, Lyst exposes a partner surface: brands and retailers integrate via product-feed synchronization and a Stripe-powered "Lyst Shop" checkout, with API access granted privately during a two-week partner onboarding. Backed by Accel and Balderton Capital, Lyst also runs an engineering organization (making.lyst.com, github.com/lyst) best known for the open-source LightFM recommendation library.

providers.name: PlantShop.me
providers.description: PlantShop.me (operated by Lamento Trading LLC, Dubai) is the largest online plant store in the Middle East, selling indoor and outdoor plants, pots and planters, seeds, terrariums, fertilizers and plant-care accessories with UAE-wide delivery and localized shipping to Saudi Arabia, Bahrain and Kuwait. It offers cash on delivery, same-week delivery, and free plant-care support from a real team. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. The company publishes no public developer API; its machine-readable surface is a first-party /llms.txt AI overview, an AI-crawler-friendly robots.txt, and schema.org structured data on product pages.

providers.name: ARIVE
providers.description: ARIVE (getarive.com) was an urban quick-commerce platform founded in Paris during the COVID-19 pandemic that delivered fashion, beauty, and lifestyle products to customers within hours. Operating across Berlin, Munich, Hamburg, Düsseldorf, Frankfurt, and Paris, it connected more than 500 brands and 200 local stores directly to young, convenience-focused urban shoppers. Backed by Balderton Capital, LaFamiglia, and Triple Point Capital with roughly €31.7M raised, the company ceased operations in mid-2023 following a sale of the business. No public API, developer portal, SDK, or other technical surface was ever published; this profile is retained for network and portfolio-graph completeness.

providers.name: Casey's General Stores
providers.description: Casey's General Stores is one of the largest convenience store chains in the United States, operating more than 2,900 stores selling fuel, made-from-scratch pizza, prepared food, and other convenience items primarily in small midwestern communities. Casey's is a publicly traded Fortune 500 company (NASDAQ: CASY) and offers a mobile app for pizza ordering, delivery, and its Casey's Rewards loyalty program. No public developer APIs have been documented; partner and supplier integrations are managed privately.

providers.name: Detoure Inc
providers.description: Detoure Inc (DETOURE) is a sustainable fashion resale marketplace, backed by 500 Global, that sources highly curated clothing from influencers and tastemakers and offers it to shoppers at thrift prices. The platform lets customers buy current trends from the creators they follow while cutting down on excess fashion waste, and lets influencers and partners apply to consign and sell items from their own closets. Detoure operates as a consumer e-commerce brand on a hosted Shopify storefront and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Dishpatch
providers.description: Dishpatch is a UK-based meal delivery service that partners with renowned chefs and restaurants to deliver restaurant-quality, finish-at-home meals nationwide. Operated by Dishpatch Ltd (part of the Waitrose family), the service curates seasonal menus from chefs such as Michel Roux, Rick Stein, Sabrina Ghayour, Jose Pizarro and Paul Ainsworth. Orders are placed a la carte rather than by subscription, delivered on Fridays in insulated, recyclable packaging via DPD, and arrive pre-prepared for simple finishing steps at home. A paid "Supper Club" membership adds free shipping, exclusive menus, early sale access and spending credits. Dishpatch operates a consumer e-commerce storefront and does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation surface.

providers.name: jokr
providers.description: JOKR is an instant grocery and convenience delivery company headquartered in Luxembourg (JOKR S.a.r.L) that operates an online supermarket delivering fresh products and local brands to consumers within minutes or on a scheduled window through its mobile app. The service offers more than 10,000 products with AI-powered personalized recommendations and competitive supermarket pricing, and reports roughly 3 million app downloads and 5 million users. In Brazil it operates under the DAKI brand (soudaki.com), the leading online supermarket in cities including Sao Paulo and Belo Horizonte. JOKR is a consumer-facing quick-commerce business with no public developer API surface; this profile captures its identity and domain posture in the API Evangelist network. Backed by Balderton Capital, GGV Capital, and HV Capital.

providers.name: Newme
providers.description: Newme (newme.asia) is an Accel-backed fast-fashion women's apparel and accessories e-commerce brand operating under the tagline "Freshest Fashion Fastest." It sells trend-driven contemporary womenswear — denim, bottoms, tops, t-shirts, dresses, co-ords, jumpsuits, bodysuits and winterwear — through its website and iOS/Android shopping apps, backed by a growing footprint of physical retail stores across India and Asia. Newme is a consumer direct-to-consumer retailer and, as of this profile, publishes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: Showroomprive.com
providers.description: Showroomprive.com is a French online private-sales (flash-sales) e-commerce platform operated by Showroomprive.com SAS, a subsidiary of SRP Groupe SA, based in La Plaine Saint-Denis. It sells discounted apparel, beauty, home, sports, and travel products from major brands, and also runs a third-party seller marketplace. The company exposes a private marketplace / seller API reached through partner onboarding and surfaced by third-party integration platforms such as ChannelEngine and Commercium, but it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or OpenAPI. Added to the API Evangelist network as an Accel portfolio lead.

providers.name: Agryco
providers.description: Agryco — trading as Agriconomie until its September 2024 rebrand — is a French online marketplace and e-commerce platform that sells agricultural supplies direct to farmers: mineral, organic and foliar fertilizers, conventional and organic seeds, phytosanitary products, animal nutrition and livestock equipment, plus tractor, spraying, harvesting and soil-working spare parts. Founded in 2014 by Clement Le Fournis, Dinh Nguyen and Paolin Pascot, the company operates a one-stop procurement site for professional farmers across France, Belgium, Germany, Spain and Italy, wrapping the catalog in advisory services (agronomy experts on the phone six days a week), fertilizer blending, equipment valuation and 60-day payment terms. It raised a EUR 60 million Series B in 2022 co-led by Treis Group, Temasek and Aliment Capital with Eurazeo participating, and publishes the Agrycomag technical magazine at agryco.com/blog. Agryco is an end-user commerce product: as of this profile it publishes no public developer program, API reference, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Kontoor Brands
providers.description: Kontoor Brands, Inc. is a global lifestyle apparel company with a portfolio of iconic denim and casual apparel brands including Wrangler, Lee, and Rock & Republic. Headquartered in Greensboro, North Carolina, the company designs, manufactures, sources, markets, and distributes its apparel products worldwide through wholesale, retail, and direct-to-consumer channels. Kontoor Brands does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation portal.

providers.name: LocateAI
providers.description: LocateAI (Locate) is an AI-integrated commercial real estate brokerage focused on retail site selection for multi-unit and franchise brands. Its platform pairs proprietary AI models with full-service advisory to help brands choose markets, source and score sites, forecast Year-1 revenue and cannibalization risk, right-size franchise territories, and negotiate leases — from the first market through the signed lease. The models analyze 200M+ mobile devices and 1,100+ variables for device-level trade-area, fair-share, and time-weighted revenue analysis. Locate is delivered as a managed service; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company.

providers.name: Mitchell & Ness
providers.description: Vintage and throwback sports apparel brand founded in Philadelphia in 1904. Holds league-licensed agreements with the NBA, NFL, MLB, NHL, and MLS to produce authentic reproduction jerseys, snapback hats, varsity jackets, hoodies, and shorts. Acquired in February 2022 by Fanatics, Inc. alongside investors Jay-Z (Marcy Venture Partners), LeBron James / Maverick Carter (SpringHill Co), and Kevin Hart.

providers.name: Bold Metrics
providers.description: Bold Metrics is an AI body data platform for the apparel and fashion industry that uses digital-twin technology to power apparel fit and sizing. From just 4-6 simple body-data inputs it predicts 50+ individual body measurements with tailor-level accuracy, without photos, scanning, or measuring tapes. Its products - Smart Size Chart, Virtual Sizer, Virtual Tailor, Apparel Insights, and the Agentic Sizing Protocol - help brands reduce returns, lift conversion, and increase average order value with personalized size recommendations. The Agentic Sizing Protocol exposes this capability to AI shopping agents while keeping retailer API credentials off the agent and out of any LLM. Bold Metrics has processed 250M+ digital twins and 12B+ body-data points. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and Techstars. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Bold Metrics publishes no public API documentation - integration is gated behind a demo/partner engagement.

providers.name: Lizee
providers.description: Lizee is a Paris-based Retail-as-a-Service platform that helps brands and retailers launch and operate circular commerce programs — rental, resale, and second-hand — end to end. Its stack pairs a rental platform, a resale/e-commerce platform, and a logistics platform (returns, refurbishment, reverse logistics) behind an operations API so a brand can offer rent or buy-back experiences on top of its existing catalog. Lizee runs a production API (api.lizee.io) and publishes a public Atlassian Statuspage, though it does not expose a public developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or SDKs — the API surface is partner and integration facing. Lizee was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Speedinvest.

providers.name: Novi Connect
providers.description: Novi Connect (Novi) is an AI shopping optimization platform and data infrastructure for CPG and retail brands. It connects brands, certification bodies, and major retailers to verify, standardize, and distribute product data so products are accurately understood, ranked, and recommended by AI shopping systems and agentic search. Products include the AI Shopping Optimizer for SKU-level product-feed optimization and the Product Authority Builder for verified direct data distribution across retailers and marketplaces. Backed by Felicis. No public developer API surface is currently published; product docs are hosted on Notion and customer access is via login apps.

providers.name: Ulta Beauty
providers.description: Ulta Beauty is the largest beauty retailer in the United States, offering cosmetics, fragrance, skin care products, hair care products, and salon services through retail stores and online. The company operates over 1,400 stores across all 50 states and an e-commerce platform. Ulta Beauty does not currently offer a public developer API, but provides an affiliate program through Impact for publishers and content creators.

providers.name: Whole Foods Market
providers.description: Whole Foods Market is an American multinational supermarket chain owned by Amazon, exclusively selling products free from hydrogenated fats and artificial colors, flavors, and preservatives. Acquired by Amazon in 2017, Whole Foods integrates with Amazon Prime for delivery, pickup, and member discounts. Supplier integrations are handled through EDI (Electronic Data Interchange) and the Whole Foods Supplier Portal.

providers.name: Dollar Tree
providers.description: Dollar Tree is a leading operator of discount variety stores in North America, operating more than 16,000 stores under the Dollar Tree and Family Dollar banners. Vendor and supplier integration is primarily handled through EDI, SAP, and ERP systems via the Dollar Tree Vendor Portal. No public REST API is currently available.

providers.name: United Refining Company
providers.description: United Refining Company is an independent, integrated petroleum company headquartered in Warren, Pennsylvania. The company owns and operates a petroleum refinery and a network of retail gasoline stations and convenience stores under the Kwik Fill and Country Fair brands in the northeastern United States. United Refining does not offer publicly documented APIs or developer resources.

providers.name: Razor Group
providers.description: Razor Group (Whele LLC) is a Berlin- and Boston-headquartered consumer goods holding company that acquires, consolidates and scales profitable e-commerce brands selling on Amazon FBA, Walmart, Target, Chewy and other online marketplaces. Founded in 2020, the company has raised over $1 billion, employs 450+ people across five offices in Europe, North America and Asia, and operates more than 40,000 SKUs across brands including GymKeg, POWRX, Tranquil Spa and Porto Vino. In August 2025 Razor merged with Infinite Commerce to form the largest consolidator in the FBA aggregator space, operating a unified internal technology platform for demand forecasting, pricing and advertising. Razor Group is a buyer and operator of physical consumer products, not a software vendor: it publishes no public API, SDK, webhook surface or developer portal.

providers.name: Stylight
providers.description: Stylight is an online fashion and home-decor shopping aggregator that curates and compares products from more than 100 retailers, letting shoppers browse women's and men's apparel, footwear, accessories, beauty and home furnishings across many brands in one place and then complete the purchase on the partner retailer's own store. The platform operates localized sites across the US, UK, Germany, Austria, Switzerland, France, Italy, Spain, Belgium, the Netherlands and Canada, runs an editorial style magazine, and monetizes through affiliate partnerships with the retailers it links to. HV Capital was an early backer. Stylight publishes no public developer API; this profile captures its public web, legal and security surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Ulta Salon, Cosmetics & Fragrance
providers.description: Ulta Salon, Cosmetics & Fragrance (now operating as Ulta Beauty) is the largest beauty retailer in the United States, offering cosmetics, fragrance, skin care products, hair care products, and salon services through retail stores and online. This entry tracks the legacy brand identity prior to the Ulta Beauty rebranding. No public developer API is currently available.

providers.name: Una Brands
providers.description: Una Brands is a Singapore-headquartered, digital-age e-commerce house of brands that acquires and operates consumer e-commerce businesses across the APAC region, accelerating their growth with operational expertise and AI-led innovation from teams in Singapore, China, and Indonesia. The company publishes no public developer API, but its website ships an llms.txt and a live Wix Site MCP endpoint that lets AI agents retrieve business details, search products and services, book appointments, and start purchases.

providers.name: Pool
providers.description: Pool.com is a Web3 domain service provider offering Infinity Domains, enabling ICANN-accredited registrars and other partners to mint and distribute Second Level Domains and integrate Web3 naming into their services through Pool's registrar API.

providers.name: VideoPoint
providers.description: VideoPoint is a Shopify app from TouchPoints Inc. (a 500 Global portfolio company) that turns a merchant's existing product photos and videos into shoppable, on-site experiences on product-detail and collection pages, with the company reporting an 11-35% conversion uplift and 60-120x ROI from existing content. It is part of the broader TouchPoints suite of AI-powered Shopify apps (alongside TryPoint virtual try-on, plus A/B testing and AI-powered chat) built to engage shoppers, boost conversions, and drive more sales. VideoPoint ships as an embedded Shopify app installed from the Shopify App Store; it exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface at this time. Added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile and enrichment lead.

providers.name: Aiperia
providers.description: Aiperia (formerly PlanerAI) is a German AI company whose SaaS platform automates demand forecasting and fresh-food supply-chain planning from production through to the end consumer. Its machine-learning models predict fresh-food demand up to 21 days ahead using around 150 external factors, then generate automated order and production suggestions for bakeries and self-service stations, food manufacturers, and supermarkets to reduce food waste and overproduction. Aiperia is a portfolio company of Earlybird Venture Capital.

providers.name: Clockster
providers.description: Clockster is a frontline staff-management super-app for food & beverage and retail businesses, consolidating attendance and time tracking, shift scheduling, automated payroll, earned wage access, business communication, tasks and checklists into a single mobile-first platform. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Singapore with offices across Kazakhstan and Indonesia, Clockster serves more than 1,300 SMEs across Central and Southeast Asia — including brands such as KFC, Hardee's and Costa Coffee — and is backed by 500 Global, I2BF Global Ventures and Quest Ventures. It is delivered as iOS, Android and Huawei mobile apps plus a web console and currently exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Cracker Barrel Old Country Store
providers.description: Cracker Barrel Old Country Store, Inc. is an American chain of restaurants and gift shops with a Southern country theme, offering home-style meals and retail merchandise. Founded in 1969 and headquartered in Lebanon, Tennessee, Cracker Barrel operates roughly 656 restaurant and retail locations across 44 U.S. states. No public API or developer portal is published; the company offers a consumer website, iOS and Android mobile ordering apps, To-Go and catering ordering, gift cards, and the Cracker Barrel Rewards loyalty program for guests.

providers.name: DailyDeal.de
providers.description: DailyDeal.de is a German consumer deals, coupons, and discounts platform ("Deals, Gutscheine & Schnäppchen") that aggregates daily deals across categories including electronics, fashion, home and garden, beauty, kids, sports, and free-to-try product samples ("gratis testen"). Shoppers browse discounted products, brand vouchers, and shop-specific coupon codes, and read shopping guides in the site's Magazin. Originally founded in Berlin in 2009 and briefly owned by Google, DailyDeal today operates as a WordPress-based consumer commerce and content site and publishes no public developer API program. It was added to the API Evangelist network as an Insight Partners portfolio lead.

providers.name: Every.tv
providers.description: Every, Inc. (株式会社エブリー, corp.every.tv) is a Tokyo-based Japanese video-media and advertising company that runs consumer lifestyle products including DELISH KITCHEN (recipe video media), retailHUB (a retail promotion and data platform connecting physical stores with digital channels), トモニテ / Tomonite (parenting video media and community), and MOMENTH (a professional video production and social team). Led by CEO Taissei Yoshida and headquartered in Roppongi, Minato, Tokyo, the company approached an IPO on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Growth Market. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Every, Inc. publishes an engineering blog and owned media but exposes no public developer API program.

providers.name: Iwarranty
providers.description: iWarranty is a London-based, AI and machine-learning powered warranty management software platform that digitizes the entire warranty lifecycle for manufacturers, retailers, warrantors, and consumers. The platform covers QR-code product registration, automated claims processing and verification, repair and replacement coordination, fraud detection, and real-time product performance analytics, and integrates with existing ERP and CRM systems such as SAP, Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics, Oracle, and NetSuite. iWarranty emphasizes sustainability by reducing paper waste and e-waste through digitized processes. The company is backed by Anthemis and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile is maintained as an API Evangelist network enrichment lead.

providers.name: Maman
providers.description: Maman is a French-inspired bakery and cafe chain founded in New York City, with locations across the United States and Canada. Maman serves seasonal pastries, coffee, salads, sandwiches and its signature nutty chocolate chip cookie in design-forward spaces, and operates online ordering for pickup and delivery, a nationwide cookie and gift shop, full-service event and corporate catering, private event venues, a loyalty mobile app, and a published cookbook. This API Evangelist profile tracks Maman's public web and commerce properties; the company exposes no first-party developer API surface.

providers.name: merama
providers.description: Merama is a Latin American e-commerce company that invests in and scales established online brands selling on marketplaces such as Amazon and MercadoLibre. It acquires a substantial stake while founders retain operational control, then provides working capital, business intelligence, digital marketing, cross-border expansion across Latin America and the US, and proprietary operating technology to accelerate growth. Merama operates as a brand aggregator / roll-up rather than a developer platform and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Rebag
providers.description: Rebag is an online marketplace for buying, selling, and trading pre-owned luxury goods — designer handbags, watches, fine jewelry, shoes, apparel, and accessories from houses such as Chanel, Hermes, Louis Vuitton, Prada, Goyard, and Gucci. Founded in 2014 and headquartered in New York City, Rebag authenticates every item in-house and is known for Clair (Comprehensive Luxury Appraisal Index for Resale), an AI-driven pricing engine that gives sellers instant, guaranteed buyback quotes. Rebag operates a mobile app, physical retail stores, and consignment/trade-in programs, and is backed by investors including General Catalyst. This profile tracks Rebag's public web presence; no public developer API has been identified.

providers.name: Saxbys Coffee
providers.description: Saxbys is a Philadelphia-headquartered hospitality company founded in 2005 by Nick Bayer that operates a small chain of cafes across the U.S. East Coast and Midwest. The brand is unique for its "Experiential Learning Platform" (E.L.P.) — 100% student-run cafes embedded inside college and university campuses. Each E.L.P. cafe is operated by a Student Cafe Executive Officer (SCEO) who takes full responsibility for running the location while earning paid, experiential learning credit. Saxbys describes itself as "a national education company and For Students, By Students" with a mission to "Make Life Better." Saxbys does not publish a public REST API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, developer portal, or partner integration program. The only public digital surfaces are the marketing website (saxbyscoffee.com), location-specific online ordering powered by BentoBox, a "Saxbys Stories" blog, and a mobile ordering / rewards app. The Saxbys GitHub organization exists but currently holds a single internal inventory-analyzer repository. This apis.yml records the company as a non-API hospitality + education brand for the API Evangelist network catalog.

providers.name: Treet
providers.description: Treet is a branded recommerce (resale) platform that lets e-commerce brands run their own secondhand marketplaces. Founded in 2021 by marketplace veterans Jake Disraeli and Sonia Yang (formerly of Indiegogo and Airbnb), Treet powers resale for 250+ global brands through four stackable programs: Peer-to-Peer (customers buy and sell from each other for cash or brand credit), Trade-In, Off-Price liquidation of excess inventory, and Returns rerouting. Treet integrates into a brand's existing commerce stack — Shopify, Adobe Commerce, BigCommerce, WooCommerce and Salesforce Commerce, plus logistics (ShipHero, ShipBob), marketing/loyalty (Klaviyo, Yotpo, LoyaltyLion) and returns (Loop, Happy Returns) partners via its "Infinite Integrations" platform. Treet is an API consumer rather than an API producer: it publishes no public developer API, API documentation, developer portal, SDKs or webhooks of its own, and delivers to brands as a managed SaaS and Shopify app. Backed by Two Sigma Ventures and Techstars.

providers.name: TokyoOtakuMode
providers.description: Tokyo Otaku Mode (TOM) is a Japan-based e-commerce company and online destination for fans of Japanese pop culture, selling official anime figures, manga merchandise, apparel, and collectibles worldwide through its otakumode.com shop. Grown out of a large social-media following, TOM curates and ships Japanese otaku goods internationally. It runs a private, API-key-gated backend (api.otakumode.com) that powers its storefront, but publishes no public developer program, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specifications, or first-party client SDKs. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched from live public probes.

providers.name: Alkemics
providers.description: Alkemics was a French SaaS company founded in 2011 in Paris that operated a collaborative commerce platform connecting consumer packaged goods (CPG) brands and retailers to share, enrich, and distribute product content and data across the FMCG/grocery supply chain. Backed by investors including Partech, Cathay Innovation, and Serena, Alkemics was acquired by Salsify (a US product experience management company) in October 2020. The product now lives on as "SupplierXM by Salsify"; alkemics.com and docs.alkemics.com redirect to Salsify, and the successor developer documentation is hosted at docs.supplierxm.salsify.com. This company profile is preserved in the API Evangelist network with an honest acquisition/successor record. No independent Alkemics-owned API surface remains.

providers.name: CQuotient
providers.description: CQuotient is the artificial intelligence and shopper-data technology that powers personalization and predictive commerce for Salesforce B2C Commerce (Commerce Cloud) Einstein. Originally an independent commerce-personalization startup, CQuotient was acquired by Demandware in 2013, and Demandware was in turn acquired by Salesforce in 2016. Today the CQuotient engine underpins Einstein product recommendations, predictive sort, Einstein search dictionaries, and shopper activity capture. Its developer surface is the Salesforce B2C Commerce Einstein API (also referred to as the CQuotient API), documented within the Salesforce Developers documentation rather than on a standalone CQuotient portal.

providers.name: Levit
providers.description: Levit Inc. (레브잇) is a software company headquartered in Seoul, South Korea, best known for Alwayz (올웨이즈) — a mobile-first team-purchase commerce app launched in July 2021 that lets shoppers group together with other buyers to unlock prices below normal retail. Levit describes itself as building "a service that everybody uses everyday," and previously launched Ping in March 2021. The company runs the Alwayz Seller Center for merchants selling on the platform and publishes a seller-focused commerce blog. As of this profile Levit publishes no public developer API program, no API documentation or reference, no developer portal, and no SDKs — the enrichment pipeline probed the company and product domains and found no developer surface.

providers.name: Tamara Mellon
providers.description: Tamara Mellon Brand, Inc. is a Los Angeles based direct-to-consumer luxury footwear company founded in 2016 by designer Tamara Mellon, co-founder of Jimmy Choo, together with chief executive Jill Layfield. The brand sells Italian-made women's shoes and accessories straight to customers online rather than through wholesale, releasing product in monthly drops instead of following the traditional fashion calendar, and it is reported to have raised roughly $87 million in venture funding after the earlier Tamara Mellon LLC filed for Chapter 11 in 2015. In August 2025 the company announced a licensing and operating partnership with footwear licensing firm Titan Industries. It is a consumer goods retailer rather than a software company: it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification of any kind. As probed on 2026-08-29 its canonical domain returns HTTP 404 on every path from an unprovisioned CDN origin, and its Shopify storefront at shop.tamaramellon.com redirects to a store password gate.

providers.name: Carter's
providers.description: Carter's, Inc. is the largest branded marketer of young children's apparel in the United States, operating the Carter's, OshKosh B'gosh, and Skip Hop brands. Its customer-facing digital surface includes carters.com and carters.com/cart e-commerce, mobile apps, a rewards program, and vendor / supply-chain integrations, but no public developer API or partner program is currently published.

providers.name: Dewu (POIZON)
providers.description: Dewu (POIZON) is a leading Chinese online marketplace for sneakers, streetwear, luxury goods, and collectibles, distinguished by its integrated product authentication (legit-check) service that verifies items before they ship to buyers. Operated by Shanghai-based Poizon and backed by Hongshan (formerly Sequoia China), it runs both the domestic Dewu (得物) app and the global POIZON marketplace. For developers it operates the POIZON / Dewu Open Platform (open.poizon.com and open.dewu.com), a partner program that lets sellers, ISVs, and ERP integrators connect to the marketplace over an app-key plus request-signature authenticated API covering product data, pricing, catalog search, delivery modes, and vendor information.

providers.name: Konga
providers.description: Konga is a Lagos, Nigeria-based e-commerce company founded in July 2012 and now operating as Nigeria's leading online shopping marketplace, combining a first-party retail business with a third-party seller marketplace across consumer electronics, mobile phones, home appliances, fashion, groceries, beauty, and lifestyle categories. Konga runs a vertically integrated stack alongside its storefront: KongaPay, a Central Bank of Nigeria-licensed and NDIC-insured payments platform offering checkout, transfers, virtual accounts, multi-currency wallets, POS, bill payments, savings, and merchant payouts; Konga Travel & Tours, an IATA-certified travel agency providing flight bookings, hotels, and vacation packages; Konga Health (Medical Direct); Konga Foods/Groceries; KongaNow same-day delivery; and KXpress Logistics for nationwide fulfillment. Konga's revenue model spans marketplace commissions, first-party retail margin, KongaPay transaction fees, logistics fees, travel agency commissions, and seller advertising. Konga does not operate a unified public developer program: the marketplace exposes no documented public REST API for orders, products, or sellers; KongaPay published Android, iOS, and WooCommerce SDKs and SDK docs at kongapay.github.io, but that GitHub organization was archived on July 1, 2023, and the current KPay aggregator API documentation lives at kpayment-org.gitbook.io with limited public surface area focused on POS, Web Payment Gateway, Virtual Account, and Payment Link integrations for approved merchants. As a result, Konga is profiled here as a provider index rather than as an actively documented public-API company.

providers.name: MisterSpex
providers.description: Mister Spex SE is a European online-first eyewear and optical retailer selling prescription glasses, sunglasses, and contact lenses across more than 100 premium, luxury, independent, and private-label brands. Founded in Berlin in 2007 and listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, the company serves more than 8 million customers online in five countries and operates 65 stores in Germany plus a network of over 300 partner opticians. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Point Nine and added to the API Evangelist network; the company publishes no public consumer or developer API, so this profile captures corporate identity and security-surface artifacts derived from live probes rather than an API catalog.

providers.name: Huckberry
providers.description: Huckberry is an American direct-to-consumer online retailer of men's apparel, outdoor gear and lifestyle goods, founded in 2010 by Andy Forch and Richard Greiner and headquartered in San Francisco with offices in Austin and Columbus. It pairs a first-party e-commerce storefront with a large editorial operation — the Huckberry Journal — and an in-house brand portfolio, selling an "everyday adventure" assortment that sits between traditional outdoor retail and menswear. Huckberry is a retailer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, no public API, no SDK and no machine-readable contract. Its public GitHub organization (Huckberry Inc) holds eight repositories, seven of them forks of third-party Ruby e-commerce gems — Solidus AvaTax, Affirm, Paperclip, omniauth-slack — which evidence a self-hosted Ruby storefront rather than a published platform. Partner and affiliate integration is outsourced to the Partnerize network, and customer self-service runs on a Zendesk help center tenant at help.huckberry.com.

providers.name: Pet Circle
providers.description: Pet Circle is Australia's largest online pet-supplies retailer, selling pet food, flea and worming treatments, toys, bedding and prescription veterinary products direct to consumers across Australia. Founded in mid-2011 in Sydney by Mike Frizell and James Edwards as Paws for Life and rebranded to Pet Circle in early 2014, the company reached unicorn status with a valuation above AU$1 billion after a $125 million Series C in December 2021, and extended into adjacent lines with Pet Circle Pharmacy (petcirclepharma.com.au) and Pet Circle Insurance (petcircleinsurance.com.au, launched May 2023). Its storefront is a headless commerce stack — a commercetools back end fronted by a Vue Storefront / Alokai layer on Vercel, with Google Cloud Functions gluing SaaS services together — but Pet Circle operates that architecture internally: it publishes no public developer portal, no API reference, and no machine-readable API contract. Trading-partner integration is handled out of band through EDI, and consumer-side partner traffic runs through third-party affiliate networks rather than a first-party API program.

providers.name: Bloomingdale's
providers.description: Bloomingdale's is an American luxury department store chain and a subsidiary of Macy's, Inc. Bloomingdale's does not publish a public developer portal; partner integration is delivered through the parent Macy's Inc. vendor and trade partner programs, drop-ship and EDI channels with suppliers, the Bloomingdale's affiliate program for marketing partners, and the shared Macy's Inc. technology platform powering Bloomingdale's commerce, loyalty, and fulfillment.

providers.name: CrossAmerica Partners
providers.description: CrossAmerica Partners is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The CrossAmerica Partners API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Green Thumb Industries
providers.description: A leading U.S. cannabis consumer packaged goods company operating a nationwide portfolio of retail dispensaries under the RISE brand and a collection of cannabis brands. Operates manufacturing facilities and retail locations across multiple states.

providers.name: Hallmark Cards
providers.description: Hallmark Cards is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Hallmark Cards API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: ShelterLogic Group
providers.description: ShelterLogic Group is the world leader in shade, shelter, storage, and outdoor lifestyle products with over 70 years of industry experience. Launched in 1991, ShelterLogic develops tough, affordable shelter solutions for everyday consumers and commercial customers. The company operates three manufacturing facilities in the US and China and maintains worldwide distribution. The ShelterLogic brand portfolio includes ShelterLogic, SOJAG, Arrow Storage Products, Quik Shade, CAMP&GO, RIO Beach, and licensed brands including Tommy Bahama, Margaritaville, Life is Good, and Scotts Miracle-Gro. As a B2C manufacturer and retailer, ShelterLogic does not expose a public developer API.

providers.name: ApnaMart
providers.description: ApnaMart (Apna Mart) is a Bengaluru-based Indian retail and quick-commerce company founded in 2022 by Chetan Kumar Garg and Abhishek Singh. It operates a network of franchise-model neighborhood grocery and FMCG stores combined with a 15-minute delivery app, serving customers across roughly 14 cities including tier-2 and tier-3 markets such as Ranchi, Hazaribagh, and Bilaspur. Backed by Accel, Peak XV, and Fundamentum, the company blends brick-and-mortar retail with on-demand delivery of daily essentials. ApnaMart is a consumer retail business and does not publish a public developer platform or API surface; this profile in the API Evangelist network captures its identity, domain-security posture, and published web properties.

providers.name: Breadfast
providers.description: Breadfast is an Egyptian quick-commerce and online grocery platform, founded in 2017 in Cairo by Mostafa Amin, Muhammad Habib, and Abdallah Nofal. It delivers groceries, freshly baked bread, dairy, fresh produce, ready-to-eat meals, household essentials, pharmacy, and beauty products — more than 7,000 SKUs — to customers in roughly 60 minutes through a vertically integrated network of dark stores and company-owned bakeries, and also operates Breadfast Pay fintech services. The company serves 300,000+ active users across Cairo, Giza, Alexandria, and Mansoura and processes close to a million orders a month. Breadfast runs a consumer WordPress/WooCommerce marketing site and native iOS/Android apps and does not publish a public developer API; this profile tracks the company in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Chiquita Brands International
providers.description: Chiquita Brands International is a leading global producer, marketer, and distributor of bananas and other fresh produce, recognized worldwide by the iconic Blue Sticker on its bananas. Founded in 1899 as the United Fruit Company and rebranded as Chiquita in 1990, the company is headquartered in Etoy, Switzerland (with significant operations in Fort Lauderdale, Florida) and sources fruit from plantations across Latin America (Honduras, Guatemala, Costa Rica, Panama, Colombia, and Ecuador) for distribution in the United States, Europe, and other markets. Beyond core Cavendish bananas, Chiquita markets specialty banana varieties (organic, Reds, Manzanos, Minis), plantains, pineapples (including the Sunburst Gold variety), and partners with retailers worldwide. Chiquita does not currently publish a consumer-facing developer API; supplier, retailer, and grower integrations are managed through internal portals and bilateral EDI systems, and consumer-facing digital experiences focus on recipes, sticker collection campaigns, and retail merchandising.

providers.name: FabFitFun
providers.description: FabFitFun is a members-only lifestyle subscription company that delivers curated seasonal boxes of full-size beauty, fashion, wellness, and home products from premium brands, plus a members' community, customization, and weekly flash-sale shopping. Founded in Los Angeles and backed by 500 Global, Bond Capital, and Kleiner Perkins, FabFitFun serves over one million members with seasonal boxes valued up to $350 for as low as $65 per season. The company operates a direct-to-consumer commerce website, a members' account and box-customization experience, a support/help center, and the FabFitFun Magazine content property. As of this profile FabFitFun publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or API reference; this entry captures its public web and legal surface plus a probed domain-security posture, and remains a portfolio-sourced lead for further enrichment.

providers.name: Miniso
providers.description: MINISO is a global value retailer of lifestyle and consumer products — home goods, accessories, cosmetics, stationery, toys and seasonal items — known for its IP-collaboration merchandise (Harry Potter, PEANUTS, Sanrio, BT21 and others). Founded in Guangzhou, China and publicly listed (NYSE/HKEX), the company operates 7,700+ stores across 112 markets worldwide. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Hillhouse; the public web presence is consumer- and investor-facing and exposes no developer API, developer portal, or partner integration platform at this time.

providers.name: NOTHS
providers.description: NOTHS (Not On The High Street, notonthehighstreet.com) is a UK online marketplace that curates and sells unique gifts, jewellery, homeware and personalised products made or sourced by thousands of small UK creative businesses. Founded in 2006 and backed by Index Ventures, the platform connects independent sellers ("partners") with consumers through a curated storefront, seller onboarding, and an affiliate programme. It exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation surface; its api.notonthehighstreet.com host is a private backend serving the company's own web and mobile storefront. This profile is a VC-portfolio lead enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline via live domain/security probing.

providers.name: Retailo
providers.description: Retailo (Retailo Technologies) operates a B2B marketplace that helps independent retailers across the MENAP region (Middle East, North Africa and Pakistan) restock their shops, offering thousands of products, instant price comparisons and next-day delivery through the Retailo App. Its ecosystem also includes the Hisaab App, a fintech and bookkeeping product for merchants, and HORECA supply services for the hospitality trade. Founded by Talha Ansari, Muhammad Nowkhaiz and Wahaj Ahmed and backed by 500 Global, the company is operational in markets including the UAE and Pakistan. Retailo distributes its products as native iOS and Android mobile applications and, as of this profile, publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or programmatic integration surface.

providers.name: Smartsign
providers.description: Smartsign (SmartSign) is a Brooklyn, New York-based e-commerce retailer of customizable signs, labels, and tags for regulatory, compliance, and safety applications, founded in 1999. It sells pre-designed and custom signage - safety, parking, traffic, property, and facility signs, plus banners and labels - online to businesses of all sizes, including a large share of the Fortune 1000 across education, healthcare, and industrial verticals. Norwest Venture Partners acquired the company in 2019 and Sentinel Capital Partners acquired it in September 2022. SmartSign operates as a business-to-business and business-to-consumer e-commerce storefront and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: THG
providers.description: THG plc (formerly The Hut Group) is a UK-based consumer brands group founded in 2004 in Manchester and listed on the London Stock Exchange.
