Following the 2025 demerger of its Ingenuity technology and fulfilment division, THG is a pure-play consumer brands business operating two divisions: THG Beauty (home to Lookfantastic, Cult Beauty, Dermstore and prestige brand partners) and THG Nutrition (led by Myprotein, one of the world's largest online sports-nutrition brands). THG designs, manufactures and sells beauty and nutrition products direct-to-consumer across global markets. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Balderton Capital, an early investor. THG operates corporate, investor-relations and careers web properties but publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; this profile captures its identity and a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: Vend
providers.description: Vend was a cloud-based retail point-of-sale and inventory management software company founded in Auckland, New Zealand, backed by investors including Point Nine. Lightspeed announced its acquisition of Vend in March 2021 for approximately US$350 million, and the product lives on as Lightspeed Retail (X-Series). vendhq.com redirects to lightspeedhq.com/vend/, and the former Vend API is documented today at x-series-api.lightspeedhq.com. The X-Series API surface is profiled in the API Evangelist network under the Lightspeed provider, so this profile records the acquired Vend brand rather than duplicating that API.

providers.name: Burlington Stores
providers.description: Burlington Stores is an American national off-price department store retailer offering brand-name clothing, footwear, accessories, home decor, and more at everyday low prices. Explore a wide selection of high-quality, brand-name clothing, home decor, and more at unbeatable prices at Burlington.

providers.name: BuyBuddy
providers.description: BuyBuddy is an AI-powered retail merchandising platform positioned as an "AI Merchandiser that tracks, thinks & acts for you." It automates in-store operations for retailers and brands, including planogram compliance and shelf monitoring via computer vision, stockout prevention, product placement optimization, dynamic pricing and promotions, demand forecasting, store transfers, and shopper-behavior analysis through smart tags. BuyBuddy is a portfolio company of 500 Global. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; at time of enrichment BuyBuddy publishes no public developer API, documentation, SDK, or specification surface, so this remains a company-level profile.

providers.name: Warby Parker
providers.description: Warby Parker (NYSE: WRBY) is a direct-to-consumer eyewear and vision care company founded in 2010, selling prescription eyeglasses, sunglasses, contact lenses, and eye exams online and across 900+ retail stores. It operates a headless, modular commerce architecture and a proprietary point-of-sale system (Point of Everything), plus consumer-facing tools like Virtual Vision Test and PD measurement. Warby Parker does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; its API surface (api.warbyparker.com) is internal. The company does publish a public llms.txt for AI agents and an RFC 9116 security.txt with a bug-bounty contact. This API Evangelist profile captures that agent-facing and security posture; there is no OpenAPI/AsyncAPI or SDK surface to harvest.

providers.name: ARKO Corp
providers.description: ARKO Corp (Nasdaq: ARKO) is a Fortune 500 company and one of the largest operators of convenience stores and wholesalers of fuel in the United States. Through its subsidiary GPM Investments, ARKO operates approximately 1,400 company-operated stores under 25+ regional brands across 30+ states, as well as proprietary cardlock locations and a fleet fueling network. In 2026, ARKO completed the IPO of ARKO Petroleum Corp., which operates its wholesale, fleet fueling, and petroleum distribution segments.

providers.name: Barnes & Noble
providers.description: Barnes & Noble is the largest retail bookseller in the United States and the operator of the Nook digital reading platform. Barnes & Noble does not currently publish a public general-purpose developer portal. Trade and affiliate partners integrate through B&N's affiliate program, the B&N Press self-publishing platform for independent authors, EDI-based wholesale channels with publishers, and the Nook content distribution and reading ecosystem.

providers.name: Sonic Automotive
providers.description: Sonic Automotive is one of the largest automotive retailers in the United States, operating 100+ franchise dealerships across 13 states representing 25+ automotive brands, and operating EchoPark Automotive used-vehicle stores. The company invests in digital retail, inventory management technology, and automotive data platforms to enhance customer experience across vehicle sales, service, finance, and insurance. Technology partners include Stripe, NETSOL, and CDK Global.

providers.name: VF Corporation
providers.description: VF Corporation is a global apparel and footwear company headquartered in Denver, Colorado. VF owns major brands including Vans, The North Face, Timberland, Altra, Eastpak, Icebreaker, JanSport, Kipling, Napapijri, and Smartwool. The company does not offer a public developer API program; its technology integrations are handled through third-party e-commerce platforms and enterprise supply chain systems. VF Corporation operates more than 1,500 stores globally and integrates with platforms such as Shopify, Amazon, Magento, WooCommerce, and BigCommerce via third-party integration services.

providers.name: Beeline Bikes
providers.description: Beeline Bikes (now operating as Beeline Connect) is a B2B software platform for the bicycle industry that links riders, retailers, and brands across North America, with roughly 3,300 participating retailers. The platform provides real-time service scheduling and 24/7 appointment booking, live market inventory management, test-ride booking, local bicycle assembly coordination, warranty submission and reimbursement tracking, an affiliate e-commerce sales channel with revenue sharing to local dealers, and a dynamic dealer locator. It supports both mobile and in-shop retail operations and serves established brands such as Aventon, Priority, Lectric, and Pedego. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API, documentation, or integration surface has been found at this time.

providers.name: Bloom & Wild
providers.description: Bloom & Wild is a UK-founded direct-to-consumer flower delivery and gifting company, known for pioneering letterbox flowers that fit through a standard mail slot. Founded in 2013 and headquartered in London, it operates across the UK and Europe under a family of brands including Bloom & Wild, Bloomon and Bergamotte, offering one-off bouquets, plants, gifts and flower subscriptions through its website and mobile apps. Backed by General Catalyst and Index Ventures, it is a consumer e-commerce business rather than a public API provider; this profile captures its public web, security and domain posture. It publishes a /.well-known/security.txt security contact but no public developer program, OpenAPI, or API documentation was found.

providers.name: OpenStore
providers.description: OpenStore (Miami Labs, Inc. d/b/a OpenStore) is a Miami-based e-commerce holding company that buys direct-to-consumer Shopify businesses from their founders, offering data-driven valuations, offers in as little as 24 hours, and closings in about a week. After acquiring long-tail Shopify merchants, OpenStore uses its own software, marketing, and operations platform to run and grow the brands under one portfolio. Founded in 2021 by Keith Rabois and Atomic's Jack Abraham, OpenStore is backed by General Catalyst, Founders Fund, Atomic, Khosla Ventures, and others. It is a consumer/operator business and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its corporate and web-property surface.

providers.name: Dupe
providers.description: Dupe.com is a free AI-powered visual search engine and product-comparison platform that finds near-identical, lower-priced alternatives ("dupes") to designer and higher-priced products. Users paste any product URL, upload an image, or type a description, and Dupe's visual matching surfaces similar items from thousands of online retailers at up to 90% less — spanning furniture, home decor, fashion, footwear, beauty, and more. The service also offers AI research reports, room/outfit restyling, a Chrome extension, an iOS app, and a $DUPE rewards program, and it earns revenue through affiliate commissions at no extra cost to users. Dupe additionally operates a hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server so AI assistants can search its catalog programmatically. Backed by Kindred Ventures.

1919 (壹玖壹玖 / 1919酒类直供) is a Chengdu-based Chinese alcoholic-beverage retail and supply-chain platform operated by Sichuan 1919 Wines & Spirits SCM Co., Ltd. Founded in 2006, it runs an omnichannel online-to-offline model: the 1919吃喝 consumer app and a third-party e-commerce matrix layered on more than 3,000 franchised stores across 1,000+ Chinese cities, marketed on a 19-minute rapid-delivery promise, alongside a B2B liquor supply-chain business selling order management, logistics and data-marketing services to distributors. The company listed on China's NEEQ board in 2014 (830993), took a RMB 2 billion strategic investment from Alibaba in 2018, and delisted from NEEQ in 2023; its shares now change hands on private secondary marketplaces.

providers.name: A-Frame
providers.description: A-Frame Brands is a Los Angeles-based consumer brand incubator and product-development company founded in 2019 by entrepreneur Ari Bloom and actor Hill Harper. It partners with celebrities and cultural figures to build purpose-driven personal-care, beauty, fragrance, home-care, and pet-care brands, taking each from opportunity identification through product development, design, sourcing, production, and retail go-to-market. Brands in its portfolio include LOVED01 (John Legend), Kinlo (Naomi Osaka), Proudly (Gabrielle Union and Dwyane Wade), and Purrfect Paws, sold through retailers such as Target, Walmart, Amazon, CVS, JCPenney, QVC, and Bath & Body Works. Backed by Initialized Capital. This is a consumer company profile in the API Evangelist network; A-Frame publishes no public API or developer program.

providers.name: A-Frame Brands
providers.description: A-Frame Brands is a Venice, California based consumer brand incubator and product development platform founded in 2019 by Ari Bloom and Hill Harper. It builds and grows purpose-driven personal care, beauty, suncare, baby care, home care, and pet care brands, frequently in partnership with celebrity and talent founders such as John Legend, Naomi Osaka, Gabrielle Union, and Dwyane Wade, with a focus on products formulated for historically underserved and melanin-rich consumers. Its portfolio includes Loved01, Kinlo, Proudly, and Purrfect Paws, distributed direct-to-consumer and across more than 10,000 national retail locations including Walmart, Target, CVS, and Amazon. Backed by Forerunner Ventures. This is a consumer company profile in the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Being
providers.description: Being (Being Juice, operated by Being Global Sdn Bhd) is a Malaysian smoothie and cold-pressed juice brand founded by Sayantan Das, the former CEO of foodpanda Malaysia and Brunei, on the promise that "you are what you drink." The company sources ingredients from local farmers and handcrafts fresh, feel-good smoothies and juices daily, sold through physical outlets across the Klang Valley and through a mobile rewards app. Being is backed by 500 Global and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company profile awaiting enrichment. It publishes a consumer web presence but no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Bluestem Brands
providers.description: Bluestem Brands, Inc. is an American multi-brand direct-to-consumer retailer headquartered in Eden Prairie, Minnesota. It is best known for Fingerhut, a credit-based catalog and online retailer that extends revolving credit (via partner WebBank) to underserved consumers so they can purchase brand-name merchandise across home, electronics, apparel, and general merchandise categories. Bluestem historically operated a broader portfolio of catalog and e-commerce brands and reaches shoppers through its websites, mobile apps, and printed catalogs. No public developer program, API, or documentation surface was found for Bluestem Brands or Fingerhut at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: CityMall
providers.description: CityMall is an Indian social-commerce and e-commerce platform operated by Rashanbox Retail Private Limited (CIN U52190HR2020PTC086114), serving Tier-2 and Tier-3 towns through a community-group-buying model. Customers shop across groceries, staples, fashion, electronics, home and kitchen, beauty and health, kids and toys, and books and stationery, with cash-on-delivery and free-delivery options via web and native Android/iOS apps. The company runs on modern web infrastructure (CloudFront CDN, next-gen image optimization) and is backed by Accel, General Catalyst, and Norwest Venture Partners. No public developer API, portal, or documentation surface is currently published; this profile captures the company identity and its verified domain-security posture.

providers.name: GlamSt
providers.description: GlamSt (GlamST LLC) builds customized virtual makeover and try-on solutions for beauty brands and retailers, combining augmented reality (AR), artificial intelligence, and machine learning to power virtual makeup and cosmetics try-on across mobile, web, and in-store experiences. Founded with offices in San Francisco, Montevideo (Uruguay), and Wilmington (Delaware), the company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. GlamSt was acquired by Ulta Beauty in 2018 and integrated into Ulta's digital innovation team; it exposes no public developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface, so this profile is identity-only.

providers.name: Lexius
providers.description: Lexius is a Y Combinator-backed AI loss-prevention platform that turns a retailer's existing security cameras into proactive, revenue-protecting systems. It detects shoplifting in real time (concealment, product sweeping, known-offender entry), sends instant mobile alerts with video clips, and offers traceback search — natural-language search across every connected camera feed. Lexius also builds case files for law enforcement, flags known offenders chain-wide, and detects slip-and-fall events for liability protection. It connects to existing NVR/VMS systems from any brand, including Hikvision, Axis, Dahua, Hanwha, Bosch, Honeywell, Uniview, Lorex, LTS, Avigilon, and Genetec, and is typically deployed remotely in under 24 hours without replacing hardware. Lexius publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface as of this profile; it is delivered as a hosted dashboard plus camera/NVR integrations.

providers.name: Peach
providers.description: Peach (Peach, inc., ticker PEAC on secondary markets) was a Waltham, Massachusetts direct-sales retailer of intimate apparel, basics and athleisure for women, founded in 2013 by Janet Kraus (CEO) and Derek Ohly. It blended an in-home personal-styling experience delivered by a network of independent stylists with an online replenishment storefront at discoverpeach.com, raising roughly $10.2M before winding down. The company has since closed: its own homepage carries a farewell notice ("Peach has closed its doors") and refers customers to Cabi Clothing. Peach was a consumer retail brand, not a software vendor — it never operated a developer program, published no API documentation, and no machine-readable contract of any kind was found on its surviving surface.

providers.name: Send4 Tecnologia
providers.description: Send4 Tecnologia (rebranded as After Sale) is a Brazilian post-purchase platform for e-commerce, automating product exchanges, returns, and reverse logistics. Founded in 2017, it has processed over 6 million reverse-logistics transactions and offers intelligent authorization rules for approvals and blocks, a self-service customer exchange portal, real-time returns dashboards, revenue-retention offers (vouchers and cashback), integrated shipping labels and tracking, automated refunds and store credit, and multi-channel WhatsApp and email support. It advertises a simple, flexible API to connect with any e-commerce platform in minutes, though no public developer documentation is currently published. After Sale is now part of the Confi ecosystem alongside Neotrust and the Confi consumer app.

providers.name: Smart & Final Stores
providers.description: Smart & Final Stores is a warehouse-style food and supply retailer operating over 250 stores in the Western United States and 15 stores in northwestern Mexico. The company sells a wide variety of fresh perishables, everyday grocery items, and warehouse-club-sized products to both households and businesses. Smart & Final does not operate a public developer API program but participates in grocery industry digital commerce integrations through third-party platforms.

providers.name: SupplyHog
providers.description: SupplyHog is an ecommerce platform built specifically for hardware and building-materials retailers, giving independent hardware and building-supply stores a branded online storefront to sell their products. The platform provides co-op and custom product catalogs, flexible fulfillment (in-store pickup, ship-to-store, local delivery, and ship-to-home with Shippo shipping labels), Stripe-powered payments, TaxJar tax calculation, real-time ERP inventory and pricing synchronization, custom branding and domains, location-aware search, and admin tools for order fulfillment and abandoned-cart recovery. Founded in 2010 as the Nopone.com reverse-auction marketplace, SupplyHog went through the DreamIt and 500 Startups accelerators, pivoted to full ecommerce services, and was acquired by construction-supply retailer R.P. Lumber in 2016. It does not publish a public developer API surface; it acts as a consumer of Stripe, TaxJar, and Shippo.

providers.name: THIS
providers.description: THIS™ is a UK plant-based food company making high-protein vegan meat alternatives — including meat-free chicken, bacon, sausages, burgers and mince — sold through major British supermarkets such as Tesco, Sainsbury's, Waitrose, Ocado, Morrisons, Asda and Co-op. Founded in 2019 and backed by Seedcamp, THIS™ is a consumer packaged goods (CPG) brand focused on absurdly tasty plant-based food rather than a developer platform. It operates a marketing and recipe website but publishes no public API, developer documentation, or SDK at the time of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Bloomon
providers.description: Bloomon is a flower and gift delivery service that lets customers order one-off bouquets or sign up for a recurring flower subscription delivered on a chosen cadence. It offers seasonal hand-tied and letterbox arrangements, gifting options, gift vouchers, and add-ons, with delivery across the United Kingdom and other European markets. Bloomon is part of the Bloom & Wild Group (confirmed via its published .well-known/security.txt, which points to bloomandwild.com). The company operates a consumer-facing e-commerce and subscription website rather than a public developer API; this API Evangelist profile therefore captures its web, security, and discovery surface rather than a machine-readable API.

providers.name: Belk
providers.description: Belk is a privately-held American department store chain headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, serving the southeastern United States. The company sells clothing, handbags, jewelry, beauty products, and home goods. Belk operates an omnichannel retail model with physical stores and an online marketplace. Supplier and marketplace integrations are handled via EDI through value-added networks, with order management integration available through Rithum (formerly CommerceHub) and other channel management platforms.

providers.name: American Eagle Outfitters
providers.description: American Eagle Outfitters (AEO) is a global specialty retailer operating the American Eagle and Aerie brands, offering on-trend clothing, accessories, and personal care products at affordable prices. The company operates over 1,000 stores across the Americas and online, with a unified commerce strategy spanning e-commerce, mobile, and in-store experiences.

providers.name: Drop
providers.description: Drop (formerly Massdrop) is a consumer e-commerce brand operated by Corsair that sells limited-edition, community-driven products across mechanical keyboards, audiophile gear, and licensed gaming collaborations (Fallout, Cyberpunk 2077, The Witcher, Call of Duty and others). Founded in San Francisco and backed by Cowboy Ventures and other investors before its acquisition by Corsair, Drop runs a direct-to-consumer storefront at drop.com with a Zendesk-based support helpdesk. It is a retail brand with no public developer API program; this API Evangelist profile tracks it as a company in the network.

providers.name: ManoMano
providers.description: ManoMano is Europe's leading online marketplace dedicated to DIY, home improvement and gardening, operating consumer storefronts across France, Germany, Italy, Spain and the United Kingdom plus a ManoManoPro offering for construction professionals and craftsmen. Founded in France and backed by Partech, it connects millions of DIY, tools, heating, electrical, kitchen, bathroom, flooring and garden products from thousands of third-party sellers and brands to individuals and trade buyers. This API Evangelist profile was added as a portfolio-company stub; enrichment found a consumer marketplace with a published llms.txt and help center, but no public developer, seller or partner API surface (no developer portal, OpenAPI, or API subdomain resolves).

providers.name: Thrive Market
providers.description: Thrive Market is a membership-based online grocery retailer headquartered in Marina del Rey, California, selling organic and natural food, pantry staples, frozen meat and seafood, beauty and personal care, baby, pet and household products directly to consumers across the United States. Members pay an annual or monthly fee in exchange for below-retail pricing, and the company operates its own Thrive Market private label alongside thousands of third-party brands. It filters its catalog by diet, ingredient, certification and social value, accepts EBT/SNAP for grocery purchases, and funds free memberships for lower-income families through its Thrive Gives program. Thrive Market is a direct-to-consumer commerce company: it ships a website and mobile apps to shoppers, but publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: VANCL
providers.description: VANCL (凡客诚品) is a Chinese direct-to-consumer online apparel brand founded in October 2007 that sells its own-brand men's wear, women's wear, shoes, children's clothing, and home goods through vancl.com and official storefronts on Tmall, JD.com, Douyin, and Youzan. Once China's leading independent B2C fashion retailer, VANCL publishes no public API or developer platform today — its legacy open-platform hosts (open.vancl.com, api.vancl.com) no longer respond. Surfaced as a Qiming Venture Partners portfolio company in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Barnes & Noble
providers.description: Barnes & Noble is the largest retail bookseller in the United States, operating physical bookstores and an e-commerce site selling books, magazines, gifts, and educational products. Barnes & Noble also operates the Nook e-reader platform and offers affiliate and publisher partner programs. No public developer API is currently offered; the company operates primarily through retail channels and affiliate marketing programs.

providers.name: Delek US
providers.description: Delek US is an alias for Delek US Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: DK), a diversified downstream energy company headquartered in Brentwood, Tennessee with assets in petroleum refining, logistics, asphalt operations, renewable fuels, and convenience store retailing. Delek operates four refineries in Tyler and Big Spring (Texas), El Dorado (Arkansas), and Krotz Springs (Louisiana) with combined crude throughput capacity of roughly 302,000 barrels per day. The canonical profile for this company is maintained under aid delek-us-holdings; this entry exists as a name alias and references the corporate site. Delek does not publish a developer API; partner integrations occur through industry-standard EDI, terminal automation, and ticketing systems.

providers.name: IKEA U.S.
providers.description: IKEA U.S. is the United States retail operation of IKEA, run by Ingka Group, the largest IKEA franchisee. The U.S. business operates ~50+ full-service stores, ~40+ Plan & Order Points, and ~80+ pick-up locations across the country, alongside the ikea.com/us e-commerce site and the IKEA mobile app. Inter IKEA Systems B.V. separately owns the IKEA Concept and brand. IKEA U.S. offers home furnishings, kitchens, appliances, lighting, the IKEA Family loyalty program, the IKEA Business Network for B2B customers, home delivery and Click & Collect, design and planning services, the Buy Back & Resell program, and IKEA Home smart products controlled via the IKEA Home smart and IKEA Home smart 1 apps. IKEA U.S. does not publish a public developer API; supplier and trading-partner integrations are handled through IKEA's vendor systems and Ingka Group's internal digital platforms.

providers.name: iPrice
providers.description: iPrice Group is a Southeast Asian e-commerce aggregator and price-comparison platform headquartered in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. It aggregates billions of live product offers and thousands of coupons from more than a thousand retail partners, letting shoppers compare prices, discover deals, and make more informed purchases across seven markets: Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam, the Philippines, and Hong Kong. Backed by 500 Global as part of the Asia Venture Group portfolio, iPrice serves tens of millions of monthly visitors and is known for its large SEA e-commerce dataset. As of this profile, iPrice does not publish a public consumer or partner API, developer portal, or OpenAPI; this record is a company profile in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Aday
providers.description: Aday is a direct-to-consumer sustainable fashion brand founded in 2015 in New York City by Nina Faulhaber and Meg He. It designs technical, long-lasting capsule wardrobes built for outfit repetition, using custom recycled fabrics (including post-consumer recycled plastic) and plant-based, beechwood-derived materials produced in closed-loop processes. Aday has raised more than $10 million in venture capital, is backed by Cowboy Ventures, and has been named one of Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies, with coverage in Vogue, Refinery29, and Conde Nast Traveler. The company sells globally through its Shopify-powered storefront at thisisaday.com and does not publish a public developer API. This profile was created as an API Evangelist network stub from Cowboy Ventures' portfolio and enriched with company identity and domain-security signals; the storefront returned a Shopify "store is unavailable" lock at the time of the enrichment probe.

providers.name: Ergo
providers.description: Ergo (ergo Offers, Inc.) is a New York-based e-commerce pricing company that lets online shoppers name their own price. Its flagship product is a Shopify app that adds a "Make an Offer with ergo" button to product pages: a customer submits the price they are willing to pay and how long they are willing to wait, and the merchant accepts or rejects the offer from a backend dashboard. Beyond bartering, Ergo captures true willingness-to-pay data and turns it into pricing analytics and a price-discovery and optimization tool, helping retailers clear excess inventory and reduce blanket discounting. Founded and led by CEO Claire Stepanek (previously supply chain at Apple), Ergo raised a $1.5M pre-seed round in October 2023 led by Anthemis with Wischoff Ventures. Ergo does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its company identity.

providers.name: Family Dollar Stores
providers.description: Family Dollar is a chain of discount variety stores in the United States offering a broad assortment of merchandise including consumables, home products, apparel, and seasonal goods at low prices. Owned by Dollar Tree, Inc., Family Dollar operates thousands of locations across the country and serves millions of customers seeking value-oriented shopping. The company does not currently publish public APIs or a developer portal.

providers.name: Busy Ming Group
providers.description: Busy Ming Group (Hunan Mingming Busy Commercial Chain Co., Ltd. / 湖南鸣鸣很忙商业连锁股份有限公司) is a mass-market snack retail chain operator headquartered in Changsha, Hunan, China, and a consumer-sector portfolio company of HongShan (formerly Sequoia Capital China). It operates two discount snack store brands — Snacks Are Busy (零食很忙, founded 2017) and Zhao Yiming Snacks (赵一鸣零食, founded 2019) — which combined into a network of more than 21,000 retail locations, heavily concentrated in county-level cities and townships. The group publishes no public developer API; this profile captures the company's corporate, franchising, and investor-relations web presence.

providers.name: COSY
providers.description: COSY (CosyRobo) is a retail-technology robotics company that builds autonomous inventory robots for physical stores. Its flagship robot, SCOUT, roams store aisles using AI and machine vision to scan shelves, map products, audit stock levels, and check planogram compliance, feeding the results into a cloud-based management system so retailers can reduce out-of-stocks and improve on-shelf availability. Backed by 500 Global, the company was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; it publishes a marketing website but does not currently expose a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: GOAT
providers.description: GOAT (operated by GOAT Group) is a global online marketplace for authentic sneakers, apparel, and accessories, launched in 2015 and headquartered in the Los Angeles area. The platform pairs a consumer buying-and-selling experience with in-house authentication that verifies new and used footwear and streetwear from thousands of brands, and GOAT Group also operates the Flight Club consignment stores and the alias seller platform. GOAT was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z, accel, index-ventures, initialized-capital, matrix-partners, and sv-angel and added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-backed company profile. It runs a consumer commerce platform rather than a public developer API, so this enriched profile focuses on verified company identity and the security surface probed from its public domain.

providers.name: Homzmart
providers.description: Homzmart is a Cairo, Egypt-based online marketplace for furniture, home decor, appliances, and workspace products that connects thousands of local manufacturers, brands, and merchants with consumers across Egypt and the wider MENA region. Founded in 2019 by Mahmoud Ibrahim and Ibrahim Mohamed, the platform lists more than 55,000 products and layers in flexible financing, delivery, and assembly services. Homzmart runs consumer web and mobile storefronts alongside merchant-facing "Sell With Us" and "Homzmart For Business" programs, and has raised roughly $40M in venture funding including a $15M Series A, with 500 Global among its backers. No public developer API program, SDK, or API documentation was found during enrichment; the company publishes a vulnerability-disclosure page and standard trust/policy pages.

providers.name: LE TOTE
providers.description: Le Tote was an online women's clothing rental and subscription-box business founded in San Francisco in 2012 by Brett Northart and Rakesh Tondon, and a member of the Y Combinator Summer 2013 batch. Unlike Rent the Runway, which concentrated on high-end event wear, Le Tote rented everyday apparel and accessories through a rotating personalized "tote" driven by its own sizing and recommendation data. In August 2019 it agreed to acquire the Lord & Taylor department-store chain from Hudson's Bay Company; both businesses filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on 2 August 2020, and Saadia Group bought the assets that October. Saadia Group was reported effectively shut down in March 2024 and the letote.com site went offline that spring. Le Tote is defunct: the domain no longer resolves, and the company never published a public API or developer portal. This profile is retained as a historical record of its open-source engineering output.

providers.name: Mathem
providers.description: Mathem is Sweden's largest pure-play online grocery retailer, delivering fresh food, household goods and pantry staples directly to consumers' homes across Sweden. Customers browse and order the full assortment of a physical supermarket through the mathem.se website and native iOS/Android apps, and receive scheduled home delivery. Mathem merged with the Norwegian online grocer Oda to form one of the Nordics' largest online grocery groups, and its security and careers functions are now operated under the shared Oda organization. Payments are handled through Klarna and the major card networks. Mathem operates a consumer e-commerce storefront and mobile apps; it does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal. This API Evangelist profile was created as a SoftBank Vision Fund portfolio lead and enriched via the enrichment pipeline; the substantive public technical surface found is an RFC 9116 security.txt and an invite-only YesWeHack bug-bounty program run through Oda.

providers.name: Avon Products
providers.description: Avon Products is a global manufacturer and marketer of beauty and related products, primarily distributed through a network of independent sales representatives.

providers.name: Hemster
providers.description: Hemster is a fashion-technology company that modernizes tailoring and garment fit through a digital "Fit Profile" system. Customers create a personalized fit pattern once, then match any garment — new or from their existing closet — to that saved profile so it can be tailored to their perfect fit rather than to a standard size. The platform aims to reduce returns, extend the life of clothing people already own, and remove size-related hesitation at purchase, with a sustainability angle around keeping garments out of landfill. Hemster operates a consumer web app at my.hemster.co and a related returns/deadstock product ((re)vive / byrevive.com). It is backed by Bullpen Capital. As of this profile Hemster publishes no public developer, API, or integration surface; this record is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company lead.

providers.name: GNC Holdings
providers.description: GNC Holdings, LLC (General Nutrition Centers) is an American specialty retailer of health, wellness, and performance products including vitamins, minerals, herbal supplements, sports nutrition, diet, and energy products. Founded in 1935 and headquartered in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, GNC is a wholly owned subsidiary of Harbin Pharmaceutical Group following its 2020 acquisition. The company operates owned and franchised retail locations, online stores, and retail partnerships across approximately 50 countries.

providers.name: Home24
providers.description: Home24 is a leading pure-play home & living e-commerce retailer in Continental Europe, founded in Berlin in 2009. It operates across Germany, France, Austria, the Netherlands, Switzerland, Belgium and Italy, selling furniture and home accessories through home24.de and its sister storefronts with a catalog of more than 250,000 products, alongside its own private labels and logistics network. Since April 2023 Home24 SE has been part of the Austrian XXXLutz Group, and it was delisted from the Frankfurt Stock Exchange in September 2023. Home24 publishes no public developer API or OpenAPI definition; its programmatic surfaces are a partner/affiliate marketing program and marketplace seller integrations used to syndicate product-data feeds, plus a public engineering blog. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the API-artifact facets are not applicable because there is no public API surface to harvest.

providers.name: Sephora
providers.description: Sephora is a French multinational chain of personal care and beauty stores and a subsidiary of LVMH, operating 2,700+ locations worldwide and a large ecommerce footprint. Sephora does not publish a public developer API and does not maintain a public GitHub organization. The Sephora storefront and Beauty Insider loyalty program are accessed only through consumer apps and the website; affiliate marketing partnerships are brokered through third-party networks such as Rakuten Advertising and Skimlinks rather than a Sephora-owned API.

providers.name: Costco Wholesale
providers.description: Costco Wholesale Corporation is a Fortune 500 American multinational membership-only big-box retail chain that operates warehouse clubs offering a wide selection of merchandise at discounted prices. Costco does not publish a public developer API; supplier and trading partner integrations are conducted through EDI and B2B channels using ANSI X12 transactions and the Costco Supplier Portal. Costco operates an e-commerce site, the Costco Travel and Costco Pharmacy properties, and the Costco Photo Center.

providers.name: Love Bonito
providers.description: Love, Bonito is a Singapore-headquartered direct-to-consumer womenswear brand, founded in 2010 out of the BonitoChico blogshop and now one of Southeast Asia's largest vertically integrated fashion labels. It designs, manufactures and retails women's apparel — Signatures, Staples and Capsule collections spanning tops, dresses, bottoms, matching sets, petites and maternity — through its own e-commerce storefront, iOS/Android shopping apps and physical stores across Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Hong Kong, Cambodia and the Philippines. The commerce stack is a Next.js storefront on a Magento-derived backend with Storyblok for content, fronted by Cloudflare, with an internal Kong API gateway at api.lovebonito.com serving its own first-party apps. Love, Bonito publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable contract; its partner surface is an affiliate program run through third-party networks (Impact, FlexOffers), not a first-party API.

providers.name: Percolata
providers.description: Percolata is a Palo Alto, California predictive-analytics company that applies machine learning to help retailers optimize labor scheduling and marketing spend. Its platform forecasts hourly sales, in-store traffic, and takeout demand to drive staffing optimization and marketing budget allocation, with published claims of 4x higher forecast accuracy, 10-20% same-store sales lift, and a forecast-accuracy guarantee. Named customers include 7-Eleven, Uniqlo, and Telefonica. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Google Ventures (GV). Percolata does not publish a public developer portal or REST API reference; its retail platform is delivered as a managed product with custom application integration. The percolata.com marketing site is now served by Wix, which provisions a live, first-party Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint and an llms.txt for agentic access to public site content.

providers.name: TakeOff
providers.description: Takeoff Technologies, Inc. is an eGrocery micro-fulfillment company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts. It paired KNAPP-built robotic storage-and-retrieval hardware with its own cloud software stack — order management, inventory, pick routing, labor management, and delivery orchestration — into micro-fulfillment centers (MFCs) installed inside or beside existing supermarkets, so grocers could assemble online orders in minutes instead of sending shoppers down the aisles. Customers and partners included Albertsons, Wakefern Food Corp., Woolworths Group and Chilean grocer SMU. The company filed for Chapter 11 in May 2024 and Woolworths Group acquired its micro-fulfillment assets in August 2024. Takeoff never published a public developer program: there is no developer portal, API reference, SDK or machine-readable specification anywhere on its public surface, and the marketing site at www.takeoff.com no longer serves TLS. A closed API gateway at api.takeoff.com remains live and actively certificate-maintained, serving customer integrations behind authentication.

providers.name: Floward
providers.description: Floward is a leading online flowers and luxury gifting company headquartered in Kuwait and operating across the Middle East and the United Kingdom. Founded in 2017, the company delivers fresh flower arrangements, curated gift boxes, chocolates, cakes, and personalized gifts to more than 40 cities across 9 countries, sourcing blooms daily from ethical growers worldwide and offering same-day and scheduled delivery through its web store and mobile apps. Floward is backed by investors including 500 Global. This API Evangelist profile tracks Floward as a company in the network; as of this enrichment pass the company publishes a consumer e-commerce storefront and corporate site but no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDKs were found.

providers.name: The Bouqs
providers.description: The Bouqs Co. is a direct-from-farm online flower and plant delivery service headquartered in Marina del Rey, California, offering fresh cut bouquets, potted plants, wedding and event florals, and recurring flower subscriptions sourced from sustainable farm partners in South America and California. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Partech. This is a direct-to-consumer e-commerce brand: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, API documentation, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts. This profile captures verifiable company identity plus live domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Wolverine World Wide
providers.description: Wolverine World Wide is a leading designer, manufacturer, and marketer of branded footwear, apparel, and accessories. Brands include Merrell, Saucony, Wolverine, Sperry, Sweaty Betty, and Hush Puppies. The company operates global wholesale, direct-to-consumer, and digital commerce channels. Wolverine World Wide does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Clutch Canada
providers.description: Clutch is a Toronto-headquartered, vertically integrated online used-car retailer serving Canadian drivers. Unlike marketplace models that broker to third-party dealers, Clutch owns its own inventory and runs an end-to-end e-commerce purchase flow at clutch.ca: browsing reconditioned pre-owned vehicles, auto financing and a loan calculator, trade-in and sell-my-car offers, protection plans, insurance, and home delivery, backed by a 10-day money-back guarantee. It operates across Ontario, Nova Scotia, New Brunswick and Prince Edward Island. Clutch is a consumer retail business rather than an API vendor: its software is shipped as an end-user web application, and it publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Curaleaf Holdings
providers.description: The largest cannabis company in the world by revenue operating cultivation, processing, and retail dispensary operations. Operates in multiple U.S. states and international markets producing cannabis flower, pre-rolls, edibles, and vape products under leading brands.

providers.name: HelloFresh
providers.description: HelloFresh SE is a publicly listed (Frankfurt Stock Exchange: HFG), Berlin-headquartered global meal-kit and food-solutions company that ships recipes and pre-portioned ingredients to households across North America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific. Its brand portfolio includes HelloFresh, Factor, Green Chef, EveryPlate, Chefs Plate, Youfoodz, and Good Chop. HelloFresh does not publish a public consumer developer API; its engineering organization is active in open source on GitHub, maintaining widely used infrastructure tooling such as the Janus API gateway, the health-go healthcheck library, and the goengine event-sourcing framework. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of HV Capital and Insight Partners and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: J.C. Penney
providers.description: J.C. Penney Company, Inc. (JCPenney) is an American department store chain offering apparel, accessories, beauty, jewelry, footwear, and home goods. The company emerged from Chapter 11 bankruptcy in late 2020 and continues to operate hundreds of department stores across the United States and Puerto Rico.

providers.name: MUSINSA
providers.description: MUSINSA is South Korea's leading online fashion platform, founded in 2001 by Cho Man-ho as a streetwear community and now operating a marketplace that connects more than 10,000 brands with over 16 million members. The company reported roughly USD 3.3 billion in GMV and USD 907 million in revenue for 2024, returned to operating profit, and is pursuing a KOSPI IPO. MUSINSA runs domestic and global storefronts (musinsa.com, global.musinsa.com), a partner/seller program for K-fashion brands, and an engineering organization that publishes on the MUSINSA tech blog. It has raised funding from investors including KKR, Sequoia/Peak XV (formerly Sequoia Capital China / HongShan) and IMM Investment. No genuine public product/developer API or OpenAPI-backed developer portal was found during enrichment; a corporate CMS Swagger UI at dev-api.corp.musinsa.com is an internal tool (its public spec still points at the Swagger petstore demo), so this profile captures company identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Sensee
providers.description: Sensee is a French direct-to-consumer online optician and contact-lens retailer, operating since 2005 and run by licensed opticians. It sells contact lenses, lens-care solutions, eye-health products and eyewear across six European markets (France, Germany, Italy, Spain, Switzerland and Austria) under localized storefronts, and supports third-party insurance payment (tiers payant) via networks such as Kalixia, Santeclair, Almerys and Optilys. Sensee is a subsidiary of Vision Group Holding AG. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; the enrichment pass found no public API, SDK or developer program, only a corporate security.txt / responsible-disclosure surface.

providers.name: YOOX NET-A-PORTER (YNAP)
providers.description: YOOX NET-A-PORTER (YNAP) is a leading digital multi-brand luxury fashion group operating the online stores NET-A-PORTER, MR PORTER, YOOX, and THE OUTNET. Following the 2025 acquisition by Mytheresa, the group operates under the parent LuxExperience B.V. (NYSE ticker "LUXE"), pairing full-price curated luxury with off-price destinations. YNAP was surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital and added to the API Evangelist network. The group runs an engineering organization (YNAP Tech) and maintains public GitHub open-source tooling, but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or partner developer portal at this time.

providers.name: All3D
providers.description: ALL3D, Inc. is a San Francisco AI-powered visual content platform that replaces traditional product photography for ecommerce brands and agencies. Users upload a product photo and its real-world dimensions, build a scene from inspiration images and props, and generate 4K studio and lifestyle images, influencer/UGC-style video, editable 3D models, 360-degree spins, product configurators, and AR "view in room" experiences accurate to real-world scale. Additional tools cover magic erase, item replacement, scale adjustment, bulk generation across hundreds of SKUs, team review/approval workflows, and direct publishing to Shopify and Amazon. Enterprise plans add API access and managed services. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bullpen Capital and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Big Lots
providers.description: Big Lots is a discount retailer offering a wide assortment of brand-name closeout merchandise including furniture, food, consumables, seasonal products, soft home, hard home, and electronics. Big Lots operated hundreds of stores across the United States. In 2024, Big Lots filed for bankruptcy and its brand and operations were acquired by Nexus Capital Management.

providers.name: Cornershop by Uber
providers.description: Cornershop is an on-demand grocery and essentials delivery service founded in 2015 in Chile by Oskar Hjertonsson, Daniel Undurraga, and Juan Pablo Cuevas, simultaneously launching in Santiago, Chile and Mexico City, Mexico. The platform connects consumers with personal shoppers who pick and deliver groceries, pharmacy items, and other goods from local supermarkets, specialty stores, and big-box retailers. After a 2018 acquisition attempt by Walmart was blocked by Mexican regulators, Uber agreed in October 2019 to acquire majority ownership, completing full acquisition in July 2021 at a reported valuation north of US$3 billion — Chile's first unicorn exit. At its peak Cornershop operated in eight countries across the Americas: Chile, Mexico, Brazil, Colombia, Costa Rica, Peru, Canada, and the United States. Beginning in 2021 Uber merged the Cornershop brand into Uber Eats, migrating the grocery vertical ("Uber Eats Grocery") into its main consumer app and progressively shutting down the standalone Cornershop apps and websites. As of 2026 cornershopapp.com and cornershop.io redirect to ubereats.com, the Cornershop LLC GitHub organization (archived October 2024) has zero public repositories, and there is no public developer API, SDK, partner program, or technical documentation under the Cornershop brand — Cornershop survives only as engineering history and as the LatAm backbone of Uber Eats Grocery. Community-built unofficial Python wrappers exist on GitHub but reverse-engineer the consumer mobile app and are not sanctioned by Uber.

providers.name: Dillard's
providers.description: Dillard's is an American department store chain offering apparel, footwear, cosmetics, handbags, menswear, and home goods from top brands. The retailer operates stores across the United States and an e-commerce site, with no publicly documented developer APIs at this time.

providers.name: Doos
providers.description: Doos is a Saudi-based quick-commerce (q-commerce) platform and mobile app that delivers groceries, fresh produce, beauty, gifting, pharmacy, and lifestyle products in minutes across Saudi Arabia. Founded in 2023 by Tala Al Sahsah, it operates cloud/dark stores in Jeddah and Riyadh with localised assortments, prices, and promotions by city and delivery zone, offering a bilingual (Arabic/English) shopping experience. Doos is backed by 500 Global and received a strategic investment from Jahez to accelerate its expansion in the Kingdom's growing quick-commerce sector. This is a consumer-facing storefront; no public developer program or API has been identified at this time.

providers.name: Floom
providers.description: Floom is a curated online marketplace for flowers and plants that connects customers with a vetted network of independent local florists, enabling same-day and next-day delivery of designer bouquets, arrangements, and gifts across the United Kingdom and United States. Rather than operating central warehouses, Floom routes each order to a nearby artisan florist, and also provides those florists with e-commerce, ordering, and fulfillment technology to run and grow their businesses online.

providers.name: HD Supply Holdings
providers.description: HD Supply is one of the largest industrial distributors in North America, providing maintenance, repair, and operations products and value-added services to multifamily, hospitality, healthcare, and government facilities. HD Supply operates as a wholly owned subsidiary of The Home Depot following its acquisition in 2020.

providers.name: Purplle
providers.description: Purplle is an Indian beauty and personal care e-commerce marketplace headquartered in Mumbai, founded in 2012 by Manish Taneja, Rahul Dash, Suyash Katyayani and Anurag Neema. The platform sells skincare, makeup, haircare, fragrance, bath and body, grooming, mom and baby and wellness products across India, carrying a catalogue of 60,000+ products from 1,000+ brands alongside its own homegrown labels — Good Vibes, DERMDOC, Alps Goodness, NY Bae, FACES CANADA, Carmesi, Salm Skin and Juicy Chemistry. Purplle became an Indian unicorn in 2022 and is backed by ADIA, Kedaara, Premji Invest, Peak XV Partners, Goldman Sachs, Verlinvest, JSW Ventures and Blume Ventures. It operates a consumer website and mobile app plus 100+ offline stores, and publishes editorial guidance through Purplle Magazine. Purplle is a direct-to-consumer retailer: as of this profile it publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract. It does publish an llms.txt at its web root describing its catalogue for AI agents.

providers.name: Service Properties Trust
providers.description: Service Properties Trust (NASDAQ: SVC) is a real estate investment trust (REIT) with approximately $9.9 billion invested across two asset categories: service-focused retail net lease properties and hotels. As of March 31, 2026 SVC owned 761 net lease properties (over 13.6 million sq ft) and 93 hotels (over 21,000 guest rooms) throughout the United States. The company is externally managed by The RMR Group (NASDAQ: RMR). SVC does not operate a public developer program and exposes no public APIs, OpenAPI specifications, SDKs, or webhooks; investor-facing endpoints are limited to SEC filings, press releases, email alerts, and end-of-day stock quotes.

providers.name: Shopzilla
providers.description: Shopzilla is a comparison-shopping brand that lets consumers search across thousands of merchants to compare products, prices, and merchant ratings. Originally launched as BizRate and later Shopzilla, Inc., the business rebranded its corporate entity to Connexity in 2014 and is today operated by Connexity, a Taboola company, alongside sibling properties such as Bizrate, Beso, and PriceGrabber. Shopzilla itself publishes no API: no Shopzilla-branded developer host resolves in DNS (developer.shopzilla.com, api.shopzilla.com and docs.shopzilla.com are all NXDOMAIN), and www.shopzilla.com sits behind an AWS CloudFront WAF that bot-challenges the root and returns HTTP 403 on every other path, including all /.well-known/ locations. The publisher/affiliate API program that was historically marketed as the Shopzilla Publisher Program is today published under the CONNEXITY brand, on Connexity-owned hosts, and is deliberately not catalogued here: the docs are titled "Connexity Monetization API", list info@connexity.com as the contact, and are served from api.cnnx.link and publisher-api.connexity.com. The legacy Catalog API host catalog.bizrate.com does still answer, but returns bare Tomcat errors and publishes no specification. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners; the 2026-08-13 enrichment pass probed 18 paths across three hosts, swept five package registries, and found no Shopzilla developer surface of any kind.

providers.name: Topgolf Callaway Brands
providers.description: Topgolf Callaway Brands is a Carlsbad, California–headquartered modern golf and active lifestyle company, formerly Callaway Golf Company, that rebranded in August 2022 following its 2020 acquisition of Topgolf for approximately $2 billion. The company operates across three reportable segments: Topgolf entertainment venues, Golf Equipment (Callaway and Odyssey clubs and balls), and Active Lifestyle (TravisMathew, Jack Wolfskin, OGIO, and Callaway apparel and gear). Adjacent technology offerings include Toptracer, the ball-tracing platform powering over 1,200 driving ranges globally and used as the official ball-tracing partner for major broadcasters including NBC, CBS, Golf Channel, and Sky Sports, as well as Toptracer Range, Toptracer Go, and Topgolf Swing Suite golf simulation. In September 2024 the company announced plans to separate Topgolf into a standalone publicly traded company by late 2025, with Callaway retaining a minority stake and remaining its official golf equipment supplier. The company does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, partner SDK, or open-source library across any of its consumer or facility-operator surfaces. The TopGolf GitHub organization (github.com/TopGolf) contains only generic internal infrastructure tooling — RabbitMQ wrappers, Docker logging drivers, Ansible roles, AWS WAF templates, a Lyft iOS SDK fork — with no Topgolf-, Callaway-, or Toptracer-branded APIs, clients, or schemas. Toptracer facility integrations and Topgolf venue partnerships are handled through private commercial agreements rather than a self-serve developer program.

providers.name: Topo Athletic
providers.description: Topo Athletic is a performance footwear brand offering road running, trail running, hiking, and recovery shoes plus apparel and accessories (Topo Gear). Its shoes are known for a roomy toe box, secure midfoot and heel fit, low heel-to-toe drop, and the ZipFoam midsole, designed to promote natural movement and foot health. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Topo Athletic operates a direct-to-consumer e-commerce site at topoathletic.com; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation. It does publish a machine-readable /llms.txt describing its catalog and support surface.

providers.name: Tupperware Brands
providers.description: Tupperware Brands Corporation was an American multinational consumer goods company that manufactured and marketed premium kitchen storage, preparation, and serving products under the Tupperware brand, as well as related home product lines. The company distributed products to approximately 70 countries through independent sales force members. Tupperware Brands filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in September 2024 and underwent liquidation in 2025. The Tupperware brand name was subsequently acquired by Party Products LLC. No public developer API program was available during the company's operation.

providers.name: Ula
providers.description: Ula was a B2B wholesale commerce platform for small neighborhood retail shops (warungs), providing supply chain technology, inventory management, and credit access across Indonesia, India, and Singapore. Backed by Prosus Ventures, Ula closed its core operations in late 2023 and ula.app now hosts a retrospective of the company. No public API, developer portal, or SDKs were ever published, and no developer subdomains resolve.

providers.name: Westwing
providers.description: Westwing is Europe's number one "Beautiful Living" e-commerce company, present in more than 20 European countries. It is a premium one-stop Home & Living destination that offers design lovers a carefully curated selection of the best design brands alongside its own Westwing Collection, created by an in-house team in Munich, spanning furniture, sofas, lighting, beds, rugs, textiles, outdoor and home accessories. Westwing (Westwing Group SE) is a publicly listed company and was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of HV Capital and Point Nine. It publishes no public developer API; its primary machine-facing surface is a root-level /llms.txt policy that governs how LLMs and agents may use its catalog and editorial content.

providers.name: Boise Cascade
providers.description: Boise Cascade is a leading North American manufacturer and distributor of building materials for the residential and commercial construction industry. The company produces engineered wood products (EWP) including I-joists, LVL beams, and glulam, as well as structural panels and lumber, and distributes a broad range of building materials through its wholesale distribution network.

providers.name: Brodo
providers.description: Brodo (PT Brodo Ganesha Indonesia) is an Indonesian direct-to-consumer footwear and menswear brand founded in Bandung, selling shoes, apparel, and accessories through its official webstore at bro.do. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. Brodo runs a consumer e-commerce storefront on a third-party commerce platform (Plugo) with local Indonesian payment rails (NicePay); it publishes no first-party developer API, OpenAPI, developer portal, SDK, or public integration surface at this time, so there are no API artifacts to enrich beyond this company profile.

providers.name: Cosmart
providers.description: Cosmart is an Indonesian membership-only B2B e-commerce and procurement platform, founded in 2021 by Alvin Kumarga and Robert Tan, where members (individuals and SMEs) purchase their recurring daily and business needs in larger quantities at competitive prices. The platform lists over 100,000 products across categories including office supplies, electronics, household items, automotive parts, industrial equipment, furniture, and services, with nationwide delivery, flexible payment terms, and dedicated relationship managers for corporate clients. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Lightspeed India Partners. Cosmart does not publish a public developer program, API, or SDKs; this profile captures its identity and public web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Eyewa
providers.description: Eyewa is an online-first eyewear retailer serving the Middle East, selling prescription eyeglasses, sunglasses, clear and colored contact lenses, eyewear accessories, and eye-health vitamins through its e-commerce storefront and a network of 260+ physical stores with click-and-collect. Headquartered in Dubai, UAE, Eyewa operates across the GCC and offers regional payment options such as Tabby, Tamara, and Apple Pay. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global. Eyewa publishes a consumer storefront, an educational vision-and-eyewear blog, and standard commercial policy pages, but does not currently expose a public developer API, SDKs, or documented API surface.

providers.name: H&M
providers.description: A Swedish multinational fast-fashion retailer offering affordable clothing, accessories, and home goods. Operates thousands of stores globally and is one of the world's largest fashion companies. No public developer portal or open API catalogue was located on hm.com or hmgroup.com.

providers.name: Liberty Interactive
providers.description: Liberty Interactive Corporation owned and operated a broad range of video and online commerce companies, including QVC, HSN, and zulily, before being reorganized into Qurate Retail Group in 2018. The corporation tracked separate operating units through Liberty Interactive Group and Liberty Ventures Group tracking stocks.

providers.name: navabi
providers.description: navabi is an online retailer specializing in plus-size designer fashion for women, founded and headquartered in Aachen, Germany. As of July 2026 only the Canadian storefront (navabi.ca) is live: navabi.com now redirects to an unrelated parked domain (gitinama.site) and navabi.de returns a maintenance page, indicating the brand has largely wound down its international operations. The shop curates dresses, tops, jackets, jeans, coats, swimwear and accessories from luxury and contemporary labels such as Anna Scholz, Basler, Bogner, Lacoste, Roberto Cavalli and Zizzi, alongside styling advice, a fashion magazine and an affiliate program. navabi was surfaced as a portfolio company of Index Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. It is a consumer e-commerce brand with no public developer portal, API, well-known discovery surface, or published security program; enrichment probes captured only its web/domain security posture (navabi.ca).

providers.name: On
providers.description: On (On Holding AG) is a Swiss performance sportswear company founded in 2010, known for its CloudTec running shoes and athletic apparel. It designs and sells premium running footwear, clothing, and accessories worldwide through on.com and retail partners, and is publicly traded on the NYSE (ONON). On was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bond Capital. On does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures the company identity and its domain-security posture within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Packworks
providers.description: Packworks is a Philippine business-to-business technology company empowering micro-entrepreneurs through connected commerce. Its Sari IQ platform gives sari-sari store owners and other micro-retailers an integrated mobile, web, and chat-based toolkit for inventory management, bookkeeping, sales analytics, credit (utang) tracking, deliveries and collections, loyalty programs, and financial literacy. Backed by Techstars, Packworks operates as an end-user SaaS platform for neighborhood retail and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, well-known discovery surface, or integration program.

providers.name: Pennsylvania Real Estate Investment Trust (PREIT)
providers.description: Pennsylvania Real Estate Investment Trust (PREIT) is a Philadelphia-based mall REIT founded in 1960 by Sylvan M. Cohen. The trust developed, owned, and managed mixed-use retail destinations — including Cherry Hill Mall, Woodland Mall, Mall at Prince George's, and Springfield Town Center — across roughly nine states in the eastern and midwestern United States. PREIT filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection twice in four years. The first filing, on November 1, 2020, was a pre-packaged restructuring resolved by December 11, 2020. The second filing, on December 10, 2023, was a more consequential restructuring that wiped out public shareholders. PREIT emerged from its second Chapter 11 in early 2024 as a private company owned by its former lenders (reported to include Redwood Capital Management and Nut Tree Capital Management). Common shares were delisted from the New York Stock Exchange, and Jared Chupaila was appointed CEO of the reorganized, privately held entity. The post-emergence PREIT continues to operate its mall portfolio as a private operator. It exposes no public APIs, no developer portal, no documented machine-readable surfaces, and maintains no GitHub organization. This profile is preserved primarily to document the company's Chapter 11 history and its absence from the API economy.

providers.name: Related Companies
providers.description: Related Companies is a privately held, fully integrated real estate firm founded by Stephen Ross in 1972 as an affordable-housing developer and now active across luxury residential, affordable housing, retail, office, hospitality, data centers, and city-scale mixed-use development. Related is the developer of Hudson Yards in New York City, The Grand LA, Time Warner Center (now Deutsche Bank Center), The 78 in Chicago, and operates regional platforms including Related Beal, Related Midwest, Related California, Related Ross, and Related Argent in the UK. The firm owns and manages roughly 55,000 affordable and workforce housing units and has stated it has never converted a single affordable unit to market rate. Stephen Ross also owns a majority stake in Equinox Holdings (Equinox fitness clubs, Equinox Hotels, SoulCycle, Blink Fitness) and the Miami Dolphins / Hard Rock Stadium.

providers.name: Wineaccess
providers.description: Wine Access is an online wine retailer that curates limited-production and hard-to-find wines from around the world, sourced and vetted by its team of sommeliers and wine experts. Beyond direct e-commerce, the company operates a portfolio of subscription wine clubs (Discovery, Connoisseurs, Champagne, Collector's, Decanter, and Sunset clubs), a wine podcast and editorial content platform at discover.wineaccess.com, corporate and personal gifting, gift cards, and climate-controlled shipping. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners. As of this profile, Wine Access publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; it is a consumer e-commerce brand rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Zepto
providers.description: Zepto (Zepto Marketplace Private Limited) is an Indian quick-commerce grocery delivery company founded in 2021 that delivers groceries, fresh fruits and vegetables, meat, pet care, beauty and household products "in minutes" from a network of dark stores across major Indian cities. It operates a consumer-facing mobile app and website (zepto.com, formerly zeptonow.com) and publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; its partner-facing surfaces are limited to merchant onboarding (Sell on Zepto / brands.zepto.co.in), delivery-partner and franchise programs. Backed by General Catalyst, Lightspeed Venture Partners and Y Combinator.

providers.name: Barnes & Noble Education
providers.description: Barnes & Noble Education, Inc. (NYSE: BNED) is one of the largest operators of college bookstores in the United States, operating physical and virtual campus stores alongside digital course-materials and educational services. BNED reaches more than 5.7 million students through 1,125+ physical and virtual stores across higher education and K-12 institutions, primarily through its Barnes & Noble College Booksellers subsidiary and the MBS Textbook Exchange wholesale business. Flagship offerings include the First Day and First Day Complete affordable-access course-materials programs, BNC OER+ digital courseware, faculty adoption tools, campus retail and ecommerce services, and BNC AI Tools. BNED separated from Barnes & Noble, Inc. in August 2015 and is not affiliated with the Barnes & Noble retail bookstore chain. This repository captures any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable artifacts associated with BNED. No public developer APIs or developer portal have been identified at this time; integrations with campus systems and learning-management systems are delivered through institutional partnerships rather than a public API surface.

providers.name: Nordstrom
providers.description: Nordstrom is a leading fashion retailer offering compelling clothing, shoes, and accessories for men, women, and children through Nordstrom and Nordstrom Rack stores and online. Nordstrom does not currently operate a public developer portal or expose general-purpose APIs to third-party developers; this repository captures the company profile and any future developer-facing artifacts.

providers.name: Onda
providers.description: Onda is a ready-to-drink spirits brand that makes canned sparkling tequila — blanco tequila from a woman-owned distillery in Jalisco, Mexico, blended with sparkling water and real fruit juice and sold in 12 oz cans at 5% ABV, 100 calories, zero sugar and naturally gluten free, in lime, blood orange, watermelon and grapefruit. The company was founded in 2019 and launched publicly in July 2020 by Noah Gray (CEO), Max Dworin (COO), Kelli Adams (CCO) and actor-producer Shay Mitchell (Chief Brand Officer). It raised a $5M Series A in 2021 and a $12.5M growth round in 2022 from existing investors including Aria Growth Partners and 25madison, and sells through national grocery, liquor retail and third-party beverage e-commerce alongside its own direct-to-consumer store. NO PUBLIC API SURFACE: Onda is a consumer packaged goods company, not a software vendor — there is no developer program, no API documentation, no SDK and no machine-readable contract of any kind. Its only owned web property, drinkonda.com, is a Shopify storefront that on 2026-08-26 returned HTTP 404 "This store is unavailable" on every path probed, with a robots.txt that disallows all crawling and a Shopify-generated /llms.txt that states agent interaction is not possible; the last archived working capture of the storefront is 2026-02-18. Onda appears in the API Evangelist network because it trades on the private secondary market (EquityZen, Nasdaq Private Market), not because it publishes an API.

providers.name: bigbasket
providers.description: bigbasket is India's largest online grocery and daily-essentials retailer, now part of the Tata Group, delivering fresh produce, packaged foods, household, and personal-care products across Indian cities via web and mobile apps (bigbasket, bbnow, and bbdaily subscription delivery). Surfaced as a Bessemer Venture Partners portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. bigbasket operates as a consumer app rather than an API platform: it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or client SDKs. Its only first-party public developer surface is the github.com/BigBasket organization and the open-source @bb-tech react-admin UI component libraries on npm.

providers.name: Colgate-Palmolive
providers.description: Colgate-Palmolive Company is a global consumer-products manufacturer operating in oral care, personal care, home care, and pet nutrition through brands such as Colgate, Palmolive, Hill's Pet Nutrition, Speed Stick, Ajax, and Softsoap. Colgate-Palmolive does not publish a general-purpose public developer REST API. Its B2B integration footprint is centered on EDI exchanges with retail trading partners (X12 messages, AS2, VAN), supplier integrations through SAP Ariba, and internal corporate systems. There is also a corporate sustainability and ESG reporting surface, but it is not exposed as a developer API.

providers.name: Foot Locker
providers.description: Foot Locker is a global retailer of athletic footwear and apparel, operating stores under banners including Foot Locker, Kids Foot Locker, Lady Foot Locker, Champs Sports, Eastbay, and Footaction. Foot Locker does not publish a public developer portal or open API. Integrations with Foot Locker (loyalty, gift cards, retail media, e-commerce affiliate, supplier EDI) are arranged through partner programs and require commercial agreements.

providers.name: Lululemon Athletica
providers.description: Lululemon Athletica is a designer, distributor, and retailer of technical athletic apparel, footwear, and accessories for women, men, and girls. Lululemon does not currently publish a public developer portal or open APIs; digital integrations are handled through partner relationships and internal ecommerce, retail, and supply-chain platforms.

providers.name: Minted
providers.description: Minted is a San Francisco-based online design marketplace that crowdsources graphic and fine-art designs from a global community of independent artists and sells the winning work as stationery, wedding invitations, holiday cards, art prints, home decor, and personalized gifts. Its e-commerce storefront at minted.com pairs artist-submitted designs with in-house printing and fulfillment. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and Slow Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network; the enrichment pass probed for any public developer surface and found no documented public API — Minted operates as a direct-to-consumer commerce brand, not an API provider.

providers.name: Operand
providers.description: Operand is an AI-enabled pricing and commercial strategy platform for consumer retail, founded in 2024 and backed by Felicis, Y Combinator, SV Angel, and Soma Capital. It applies proprietary AI systems — an autonomous "agent swarm" — to set pricing and promotion strategy for mid-market and enterprise brands and retailers managing thousands of SKUs, volatile demand, and thin margins, running simulations to benchmark margin, revenue, and inventory-turn objectives before automating price changes. Operand is delivered as a managed platform with expert support and request-a-quote pricing rather than a public developer API; it currently publishes no OpenAPI, developer portal, or self-serve SDKs. An earlier Operand product at operand.ai offered an embeddings / semantic-search API with Python, Go, and TypeScript SDKs, now discontinued.

providers.name: Pep Boys
providers.description: Pep Boys is an American automotive aftermarket service chain founded in 1921 and headquartered in Bala Cynwyd, Pennsylvania. Owned by Icahn Enterprises since 2016, Pep Boys completed its transition away from retail parts in December 2023 and now operates as a service-only chain with roughly 850 to 900+ service centers across the U.S. and Puerto Rico, including a Pep Boys Mobile Crew offering for fleet and on-location maintenance. Pep Boys does not publish a public developer program, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or webhooks.

providers.name: Publix Super Markets
providers.description: Publix Super Markets is one of the largest employee-owned supermarket chains in the United States, headquartered in Lakeland, Florida. It operates grocery stores, pharmacies, delivery, catering, and online ordering services across the southeastern United States. Publix is a Fortune 500 company. No public developer APIs or developer portal have been identified at this time.

providers.name: PVH Corp
providers.description: PVH Corp, formerly known as the Phillips-Van Heusen Corporation, is an American clothing company headquartered in Manhattan, New York City and listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker PVH. Founded in 1881, PVH today operates two iconic owned global brands — Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger — along with licensed brands including Kenneth Cole New York and Michael Kors. PVH divested its Heritage Brands wholesale business (Van Heusen, Arrow, Izod, Geoffrey Beene) to Authentic Brands Group in August 2021, refocusing the company on its two flagship designer lifestyle brands. PVH does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal at the corporate level; technology and commerce integrations are handled brand-by-brand and through closed wholesale, licensing, and retail technology partnerships.

providers.name: Rent the Runway
providers.description: Rent the Runway is a New York-based fashion technology company operating a subscription and one-time rental service for designer apparel and accessories, delivered direct-to-consumer through its website and mobile apps. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass the company publishes no first-party public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal; its GitHub organization holds only internal Java/RabbitMQ tooling and forks, and third-party access is limited to an affiliate program run through external commerce networks.

providers.name: Wawa
providers.description: Wawa is a privately held, family-owned convenience store and fuel retail chain headquartered in Pennsylvania.
