Founded in 1803 as a dairy farm and operating convenience stores since 1964, Wawa runs approximately 1,100 stores across Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Delaware, Maryland, Virginia, Florida, North Carolina, Indiana, and Alabama. The company is a regional fresh-food, beverage, and fuel brand with a strong loyalty program (Wawa Rewards) and a mobile ordering app. Wawa operates an internal API management platform (built with MuleSoft) used to connect to third-party services such as Uber Eats, Grubhub, and DoorDash for delivery, but does not publish a public developer portal or expose public APIs.

providers.name: Williams-Sonoma
providers.description: Williams-Sonoma, Inc. is a Fortune 500 American publicly traded retail company specializing in kitchenware and home furnishings. It is one of the largest e-commerce retailers in the United States. The company operates multiple brands including Williams Sonoma, Pottery Barn, Pottery Barn Kids, PBteen, West Elm, Rejuvenation, Mark and Graham, and Green Row. Williams-Sonoma does not offer a public developer API. The company uses internal APIs and third-party platforms for e-commerce, registry services, and supply chain management.

providers.name: Dick's Sporting Goods
providers.description: Dick's Sporting Goods is a leading omni-channel sporting goods retailer offering an extensive assortment of authentic, high-quality sports equipment, apparel, footwear, and accessories. As a Fortune 500 retailer, Dick's Sporting Goods does not currently publish a public developer portal or APIs; this repository is maintained as a placeholder for any APIs, developer tools, or machine-readable artifacts that may emerge.

providers.name: Jumia
providers.description: Jumia is a pan-African e-commerce company often described as the "Amazon of Africa." Headquartered in Berlin and listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker JMIA since its 2019 IPO, Jumia Technologies AG operates a third-party marketplace, a logistics network (Jumia Logistics), and a digital payments arm (JumiaPay) across eight African markets as of 2026: Egypt, Ghana, Ivory Coast, Kenya, Morocco, Nigeria, Senegal, and Uganda. The company exited Algeria in February 2026 and previously wound down Cameroon, Gabon, Rwanda, and Tunisia as part of a multi-year restructuring program targeting full-year profitability in 2027. Jumia's commerce platform connects more than 100,000 sellers with consumers across diverse categories including phones and electronics, fashion, home and living, beauty, FMCG, and groceries. Its developer surface is non-trivial: the Jumia Vendor API (vendor center, OAuth 2.0) supports order, inventory, product, and shipment integration for marketplace sellers, while the legacy SellerCenter API (a SellerCenter / Rocket Internet lineage shared with Lazada and Daraz) remains documented with PHP, Python, Ruby, and Node SDKs. JumiaPay exposes a Merchant API for payment creation, verification, refund, recurring-payment agreements, and callback-based webhooks, plus official WooCommerce and Magento payment-gateway plugins. The Jumia GitHub organization is sparse (an open-source playbook, Jumia Tech Blog, and Tech in Porto event site) while the JumiaPay AIG GitHub org hosts the WooCommerce and Magento gateway plugins under Apache 2.0.

providers.name: Acne Studios
providers.description: Acne Studios is a Stockholm-based fashion house founded in 1996 as part of the creative collective ACNE (Ambition to Create Novel Expressions). The company designs and sells ready-to-wear womenswear and menswear, footwear, leather goods, denim, and accessories through its global network of retail stores and its official e-commerce site at acnestudios.com. Surfaced as a portfolio company of idg-capital and added to the API Evangelist network. Acne Studios publishes no public developer API program or developer portal; this profile captures its public web identity and live domain-security posture. Sector: consumer / fashion retail.

providers.name: Ailumia
providers.description: Ailumia is an AI-driven retail operations platform that helps brands and sellers grow on the world's most valuable marketplaces, with a focus on Amazon. The platform applies artificial intelligence across the retail workflow to manage marketplace sales, inventory, supply chain, and finances, giving operators data-driven guidance and automation to navigate the challenges of modern e-commerce. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in Taipei, Taiwan, Ailumia is backed by 500 Global. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced from the 500 Global portfolio; enrichment probing found a Cloudflare-fronted WordPress marketing presence but no public developer, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Alltricks
providers.description: Alltricks is a French online retailer specializing in cycling, running, and outdoor / mountain-sports equipment. Founded in 2008 and headquartered near Paris in Saint-Cyr-l'Ecole (Yvelines), France, the company sells bikes and frames, components and parts, apparel, footwear, nutrition, and accessories across France and multiple European markets. Alltricks operates as a direct-to-consumer e-commerce storefront at alltricks.fr and was an early Partech portfolio company. As of this pipeline run the company publishes no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or /.well-known/ discovery surface; this profile captures its identity and the domain-security posture of its production host.

providers.name: amberjack
providers.description: Amberjack is a direct-to-consumer men's footwear brand based in Brooklyn, New York, that designs and manufactures dress shoes engineered with athletic-inspired technology such as heat-activated arch support and dual-density outsoles for all-day comfort in hybrid work settings. The company sells direct to consumers through a Shopify storefront and is backed by Slow Ventures. Enrichment found no public developer or API surface (no docs portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, OAuth, or /.well-known endpoints); it remains catalogued as a consumer-brand company profile rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Anycart
providers.description: Anycart is a consumer grocery delivery and store-pickup platform that lets shoppers enter a zip code, choose a favorite local grocery store, and shop for anything they need with no price markups and no service fees. The service spans multiple U.S. retailers and focuses on transparent pricing for everyday grocery ordering, delivery, and pickup. Anycart was surfaced as a portfolio company of Menlo Ventures and Techstars and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. It operates a consumer web and mobile storefront (anycart.com) and does not publish a public developer program, OpenAPI definition, or API documentation at this time.

providers.name: appconomy
providers.description: Appconomy was a mobile-commerce platform company, founded in 2010 and dual-headquartered in Austin, Texas and Shanghai, China, that let brands, retailers, service providers, and mobile carriers add commerce functionality (daily deals, coupons, loyalty and rewards, mobile gifting, and merchant app generation for marketplaces such as Taobao) to their mobile apps. It was venture-backed with strategic investors including Qiming Venture Partners (lead of a $10M Series A), True Ventures, Neusoft Holdings, and WTI. The company is now permanently closed and publishes no live developer surface. The appconomy.cn domain does not resolve, appconomy.com returns 404, and no public API, documentation, developer portal, SDK, or /.well-known/ endpoint could be found. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-graph record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: asgoodasnew
providers.description: asgoodasnew is a German e-commerce retailer of refurbished and pre-owned consumer electronics, including smartphones, tablets, laptops, cameras, and related accessories, sold with warranty through its online store at asgoodasnew.de (asgoodasnew.com redirects there). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Point Nine and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. Probing the public surface found no developer portal, API documentation, or API host — this is a consumer-facing storefront with no public API program at this time. The profile is retained as a portfolio lead; only mechanical domain-security signals for the web host could be captured.

providers.name: Babycare
providers.description: Babycare is a Chinese mother-and-baby (母婴) consumer brand offering a broad range of maternity and infant-care products, including diapers, wipes, strollers, baby carriers, feeding bottles, toys, and maternal care goods. It operates primarily as a direct-to-consumer brand, selling through major Chinese e-commerce marketplaces (Tmall, JD.com, Douyin) alongside its own channels and offline retail, and is one of the leading new-generation mother-baby brands in China. Babycare is backed by venture investor Hongshan (formerly Sequoia Capital China). This profile is a consumer-brand entry in the API Evangelist network; no public developer API surface has been identified for this provider.

providers.name: BAMA TEA
providers.description: BAMA TEA (八马茶业), a brand of Fujian Bama Tea Industry Co., Ltd., is a large-scale Chinese tea enterprise founded in 1997 and headquartered in Anxi County, Quanzhou, Fujian Province. It integrates tea plantation cultivation, production and processing, branded retail-chain distribution, and export, and is best known for Tieguanyin oolong. The company operates a nationwide network of branded retail stores across China and sells oolong, black, green, white, and dark teas. It is a publicly listed company and a portfolio investment of IDG Capital. Added to the API Evangelist network as a consumer-sector lead: BAMA TEA publishes a consumer e-commerce website but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface, so the API-artifact enrichment recipes do not apply.

providers.name: Bed Bath And Beyond
providers.description: Bed Bath & Beyond was a chain of domestic merchandise retail stores selling home furnishings, bedding, kitchenware, and other home goods. The company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in April 2023. The brand was subsequently acquired by Beyond Inc. (formerly Overstock.com), which relaunched Bed Bath & Beyond as an online retail destination. Beyond Inc. also owns Overstock, buybuy BABY, and related brands.

providers.name: Belle International
providers.description: Belle International Holdings (百丽国际) is one of China's largest women's footwear and fashion retailers, designing, manufacturing, and distributing shoe brands such as Belle, Teenmix, Tata, and Staccato alongside a sportswear-distribution business, across thousands of directly operated retail outlets and a growing e-commerce presence. Formerly listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, the group was taken private in 2017 by a consortium led by Hillhouse Capital and CDH Investments in one of the largest Hong Kong take-private deals. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Hillhouse; enrichment found no public developer portal, API program, or machine-readable API surface for this consumer-retail company. This remains an identity and domain-security profile rather than an integratable API provider.

providers.name: BetaStore, Beta Store
providers.description: BetaStore (legal entity SimpleMarket Inc., trading as BetaStore.co) is a B2B retail marketplace founded in 2020 by Steve Dakayi-Kamga and Leo-Armel Tchoudjang that serves informal neighborhood retailers in West and Central Africa, operating across Nigeria, Senegal and Ivory Coast from offices in Lagos and a Wilmington, Delaware registration. The platform lets small shopkeepers restock fast-moving consumer goods directly from manufacturers and distributors at wholesale prices, ordering through SMS, chat, WhatsApp and a mobile app, with logistics partners delivering to the store within 24 hours, and it layers embedded working-capital financing on top of observed retailer sales. BetaStore raised a 2.5 million dollar pre-Series A in May 2022 led by 500 Global with VestedWorld and Loyal VC. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass BetaStore publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDK or machine-readable artifact of any kind, and its betastore.co domain serves no content -- both the apex and www hosts answer every path with a blanket Cloudflare 301 to unrelated third-party domains, and no api/app/docs subdomain resolves.

providers.name: Big Heart Pet Brands
providers.description: Big Heart Pet Brands was a producer and marketer of branded pet food and snacks with brands including Meow Mix, Milk-Bone, Kibbles 'n Bits, 9Lives, Natural Balance, Pup-Peroni, Gravy Train, Nature's Recipe, Canine Carry Outs, and Milo's Kitchen. Big Heart Pet Brands was acquired by The J.M. Smucker Company in 2015 and no longer operates as an independent entity. All brands are now managed under J.M. Smucker's Pet Foods division.

providers.name: black-unique
providers.description: Black Unique (全球购骑士特权, "Global Shopping Knight Privilege") is a membership-based consumer e-commerce and discounts platform founded in 2018 and headquartered in Guangzhou, China. Its core product is a privileges/membership card that aggregates discounts and special offers across a wide range of consumer categories: online shopping on major marketplaces such as Tmall, JD.com and Kaola, in-person shopping at international duty-free shops, outlets and supermarkets across 24-plus countries, plus dining, entertainment, travel and fuel. The company operates a consumer-facing app and website rather than a public developer program, and is backed by Qiming Venture Partners along with CCV, Eastern Bell Venture Capital and INCE Capital. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a Qiming portfolio lead; enrichment found no public API, developer portal, SDK, or other developer surface.

providers.name: Blue Bottle Coffee *
providers.description: Blue Bottle Coffee is a specialty coffee roaster and retailer founded in 2002 in Oakland, California by James Freeman, known for freshly roasted single-origin beans, seasonal blends, cafes, and a direct-to-consumer subscription service that ships coffee within 48 hours of roasting. A majority stake was acquired by Nestle in 2017. The company operates cafes across the United States and Asia and sells whole-bean coffee, brewing equipment, and gift subscriptions through its e-commerce site. Surfaced as a portfolio company of gv, kindred-ventures and true-ventures; no public developer API program has been found. Sector: consumer.

providers.name: Bluestone
providers.description: BlueStone is one of India's largest online retailers of fine jewellery, founded in 2011 by Gaurav Singh Kushwaha and headquartered in Bangalore. It runs an omnichannel model spanning its e-commerce storefront and 125+ physical stores across India, offering 7,000+ BIS-hallmarked and certified designs in gold, diamond, gemstone, and platinum, plus services such as lifetime exchange, buyback, 30-day returns, and personal video consultations. The company is backed by Accel. BlueStone publishes no public developer portal or API; this profile captures the company's identity and a probed domain-security posture for the network.

providers.name: Bon-Ton Stores
providers.description: The Bon-Ton Stores was a regional department store chain in the United States that operated stores across the Midwest, Northeast, and upper Great Plains. Founded in 1898 in York, Pennsylvania, the company sold apparel, accessories, cosmetics, home furnishings, and other merchandise under banners including Bon-Ton, Bergner's, Boston Store, Carson's, Elder-Beerman, Herberger's, and Younkers. The company filed for bankruptcy and ceased operations in 2018.

providers.name: Bonobos
providers.description: Bonobos is a US menswear brand and direct-to-consumer e-commerce retailer, founded in 2007 and known for pioneering online-first apparel sales alongside its physical "Guideshop" fitting-room locations. It sells men's clothing including pants, chinos, dress shirts, suits, and casualwear through bonobos.com. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Accel, Felicis and Lightspeed Venture Partners, it is a consumer-sector retail company. Bonobos publishes a public retail website but does not operate a public developer API program; this profile captures its real published surface (identity, legal, support, and domain-security posture).

providers.name: BrandCT
providers.description: BrandCT (品牌CT) is an offline-retail market-monitoring service operated by Mashangying (马上赢市场调查 / yikuaigao), a Chinese retail-data company. It has built a national offline-retail monitoring network based on POS data from a panel of sample stores, and delivers brand owners a "BrandCT" service that scans more than 10 million products across offline retail formats to quantify market share, distribution (铺市率), and product sell-through. The platform supports quantitative analysis of product innovation, channel competition, and category trends to speed up and sharpen client decision-making. The product is delivered through a login-gated web dashboard (WeChat, phone, and email verification sign-in); no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or /.well-known discovery surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Brightloom
providers.description: Brightloom is a San Francisco customer data and customer intelligence platform for restaurant and retail brands. It began as Eatsa, the automated quinoa-bowl restaurant chain, and rebranded to Brightloom in 2019 when Starbucks licensed select components of its Digital Flywheel customer engagement software to the company, took an equity stake and a board seat alongside a $30M round. The product unifies point-of-sale, loyalty, ecommerce and marketing data into a single customer view, reports on data health, runs AI-driven hyper-segmentation and anomaly detection over that data, and recommends the next campaign and audience a brand should target. Brightloom was sold as an end-user SaaS with prebuilt connectors to common POS, loyalty and marketing platforms rather than as a developer platform, and it published no public API reference, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification. The company now appears defunct: the last dated item on its own press page is December 2022, the entire operating estate it once held TLS certificates for is gone from DNS — api.brightloom.com, api-prd/api-dev, the cgp.brightloom.com application, its auth0-cgp Auth0 tenant, and the status, support and knowledgebase hosts all NXDOMAIN — brightloom.com publishes no MX record, and only the frozen marketing site remains, with its /about/ page defaced by injected search-spam.

providers.name: BuyWithMe (Gilt Groupe)
providers.description: BuyWithMe (Gilt Groupe) is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: commerce. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Bzaar
providers.description: Bzaar is a cross-border business-to-business wholesale marketplace founded in 2020-2021 by Nishant Verman (previously head of corporate development at Flipkart) and Prasanth Nair (previously engineering and product at Amazon, Flipkart, and Lazada), headquartered in Palo Alto / San Francisco, California with operations in India. The platform connected small and medium retailers in the United States and other markets with curated suppliers and manufacturers in India and Southeast Asia, listing thousands of products across home, lifestyle, accessories, apparel, jewelry, cookware, and bakeware verticals, and layering sourcing services such as vendor management, quality control, consolidated logistics, and cross-border payments on top of the catalog. Bzaar raised a $4 million seed round led by Canaan Partners with participation from Binny Bansal, Sameer Nigam, Rahul Chari, Lee Fixel, and Ashish Gupta. As of this enrichment pass Bzaar publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface, and its bzaar.com domain resolves to a registrar parking page rather than a live product site.

providers.name: Caleres
providers.description: Caleres is an American footwear company headquartered in Clayton, Missouri, established in 1878 (rebranded from Brown Shoe Company in 2015). It designs, develops, sources, manufactures, and distributes footwear through its Famous Footwear retail segment (approximately 900 U.S. locations) and Brand Portfolio segment which includes Sam Edelman, Stuart Weitzman, Allen Edmonds, Naturalizer, Vionic, LifeStride, Dr. Scholl's, Rykä, Franco Sarto, and Blowfish Malibu. Caleres does not currently publish a public developer API program; integrations are typically handled through B2B EDI and partner channels.

providers.name: Cap Hill Brands
providers.description: Cap Hill Brands was a Seattle-based e-commerce brand aggregator founded in 2020 by Kevin Saliba and Jason LeeKeenan (both former Zulily leaders). Operating as a "tech-first" Amazon aggregator, it acquired and operated digitally-native consumer/CPG brands sold on Amazon, Walmart, and Shopify, handling supply chain, marketing, and warehousing. It raised roughly $250M in debt and equity and acquired nearly 35 brands (including Butterfly Craze, merka, and LilGadgets). In March 2024 Cap Hill Brands merged with product developer Juvo+ to form Infinite Commerce, which has since been absorbed into Razor Group. Cap Hill Brands is a consumer operating company, not an API provider: it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specs, SDKs, or partner integration surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Version One Ventures and retained in the API Evangelist network as an identity record.

providers.name: Cazoo
providers.description: Cazoo was a UK online used-car retailer founded in 2018 by Alex Chesterman, offering a direct-to-consumer platform to buy, sell, and finance used cars fully online with home delivery. The company listed on the New York Stock Exchange via a SPAC merger in 2021 before restructuring and entering administration in 2024; its consumer marketplace brand was subsequently sold. Cazoo was surfaced as a portfolio company of D1 Capital, General Catalyst, and Sapphire Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. No public developer portal or API surface was found during enrichment: the site is behind bot protection (HTTP 429) and no /.well-known/ discovery documents are published. Sector: ecommerce / automotive retail.

providers.name: chatail
providers.description: Chatail is a Shanghai-based SaaS company (founded 2016) that provides private-domain livestream and video sales software for high-end and luxury retail brands across fashion, jewelry, beauty, automotive, and home-goods verticals, pairing intelligent customer acquisition with conversion tooling ("智能获客与高效转化双轮驱动"). The product is delivered as a hosted web application at chatail.com; no public developer API, documentation portal, or OpenAPI surface is published at this time (api.chatail.com serves a default nginx placeholder). Chatail raised a Series B round led by Qiming Venture Partners and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a Qiming portfolio company.

providers.name: Chi Forest
providers.description: Chi Forest (marketed as CHI FOREST) is the US-facing consumer beverage brand of the Chinese drinks company Genki Forest (元气森林), backed by Hongshan (Sequoia China) and IDG Capital. The company produces zero-sugar, zero-calorie, zero-caffeine sparkling refreshers with Asian-inspired, fruit-forward flavors such as guava and lychee, distributed through retailers including Costco, Amazon, and H Mart. It is a direct-to-consumer and retail beverage brand with a marketing/e-commerce web presence and no public developer platform, API, or documentation surface at this time. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a consumer-sector company record.

providers.name: Chico's FAS
providers.description: Chico's FAS, Inc. is an American women's specialty retailer headquartered in Fort Myers, Florida, operating and franchising stores and websites under the Chico's, White House Black Market, and Soma brands. The company is a leading omni-channel specialty retailer of private branded sophisticated, casual-to-dressy clothing, intimates, sleepwear, and related accessories, with more than 1,400 retail and outlet stores in the United States and a substantial e-commerce footprint. Chico's FAS is part of the KnitWell Group portfolio. Chico's FAS does not currently publish a public consumer-facing developer API; partner integrations are coordinated through corporate channels and the loyalty/credit card partnership with Synchrony and Mastercard.

providers.name: Cider
providers.description: Cider is a global direct-to-consumer digital-first fashion brand geared toward Gen Z shoppers, founded in 2020 and operating primarily at shopcider.com and through its mobile apps. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), DST Global, and Greenoaks Capital, Cider reached unicorn valuation as a fast-fashion challenger to SHEIN, using a data- and community-driven, on-demand manufacturing model to offer trend-forward women's clothing and accessories worldwide. Cider is a consumer retailer; it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation. This profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: CleanCo
providers.description: CleanCo is a United Kingdom-based beverage company, founded in 2019 by Spencer Matthews, that produces premium low- and no-alcohol alternative spirits. Its product line replicates the flavour profiles of traditional spirits across key categories, including CleanGin, CleanRum, CleanVodka and CleanTequila, aimed at consumers who want to reduce alcohol consumption without sacrificing taste. The company sells direct-to-consumer through cleanliquor.com and through grocery and hospitality retail channels across the UK and international markets. CleanCo raised venture funding from Lightspeed Venture Partners in 2020. It is a consumer packaged-goods brand and does not publish a developer API, developer portal, or any machine-readable API surface; it is retained in the API Evangelist network only as an identified Lightspeed portfolio company, not as an API provider.

providers.name: Clothes Horse
providers.description: Clothes Horse was a New York-based, data-driven size-and-fit recommendation company for online apparel shopping. It matched a shopper's body measurements and brand preferences against retailers' actual garment measurements to recommend the right size at the point of sale, sold to retailers as SaaS. The company merged with Fits.me in December 2014 to form a virtual-fitting-room solutions provider, and no longer operates as an independent entity. It exposed no public API, developer portal, or documentation, and the clotheshor.se domain now resolves to an unrelated Swedish fashion/lifestyle WordPress blog. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead; enrichment found no live API surface.

providers.name: Club Factory
providers.description: Club Factory was a Chinese-owned cross-border e-commerce marketplace app that grew to roughly 70 million users globally, with India its largest market at around 40 million users. In June 2020 the Government of India banned Club Factory alongside 58 other Chinese apps citing data and privacy concerns, and the company withdrew from the Indian market shortly after. It was originally added to the API Evangelist network as a stub lead surfaced from Qiming's portfolio. Enrichment finds the company effectively defunct - clubfactory.com no longer serves a company site (it is parked for sale via Afternic nameservers and redirects to a /lander page), there is no live developer or API surface, no published SDKs, and no discoverable /.well-known documents.

providers.name: Copia Global
providers.description: Copia Global was a Kenyan B2C e-commerce and last-mile distribution company founded by Tracey Turner and Jonathan Lewis to serve middle- and low-income consumers across rural and peri-urban Africa. Rather than a consumer website, it ran an agent-network model in which customers placed catalog orders through local agents using mobile and USSD technology, and Copia processed, aggregated, and delivered goods within days. Backed by investors including DCVC and Goodwell, the company raised a $50M Series C in 2022 to expand, but suspended Uganda operations in 2023, entered administration in May 2024, and was subsequently placed into liquidation. It exposes no public API, developer portal, or specification; its primary domain now resolves to a parked page. This profile is retained as a portfolio lead for network coverage.

providers.name: Core-Mark Holding
providers.description: Core-Mark Holding Company, a subsidiary of Performance Food Group, is one of the largest broad-line, full-service marketers and distributors of packaged consumer products to the convenience retail industry in North America. The company serves more than 41,000 retail locations across the United States and Canada, supplying tobacco, candy, snacks, beverages, foodservice, and other fast-moving consumer goods. Core-Mark provides retailer technology platforms including Core-Source Portal, Retailer Analytics, Core-Mark Ordering, and Core-Mark Intellisite.

providers.name: Craftsvilla
providers.description: Craftsvilla was an India-based online marketplace for ethnic and handcrafted products — sarees, ethnic apparel, jewelry, footwear, accessories, beauty and home decor sourced from artisans, weavers and small sellers across India. Founded in 2011 and headquartered in Mumbai, it was backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, Nexus Venture Partners and Global Founders Capital before winding down its consumer operations around 2019 amid financial difficulties. It was surfaced as a Lightspeed portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Enrichment found no live public developer surface: the storefront domain now serves a broken AWS S3 redirect (www.craftsvilla.com is NXDOMAIN) and there is no API, developer portal, documentation, /.well-known/ discovery, or llms.txt to harvest.

providers.name: Crowdery
providers.description: Crowdery was a consumer retail and e-commerce startup backed by a16z, listed on the a16z investment list. Its product inverted the traditional retail sales model: shoppers voted on product designs from a curated set, Crowdery assembled a personalized marketplace from each shopper's top picks, and the highest-voted products were opened for pre-order at a discount. For brands it offered consumer feedback loops, pre-production demographic analytics, and pre-orders intended to de-risk manufacturing runs. The company never shipped a public API or developer program. As of July 2026 Crowdery appears defunct: the apex domain crowdery.com serves a Doteasy hosting placeholder page, www.crowdery.com still delegates to a decommissioned Heroku prelaunch application that returns 404, and no developer portal, documentation, GitHub organization, or API surface could be found. This profile is retained as a historical a16z portfolio record with no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Dangdang
providers.description: Dangdang (当当, dangdang.com) is a Chinese business-to-consumer e-commerce company founded in 1999 and headquartered in Beijing. It began as one of China's largest online booksellers and expanded into a broad general-merchandise marketplace spanning books, e-books and e-readers, digital reading, consumer electronics, apparel, home goods, and maternal and baby products. Once listed on the New York Stock Exchange (ticker DANG) before being taken private, Dangdang was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCM Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. No active public developer program, open platform, or machine-readable API surface was reachable during enrichment (the site is geo-restricted); this profile carries a probed domain-security posture and awaits any discoverable API artifacts.

providers.name: DealCart
providers.description: DealCart is a Pakistan-based social-commerce and group-buying startup offering discounted groceries and everyday household goods, surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company. As a consumer mobile-commerce business it publishes no public developer program. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-18 found the primary domain dealcart.io parked/expired (a Namecheap landing page) and dealcart.pk serving a password-gated Shopify storefront, with no developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or API surface to harvest. This profile carries a live domain-security probe and remains a lead pending any future public API program.

providers.name: DeporPrivé
providers.description: DeporPrivé is a Mexico-based sports e-commerce platform operating as a members-oriented "Sport Experience & Outlet" that runs flash sales and private, time-limited shopping events across more than 300 athletic brands including Adidas, Nike, and Salomon, with discounts reaching up to 70%. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in Mexico, the company curates footwear, apparel, and accessories for running, cycling, swimming, football, and general fitness, and has grown into one of the largest sport-specific online retailers in the country, fulfilling around 1,000 packages per day across multiple sales channels. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global. No public developer program, API, or documentation surface has been identified for this consumer retail brand.

providers.name: Diapers.com
providers.description: Diapers.com is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of accel and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: ecommerce. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Digby
providers.description: Digby was an Austin, Texas software-as-a-service provider of mobile commerce and mobile engagement solutions for large retailers, operating under parent company 30 Second Software Inc. Its platform — including the Localpoint location-based marketing product — delivered branded mobile web experiences and native shopping apps, connecting digital engagement to physical stores for customers such as Cabela's, Kohl's, Catalina Marketing and Hasbro. Digby raised venture funding from Battery Ventures, S3 Ventures, Daylight Ventures, Relay Ventures and the BlackBerry Partners Fund. The company was acquired by fellow Austin mobile company Phunware in May 2014 (along with its Movaya subsidiary in Seattle and Chengdu), terms undisclosed, and the Localpoint technology was folded into Phunware's product line. Digby no longer operates as an independent company: digby.com no longer resolves to a live site (last Internet Archive capture February 2015) and there is no current developer portal, documentation, API, SDK or other public API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Dingdong
providers.description: Dingdong (Dingdong Maicai / 叮咚买菜) is a Shanghai-based on-demand fresh-grocery e-commerce company operating a front-warehouse (dark-store) model that delivers fruit, vegetables, meat, seafood and prepared foods to consumers, typically within about 30 minutes, through its mobile app. The company is publicly listed on the New York Stock Exchange (ticker DDL) and is backed by Hongshan (formerly Sequoia Capital China). Its public surface (ddxq.mobi) is a consumer mobile-app backend rather than a developer platform; no public developer portal, API documentation, or open API program was found during enrichment, and the host is not reachable outside of China.

providers.name: Dingdong Maicai
providers.description: Dingdong Maicai (叮咚买菜), operated by Shanghai Yibai Mi Network Technology Co., Ltd., is a Chinese on-demand fresh grocery e-commerce and delivery platform. It runs a mobile-app marketplace for fresh produce, meat, seafood, prepared foods, and daily groceries, backed by a network of front-line neighborhood micro-fulfillment stations that enable fast, same-hour delivery in major Chinese cities. The company is publicly listed on the NYSE (ticker DDL) and was backed by SoftBank Vision Fund. It is a consumer-facing operation with no public developer program or open API surface; this profile is a network lead maintained by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: DMall
providers.description: DMall (多点数智, Dmall Inc.) is an Asia-Pacific retail digitalization service provider that pairs consulting with technology to deliver an all-in-one digital retail operating system for supermarkets, grocery chains, and other retailers. Its cloud-native SaaS platform (Dmall OS) spans supply chain, point-of-sale, store operations, membership, e-commerce, and O2O fulfillment, helping traditional retailers modernize into data-driven omnichannel businesses. The company is backed by IDG Capital among other investors. DMall does not currently publish a public developer portal, open-platform documentation, or machine-readable API specifications; this profile captures its public web identity and domain security posture while awaiting a documented API surface.

providers.name: Dollar Shave Club
providers.description: Dollar Shave Club is a direct-to-consumer men's grooming brand founded in 2011 and best known for its subscription razor and blade service that ships razors, blades, shave butter, and personal-care products to members on a recurring schedule. Acquired by Unilever in 2016 and later sold to Nexus Capital Management in 2023, the company sells online through its storefront at dollarshaveclub.com. Its e-commerce experience runs on Shopify; the storefront host exposes Shopify Customer Account OAuth2/OIDC discovery documents (including Shopify's customer-account-api and customer-account-mcp-api scopes) but Dollar Shave Club publishes no first-party public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation of its own. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub of a16z, Cowboy Ventures, Dragoneer, and Forerunner Ventures.

providers.name: Eaze
providers.description: Eaze is a California-based cannabis marketplace and delivery platform that connects licensed dispensaries and cannabis brands with adult consumers, offering online ordering and same-day delivery of flower, edibles, vapes, and related products across the state. Founded in 2014 and headquartered in San Francisco, Eaze operates a consumer marketplace plus a technology and logistics stack for compliant retail. Backed by 500 Global and DCM Ventures, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead. Eaze does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal; its api.eaze.com host is an internal, bot-protected surface.

providers.name: Ebates
providers.description: Ebates is a consumer cash-back and rebate shopping platform founded in 2000 in San Francisco that pays members a percentage of their purchases back as cash when they shop through its links at thousands of partner retailers. Rakuten acquired Ebates in 2014 and rebranded the U.S. service as Rakuten Rewards in 2019; the ebates.com domain now redirects to rakuten.com. The business is a consumer-facing rewards and affiliate-commerce brand and does not operate an independent public developer API program. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Edfa3ly
providers.description: Edfa3ly is an Egyptian cross-border e-commerce and online shopping platform that lets consumers in Egypt and the wider MENA region buy products from international retailers and marketplaces, then handles the international shipping, customs clearance, and local delivery on their behalf. It bridges shoppers to overseas stores by managing purchasing, logistics, and payment in local currency. Edfa3ly is a 500 Global (500 Startups) portfolio company. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; the company does not publish a public developer program or API at this time.

providers.name: Enjoy Technologies
providers.description: Enjoy Technology (Enjoy Technologies) was a "commerce at home" mobile-retail startup founded in 2014 by Ron Johnson, the former Apple senior vice president of retail and JCPenney CEO, and headquartered in Palo Alto, California. The company brought the retail store experience to customers' homes, dispatching mobile experts to deliver, set up, and demonstrate consumer electronics on behalf of partners such as carriers and device makers. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, Oak Investment Partners, and Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Enjoy went public via SPAC in 2021 and declared bankruptcy in 2022, with its assets subsequently acquired. Enjoy never operated a public developer program or API; this profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company record.

providers.name: Eve Com
providers.description: Eve.com was a dot-com era e-commerce retailer of prestige beauty and personal care products, founded in 1998 by Mariam Naficy and Varsha Rao. It raised venture funding from Lightspeed Venture Partners (1999) and reached a Series B before being acquired by Idealab in 2000, after which the business ceased independent operations. It is retained in the API Evangelist network only as a historical Lightspeed portfolio lead; it published no developer program, API, SDKs, or documentation. The eve.com domain is today operated by an unrelated entity (CCP Games / the EVE Online game universe) and is not a surface for this company, so no live API or developer artifacts can be harvested for it.

providers.name: Fanatics
providers.description: Fanatics is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of softbank-vision-fund, thrive-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: consumer. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: fanli
providers.description: fanli (返利网, fanli.com) is a Chinese cashback and shopping-rewards platform that aggregates promotions, coupons, and rebate offers across major online retailers, letting consumers earn money back on purchases they route through the site. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass, fanli.com is a live consumer-facing web property; no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable API definition, /.well-known discovery surface, llms.txt, or published security/vulnerability-disclosure program was found.

providers.name: Farfetch
providers.description: Farfetch is a global luxury fashion technology platform and online marketplace connecting consumers with boutiques, brands, and department stores across more than 190 countries, offering designer womenswear, menswear, kidswear, shoes, bags, and accessories. Beyond its consumer marketplace, Farfetch historically operated a B2B arm, Farfetch Platform Solutions (FPS), providing e-commerce, fulfilment, and logistics technology to luxury retailers; the group was acquired by Coupang in early 2024. No public developer portal or API documentation is currently reachable for the marketplace or the platform arm.

providers.name: Fashion, Inc. (Fab.com)
providers.description: Fashion, Inc. was the legal entity behind Fab.com, the design-focused e-commerce and flash-sale marketplace founded in 2010 by Jason Goldberg and Bradford Shellhammer after pivoting from the Fabulis social network. Fab raised roughly $150M across rounds led by Menlo Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz and Atomico, listed Battery Ventures among its backers, and passed ten million members by December 2012 before layoffs and a collapse in growth. PCH International acquired Fab's digital assets in March 2015; the site was later repositioned around health and fitness goods and went offline in December 2022. The company is defunct and operated no public developer program or API. The fab.com domain is today registered to Epic Games, Inc. and serves Epic's unrelated Fab digital-asset marketplace, so nothing currently published at that host belongs to this company.

providers.name: Fashionara
providers.description: Fashionara was an Indian premium online fashion retailer that launched in 2012 as a curated "e-fashion mall" selling ladies, men's and kids apparel, footwear and lifestyle goods. It ran a flash-sale "events" model on a Magento storefront, carried more than 200 international labels alongside Indian brands including Kenneth Cole, Calvin Klein, Fossil, Adidas, Benetton, Van Heusen, Allen Solly, Clarks and Arrow, and operated a quirky in-house sub-brand called F.lea Bazaar. It offered free shipping over Rs. 799, free returns, next-day delivery in eight Indian cities, a style-advisor booking service and an Android app (com.fnara.main). The company was backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners. Fashionara never published a public API, developer portal, SDK or OpenAPI definition — a scan of more than 8,000 archived fashionara.com URLs found no /api, /developer, /docs, /swagger, /oauth or /graphql paths, and no api/developer subdomain was ever archived. The storefront went dark in mid-2016 and the domain no longer resolves. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Flagship
providers.description: Flagship is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of index-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: retail. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: FlexEngage
providers.description: FlexEngage is a retail customer-engagement company that powered transactional and triggered customer communications for retailers and brands, including digital receipts, order and shipping notifications, and omnichannel messaging across email, SMS, and print. The company was backed by Bullpen Capital and was acquired by Narvar in 2019. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced from the Bullpen Capital portfolio; the public site (www.flexengage.com) is currently served behind CloudFront and returns HTTP 403 to automated clients, so no public developer/API surface could be captured during enrichment.

providers.name: Fossil Group
providers.description: Fossil Group is a global designer, marketer, and distributor of consumer fashion accessories including watches, jewelry, handbags, small leather goods, belts, and sunglasses sold under owned and licensed brands such as Fossil, Skagen, Michele, Relic, Misfit, and licensed lines for Michael Kors, Diesel, Emporio Armani, Tory Burch, and others.

providers.name: Foxtrot
providers.description: Foxtrot (Foxtrot Market, foxtrotco.com) is a Chicago-based retail chain of upscale convenience stores and cafes combining a neighborhood corner store with a coffee shop and a curated selection of local and specialty food, drink, and grocery goods, plus on-demand delivery and pickup. Surfaced as a portfolio company of d1-capital and added to the API Evangelist network. At the time of enrichment the public site (foxtrotco.com) is a minimal placeholder and the company exposes no public developer program, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications.

providers.name: Gemvara
providers.description: Gemvara was a Boston-based direct-to-consumer custom fine-jewelry e-commerce retailer, founded in 2006 by Matt Lauzon and Jason Reuben (Babson College), known for made-to-order jewelry customization software that let shoppers configure gemstones and metals on demand. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners among others, it was acquired by Richline Group (a Berkshire Hathaway company) in 2013 and shut down in February 2023. The company published no public developer API, and the gemvara.com domain no longer resolves to a live site. This profile is retained as a defunct-company record.

providers.name: General Growth Properties
providers.description: General Growth Properties (GGP) was a major U.S.-based commercial real estate company and the second-largest shopping mall operator in the United States before being acquired by Brookfield Property Partners in 2018. The GGP portfolio is now operated under Brookfield Properties. No public developer APIs are documented for the legacy GGP entity.

providers.name: Gentle Monster
providers.description: Gentle Monster is a South Korean luxury eyewear brand founded in 2011 and operated by parent company IICOMBINED, headquartered in Seoul. The brand designs and sells avant-garde sunglasses and optical frames, and is widely recognized for its immersive, art-installation flagship stores and experiential retail spaces. Its sister brands include Tamburins (fragrance and body care) and Nudake (conceptual dessert and patisserie). Gentle Monster sells globally through flagship stores, department-store concessions, and its direct-to-consumer site at gentlemonster.com. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; it is a consumer retail brand and publishes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Gilt
providers.description: Gilt (Gilt Groupe) is a members-only flash-sale e-commerce retailer offering limited-time sales on designer and luxury fashion, accessories, home goods, and travel at discounted prices. Founded in 2007, Gilt pioneered the flash-sale model in the United States, hosting time-boxed curated sales events for a member base. The company was acquired by Hudson's Bay Company in 2016 and later combined with Rue La La to form Rue Gilt Groupe. Gilt operates primarily as a consumer-facing web and mobile shopping experience; it does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: Gilt Groupe
providers.description: Gilt Groupe is a New York-based online retailer that pioneered the "flash sale" model in the United States, offering limited-time, members-only sales of discounted designer fashion, luxury goods, home items, and travel. Founded in 2007, Gilt was acquired by Hudson's Bay Company in 2016 and subsequently sold to Rue La La in 2018, forming Rue Gilt Groupe; the gilt.com storefront remains operational. Gilt's engineering team was an influential early adopter of Scala and microservices and open-sourced roughly fifty JVM libraries (the "gfc" Gilt Foundation Classes, Handlebars-Scala, sbt plugins) to Maven Central under the com.gilt groupId. Gilt operated no public REST API at the time of this enrichment pass - its historical developer.gilt.com API and the github.com/gilt organization are both retired. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Matrix Partners and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Givemetap
providers.description: GiveMeTap is a UK-based social-enterprise consumer brand that designs and sells reusable, BPA-free stainless-steel and insulated water bottles (500ml and 700ml, plus custom co-branded bottles for businesses). For every bottle sold, GiveMeTap funds five years of clean drinking water for a person in Ghana, giving 20% of its revenue to water projects in Africa; the company reports 116,391 people reached with clean water for life. It operates a direct-to-consumer e-commerce storefront on the Shopify platform. GiveMeTap is a physical-products company with no first-party developer API, developer portal, or public API documentation; it was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio lead and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub.

providers.name: gohoo
providers.description: gohoo was a boutique e-commerce company based in Hangzhou, China (founded circa 2001) that linked high-quality goods to supplier channels by integrating the factory supply chain to reduce brand premium. It raised a seed round in 2018 and a Series A in March 2019 with backing from Qiming Venture Partners and Bertelsmann Asia Investments. The company is no longer active (deadpooled), and its gohoo.com domain now redirects to an atom.com domain-for-sale landing page. No live company website, developer portal, documentation, or public API surface exists, so there is nothing to enrich beyond this honest identity record.

providers.name: Goodme
providers.description: Goodme (brand "Good me", Chinese: 古茗; legal entity Guming Holdings Limited) is one of China's largest freshly-made tea-beverage franchise chains, founded in 2010 by Wang Yun'an and headquartered in Hangzhou, Zhejiang. It sells fruit tea, milk tea, and coffee through a franchise model concentrated in China's lower-tier cities, and had grown to roughly 9,800 outlets nationwide by late 2024. The company listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (SEHK: 1364) in February 2025, raising about US$233 million. It is a consumer-sector portfolio company of HongShan and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile. As a food-and-beverage retail franchise, Goodme publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or agent-facing surface at this time.

providers.name: GoodsMart International
providers.description: GoodsMart is a Cairo-based premium grocery and household e-commerce delivery startup serving compounds across 6th of October, Sheikh Zayed, and New Cairo. Founded by Rami Fawzi and co-founders (soft-launched 2014, officially launched 2015), it pioneered contactless overnight grocery delivery in Egypt, dropping orders into a pre-installed GoodsMart box outside the customer's home between midnight and 6am. The company operates a consumer-facing mobile app and web storefront for groceries, personal care, and home-care products. It has raised roughly $4.37M from investors including 500 Global, Sawari Ventures, Algebra Ventures, and Savour Ventures. As of this profile, GoodsMart publishes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal; this remains a company/lead record in the API Evangelist network rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Goyaz Silver Jewellery
providers.description: Goyaz Silver Jewellery is a Hyderabad-based Indian jewellery retail brand founded in January 2023 by Priyanka Vemuluri, specializing in 92.5 premium and gold-plated silver jewellery that blends traditional Indian craftsmanship with contemporary, occasion-led design. Operating a chain of 18 retail stores across Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka (including Kukatpally, Punjagutta, Suchitra Circle, Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam), Goyaz positions gold-plated silver as an accessible luxury alternative to gold. In October 2025 the company raised a Rs 130 crore (~$14.6M) Series A round led by Norwest Venture Partners, its first institutional funding, to expand its retail footprint, strengthen design and manufacturing, and enhance its omnichannel experience. The company operates an online storefront and social commerce presence but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface. This profile entered the API Evangelist network as a Norwest Venture Partners portfolio lead.

providers.name: Grana
providers.description: Grana was a Hong Kong-based direct-to-consumer fashion brand founded in October 2014 by Luke Grana and Pieter-Paul Wittgen, selling premium wardrobe basics made from directly-sourced fabrics — Peruvian pima cotton, Chinese silk, Japanese denim, European linen, cashmere, merino and baby alpaca — online without retail middlemen. It raised roughly US$16M across seed and Series A rounds from investors including Alibaba's Hong Kong Entrepreneurs Fund, 500 Startups (now 500 Global), Golden Gate Ventures, MindWorks Ventures and the Bluebell Group. The company has since wound down; grana.com now resolves to a parked domain with no live storefront, developer program, or public API.

providers.name: Gymboree
providers.description: Gymboree is a children's apparel and accessories retailer selling clothing for babies, toddlers, and kids up to age 12 through its consumer e-commerce site at gymboree.com. The brand is owned and operated by The Children's Place, Inc. (headquartered at 500 Plaza Drive, Secaucus, NJ). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of norwest-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Gymboree publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine interface: its site is a purely consumer-facing retail storefront, so no API artifacts (OpenAPI, MCP, SDKs, webhooks) exist to harvest. This profile carries only the identity and infrastructure-security probe of the gymboree.com domain.

providers.name: haoyiku
providers.description: Haoyiku (好衣库) is a Chinese private-domain social e-commerce and brand flash-sale platform operated by Haoyiku (Hangzhou) Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd. and associated with Jingling Group, founded in December 2017. It equips millions of individual store owners with a one-click storefront, dropship supply chain, private-domain traffic tooling, operations training, and after-sales services, spanning apparel, footwear, bags, cosmetics, personal care, mother-and-baby, and daily-necessities categories across more than 15,000 brand partnerships. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners, Haoyiku is a consumer mobile-app business with no public developer platform or API program; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: HauteLook
providers.description: HauteLook was a members-only, flash-sale e-commerce destination for fashion, beauty, and home goods, founded in 2007 in Los Angeles. It was acquired by Nordstrom in 2011 and operated as a standalone flash-sale brand before being folded into Nordstrom Rack; www.hautelook.com now redirects to the Nordstrom Rack Flash storefront. The provider publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal, so no API artifacts could be enriched during the pipeline pass.

providers.name: hayneedle.com (formerly know as NetShops)
providers.description: Hayneedle (formerly NetShops) was an online retailer of home goods, furniture, and outdoor products, founded as NetShops in Omaha, Nebraska in 2002 and rebranded to Hayneedle.com in 2009. It grew into a large specialty e-commerce operator running hundreds of niche home-and-lifestyle storefronts, and was acquired by Jet.com in 2016 for roughly $90 million, becoming a Walmart subsidiary after Walmart bought Jet.com. The standalone brand was subsequently wound down and hayneedle.com now redirects into walmart.com. It was listed as an Insight Partners portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. Enrichment found no first-party public developer surface (no API docs, OpenAPI, SDKs, MCP server, or event surface); the only signal captured is honest DNS/TLS domain-security data for the still-resolving redirect domain.

providers.name: Heytea
providers.description: Heytea is a Chinese premium modern tea-beverage chain founded in 2012 in Jiangmen, Guangdong. It pioneered cheese-topped tea and fresh-fruit "new-style tea" and has grown to thousands of stores across mainland China and international markets including Singapore, the United Kingdom, Australia, Canada and the United States. Backed by investors including Hongshan (formerly Sequoia Capital China) and IDG Capital, Heytea runs its own mobile ordering app and retail loyalty program. As a consumer food-and-beverage retailer it publishes no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDKs; this profile is retained in the network as a company identity lead.

providers.name: Homary
providers.description: Homary is a direct-to-consumer home furnishings retailer that sells furniture, faucets, lighting, outdoor, kitchen, bath, storage and organization, decor and rugs sourced straight from manufacturers to shoppers' homes. The brand positions itself around "affordable luxury" home decor, operating an online storefront (homary.com) with category catalogs, deals, best sellers, a design service, and a business-to-business program. Homary was surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners. As a consumer e-commerce brand it exposes only internal storefront endpoints (/hm-api/, /chart-api/, disallowed in robots.txt) and publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation at this time.

providers.name: HopShop Inc.
providers.description: HopShop Inc. is a consumer AI fashion-discovery and creator-monetization platform, often described as "Shazam for Fashion." Shoppers upload or screenshot an outfit and HopShop's visual-search AI finds the exact item plus similar matches across 600+ brand partners, including Bloomingdale's, Nordstrom, Levi's, and Tommy Hilfiger. Creators and influencers build personalized shops, link the outfits they feature on Instagram to shoppable products, grow their communities, and earn affiliate commissions. The company is backed by 500 Global. As surfaced to the API Evangelist network, HopShop operates as a consumer-facing mobile and web application and publishes no public developer API, SDKs, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface at this time; this profile captures its identity and probed domain security.

providers.name: Hundeland
providers.description: Hundeland was a German direct-to-consumer online shop for dog supplies — dog food, treats, accessories, and pet-care products — and a portfolio company of the Point Nine venture capital firm. The hundeland.de storefront has been permanently closed ("dauerhaft geschlossen") and now 302-redirects to Pets Premium (petspremium.de), operated by the same company, which carries the same brands and product range; former customers must re-register there. Hundeland publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs, so the enrichment pipeline found no API surface to harvest. This record is retained as a Point Nine portfolio lead with the real closure status captured; the only machine-verifiable artifact is the domain-security probe of the still-resolving hundeland.de host that serves the redirect.

providers.name: Ihaveu
providers.description: Ihaveu (优众网, ihaveu.com) was a Chinese business-to-consumer luxury fashion e-commerce platform founded in 2010 by Sun Tongyu (a former president of Alibaba's Taobao) and Chen Xiao. Based in China, it sold curated high-end designer apparel and accessories from international couture brands such as Prada, Hermes, and Marc Jacobs to Chinese consumers. It raised a Series A of roughly $11M in December 2010 led by IDG Capital and Lightspeed Venture Partners, followed by a Series B in 2012 that added The CID Group and JAFCO Asia. The company is no longer active and its ihaveu.com domain is now parked and listed for sale, so it exposes no live website, developer portal, or public API. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an identity record for a defunct Lightspeed portfolio company; it has no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Inkbox
providers.description: Inkbox is a direct-to-consumer e-commerce company selling semi-permanent temporary tattoos. Its proprietary "For Now Ink" formula is made with Genipa plant extract and develops into the skin to last up to about two weeks, longer than surface-level temporary tattoos. Inkbox sells thousands of pre-designed tattoos from independent artists and offers a custom service where customers upload their own artwork to create personalized designs. The business operates as a consumer retail brand with an online store, and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: Invidica
providers.description: Invidica is an Oakland-based B2B wholesale ecommerce marketplace (founded 2019) that upgrades the wholesaler-retailer relationship for the reseller economy. It pairs a marketplace where resellers order wholesale products directly from brands with AI-driven analytics that combine Amazon sales data to predict an item's profitability, sales velocity, and competition, helping small sellers find the most profitable products to resell. Founded by CEO Sean Bovell and backed by 500 Global and 1517 Fund (pre-seed, 2021). The company appears to be pivoting under the Reroute Retail brand (rerouteretail.com, "launching soon"); its original invidica.com domain no longer resolves. No public API or developer surface is currently published.

providers.name: J.Crew Group
providers.description: J.Crew Group, Inc. is an American multi-brand specialty retailer offering women's, men's, and children's apparel, shoes, and accessories under the J.Crew, Madewell, and Crewcuts brands. The company operates retail stores, factory outlet stores, and direct-to-consumer e-commerce sites.

providers.name: JD Business
providers.description: JD Business is the enterprise-facing arm of JD.com (Jingdong), one of China's largest technology and retail companies, offering B2B procurement, supply-chain, and corporate purchasing services to businesses. JD.com operates across retail, logistics, technology, health, and industrials, and runs the JD Open Platform (JOS / "Zeus" Developer Center) at jos.jd.com, where third-party merchants and partners integrate with JD's e-commerce, order, product, and logistics systems. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-linked company and is being enriched from JD's public surface; JD's developer platform and enterprise services are primarily China-market and Chinese-language.

providers.name: Jet
providers.description: Jet.com was an American e-commerce company and online marketplace founded in 2014 by Marc Lore and headquartered in Hoboken, New Jersey. It offered a membership-style shopping model with dynamic, real-time pricing that lowered the total as shoppers added items to their cart. Walmart acquired Jet.com in 2016 for roughly USD 3.3 billion and folded its operations into Walmart's own e-commerce platform, discontinuing the Jet.com brand in 2020. The jet.com domain now redirects to walmart.com; Jet operates no public developer program, API, SDK, or documentation. This record is retained as a defunct portfolio lead for network completeness.

providers.name: Jet (Walmart)
providers.description: Jet (Walmart) was a US e-commerce marketplace founded by Marc Lore and backed by Bain Capital Ventures, acquired by Walmart in 2016 for roughly 3.3 billion USD and subsequently wound down. The jet.com domain now 302-redirects to walmart.com (confirmed 2026-07-19) and no standalone Jet developer portal, API, documentation, or SDK surface exists; the brand and its commerce technology were absorbed into Walmart. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. It is retained for lineage/graph purposes but has no live public API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Jet Com
providers.description: Jet.com was an American e-commerce marketplace founded in 2014 by Marc Lore that used dynamic, real-time pricing to lower cart totals as shoppers combined orders. Walmart acquired Jet.com in 2016 for approximately 3.3 billion dollars, folded its technology and talent into Walmart's online operation, and fully shut down the Jet.com brand and site in 2020. The jet.com domain now redirects to walmart.com, and no Jet-branded developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or API surface remain online.

providers.name: Jobedu
providers.description: Jobedu is a Jordanian pop-culture creative retail and merchandise brand known for Arabic-language streetwear, apparel, prints, and consumer goods, operating a direct-to-consumer e-commerce storefront hosted on Shopify. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass the jobedu.com storefront returns HTTP 404 (Shopify-hosted, DNS points to shops.myshopify.com) and no public API, developer portal, documentation, or /.well-known surface could be found, so no API artifacts were produced beyond a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: Jüsto
providers.description: Jüsto is a Mexican online-only supermarket founded in 2019 by Ricardo Weder, headquartered in Mexico City. It operates a direct-to-consumer grocery e-commerce and delivery model with no physical stores, sourcing produce and pantry goods directly from farmers, producers, and brands and fulfilling orders from micro-fulfillment dark stores. The company sells its catalog through web and mobile apps and has raised venture funding from investors including General Atlantic, SoftBank, Foundation Capital, and 500 Global. Jüsto has no public developer program or documented API surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: karmaloop
providers.description: karmaloop is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of insight-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: consumer. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Keychain
providers.description: Keychain is an AI-powered operating system and manufacturing network for the consumer packaged goods (CPG) industry. The platform connects brands, retailers, and private-label buyers with vetted contract manufacturers and co-manufacturers, helping teams discover production partners, source ingredients and packaging, benchmark supplier capabilities, and bring new products to market faster. Keychain aggregates data across the fragmented CPG supply chain into a searchable network so brands can find who makes what and manufacturers can surface available capacity. The company is headquartered in New York and is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners.

providers.name: L Brands
providers.description: L Brands was a Fortune 500 specialty retail holding company best known for Victoria's Secret, PINK, and Bath & Body Works. In 2021 the company split into two independent publicly traded companies, with Bath & Body Works, Inc. retaining the original NYSE listing and Victoria's Secret & Co. spun off as a standalone retailer. The L Brands brand is no longer in active use; this repository preserves the historical corporate record. No public developer API has been documented.

providers.name: Levi Strauss
providers.description: Levi Strauss & Co. is one of the world's largest brand-name apparel companies and a global leader in jeanswear, designing and marketing jeans, casual wear, and related accessories under the Levi's, Dockers, Signature, and Denizen brands. The company does not publish a public developer API program.

providers.name: LNKO
providers.description: LNKO is a Moroccan direct-to-consumer eyewear brand and e-commerce retailer selling prescription eyeglasses, sunglasses, and children's eyewear (LNKO KIDS) for men and women, plus accessories such as tote bags, pouches, hats, and eyeglass chains. It operates physical retail locations alongside an online storefront with two-day delivery across Morocco. LNKO is a consumer fashion/retail brand backed by 500 Global; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation, so it carries no API artifacts in the API Evangelist network at this time.

providers.name: lovecrafts
providers.description: LoveCrafts (LoveCrafts Group Limited) is a UK-based crafting commerce and community platform — "your home to shop, share and dream in crafts" — selling yarns and fibers, knitting, crochet, sewing, quilting and embroidery patterns, supplies, tools, kits and fabrics, alongside free and paid patterns, tutorials and inspiration content. It operates localized storefronts for North America, the UK, Germany, Australia and France on a Nuxt-based e-commerce stack. LoveCrafts was surfaced as a portfolio company of Balderton Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. It exposes no public developer portal or API surface; the only machine-discoverable public artifact is an RFC 9116 security.txt with a responsible- disclosure policy (no bug bounty programme).

providers.name: Luckin Coffee
providers.description: Luckin Coffee (瑞幸咖啡) is a Chinese multinational coffee company and coffeehouse chain headquartered in Xiamen, China. Founded in 2017, it runs a technology-driven, mobile-app-first retail model in which nearly all ordering, payment, and membership happen through its native app and mini-programs rather than at a counter. As of 31 March 2026 the company operated 33,596 stores globally. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Luckin Coffee publishes no public developer program, open platform, or API — its digital surface is a consumer ordering app, not a documented API product.

providers.name: Luckypai
providers.description: Luckypai (乐酷天 / LuckyPai Ltd) was a Chinese television home-shopping company founded around 2006-2007 that grew into a leading nationwide TV and online shopping network, selling home appliances, cosmetics, apparel, food, and digital devices. It raised roughly $25M from investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Intel Capital, and the LOTTE Group, and was acquired by Lotte Home Shopping in 2010 for approximately $160M. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of lightspeed-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. As an acquired, no-longer-operating consumer commerce business it has no public developer program, API, or independent web presence; the luckypai.com domain is parked and listed for sale.

providers.name: Lulus
providers.description: Lulus (Lulus Fashion Lounge Holdings) is a direct-to-consumer online fashion retailer offering women's apparel, dresses, shoes, and accessories, operating primarily through lulus.com and mobile apps. Surfaced as a portfolio company of IVP and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Lulus publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface: developer.lulus.com does not resolve and no /.well-known/ discovery documents are served. This profile therefore captures company identity plus a live domain-security posture probe rather than any API artifacts.

providers.name: Lyracollective
providers.description: Lyra Collective is a consumer-products holding company that owns and operates a portfolio of everyday care brands across skincare, feminine care, and family and pet products, including LOLA, EVER, QRX Labs, TriLASTIN, Nuvadermis, Natemia, Leash Boss, and Lusso Gear. It positions itself around "Exceptional Care, For Everyday Moments," emphasizing clean, quality essentials sold direct-to-consumer and through retail. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As a consumer-brands operator it publishes no public developer portal, API, or API documentation; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Madison-reed
providers.description: Madison Reed is a female-founded and female-led direct-to-consumer hair color company offering 8-Free permanent, demi-permanent, and root touch-up hair color crafted in Italy, sold as at-home kits and delivered as professional services at 95+ Hair Color Bar locations across the United States. The company blends e-commerce retail, subscription replenishment, and in-person salon booking. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and True Ventures. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface; this profile captures identity and probed domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Markato
providers.description: Markato (legally On Your Marks) is a brand builder and distributor for health, beauty, and wellness brands across Asia, positioning itself as a next-generation distribution disruptor. From bases in Hong Kong, Singapore, Taiwan, Malaysia, Thailand, and Australia, it helps high-potential brands enter, grow, and dominate the region's most competitive markets. Its capabilities span strategic channel development into top-tier offline and online retailers (Sephora, Watsons, Mannings, SaSa), e-commerce and social commerce operations across Shopee, TikTok, and Lazada, 360-degree marketing and brand building, and end-to-end local operations, logistics, product registration, and compliance. Markato is backed by a roughly US$4M seed round led by Lightspeed Venture Partners, with a team drawn from L'Oreal, P&G, McKinsey, and Lane Crawford. Markato is a services and distribution business and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Markhor
providers.description: Markhor is a direct-to-consumer commerce company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and Y Combinator and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Its site at markhor.com runs on Shopify and is currently offline, returning an HTTP 402 "Store unavailable" response. A July 2026 enrichment pass probed the domain and well-known paths and found no public API, developer platform, documentation, or SDK surface; only live DNS/TLS/HTTP domain-security signal was captured.

providers.name: MBX
providers.description: MBX (formerly Memebox) is a global, multi-brand beauty and personal care company founded in 2012 and part of Y Combinator's Winter 2014 batch. Headquartered in San Francisco with operations in Seoul, Shanghai, and Taipei, MBX uses data-driven consumer insights and Korean beauty innovation to build and scale a portfolio of cosmetics brands — including Kaja, I Dew Care, Pony Effect, I'm Meme, and Nooni — sold through retail partners such as Sephora and Ulta. The company has raised over $190M from investors including Cowboy Ventures, Y Combinator, Formation 8, Goodwater Capital, Johnson & Johnson, and Pear VC. MBX operates as a direct-to-consumer and wholesale CPG business; it does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Mensa Brands
providers.description: Mensa Brands (rebranded BRND.ME) is an India-based, technology-led house of brands founded in 2021 by Ananth Narayanan (former Myntra CEO), building and scaling digital-first consumer brands across fashion, beauty, personal care, home and FMCG. Backed by Accel, Tiger Global and Prosus Ventures, it reached unicorn status and operates a portfolio of acquired D2C brands. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of prosus-ventures; a public developer API surface was searched for and none was found — the company exposes a corporate/consumer web presence rather than a developer platform.

providers.name: Mensabrands
providers.description: Mensa Brands (now operating as BRND.ME) is a Bangalore, India based "house of brands" / digital-first brand aggregator founded in 2021 by Ananth Narayanan. Following the Thrasio model, it acquires, operates and scales digital-native consumer brands across fashion, beauty, personal care, home and general merchandise, selling through marketplaces such as Amazon, Flipkart and Myntra as well as direct-to-consumer channels. The company reached unicorn status in 2021 and is backed by investors including Norwest Venture Partners, Accel, Prosus Ventures, Tiger Global and Alpha Wave. Its original domain mensabrands.com now redirects to brndme.in. This is a consumer-brands operating company; enrichment found no public developer or API surface (no docs/developer/api subdomains, no /.well-known documents, no llms.txt) beyond the marketing site's WordPress CMS, so no API artifacts were produced.

providers.name: Meolaa
providers.description: Meolaa is an AI-first, digitally native FMCG company based in India, founded in 2023 by Ishita Sawant.
