It began as a curated e-commerce marketplace for clean, sustainable, direct-to-consumer brands across fashion, beauty, home, and baby care, and is expanding into building a portfolio of purpose-driven in-house microbrands (including HIRA) powered by a shared AI and data platform for cross-brand innovation, supply-chain resilience, and marketing. The company raised a $6M Pre-Series A round led by General Catalyst with Claypond Capital, Colossa Ventures, Turbostart Global, and Kunal Shah. Meolaa is a consumer company and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: MeUndies
providers.description: MeUndies is a direct-to-consumer apparel brand based in Los Angeles, selling underwear, loungewear, socks, and basics online through a subscription membership and one-time purchase model. It operates as an e-commerce retailer at meundies.com rather than a developer platform: an enrichment pass on 2026-07-20 probed the domain and found no public API surface (api.meundies.com and developer.meundies.com both return 404, and no /.well-known/, /llms.txt, or OpenAPI documents were discoverable). This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and carries the domain-security probe result; it will gain API artifacts only if MeUndies publishes a developer program.

providers.name: miim
providers.description: mi|im (pronounced "mime", for Movement Imaging | Intelligence Matters) develops proprietary machine-learning and computer-vision technology that turns movement into intelligence for retail. Its movement-imaging platform analyzes and optimizes how people flow through physical space, helping retailers improve customer experience, drive operational efficiency, and detect and respond to events. Surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital; no public API, developer portal, or documentation was found during enrichment (the miim.ai domain currently returns a parked WordPress error page).

providers.name: Miracle Miles
providers.description: Miracle Miles (Miracle Miles Group) is a consumer footwear e-commerce company backed by Hongshan (Sequoia China). It designs, manufactures, and sells affordable fashion footwear and accessories direct-to-consumer through a family of online brands, including DREAM PAIRS (launched 2009), Bruno Marc (men's footwear), Nortiv 8 (outdoor), and Dream Pairs Kids, selling primarily via its own storefronts and large online marketplaces. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface; this profile is maintained as a company/lead record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: mogujie
providers.description: Mogujie (蘑菇街), operated by Mogu Inc. (NYSE MOGU), is a Chinese online fashion and lifestyle social-commerce destination that pairs a shopping marketplace with live video streaming and influencer-led content across apparel, beauty, and accessories. The company was formed from the 2016 merger of Mogujie and Meilishuo, is headquartered in Hangzhou, China, and listed on the New York Stock Exchange in December 2018. Mogujie's historical third-party open platform (open.mogujie.com) has been retired and now redirects away, and no active public API developer surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Moncler
providers.description: Moncler S.p.A. is an Italian luxury fashion house best known for its high-end down jackets and technical outerwear, founded in 1952 in Monestier-de-Clermont, France and today headquartered in Milan, Italy. The Moncler Group operates the Moncler and Stone Island brands, sells globally through directly operated retail boutiques, department-store wholesale and a direct-to-consumer e-commerce storefront, and is listed on Borsa Italiana (MONC). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of idg-capital and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; probing found a consumer e-commerce storefront but no public developer API program.

providers.name: mucho
providers.description: Mucho (Mucho Indonesia) was an Indonesian social-commerce startup founded in 2018 and headquartered in South Jakarta, positioned as Indonesia's first social online shopping application and often described as an aspiring "Pinduoduo for Indonesia." Its mobile app let users buy together with friends to unlock group-buying discounts, cutting distribution layers by working directly with brand owners and pairing frictionless payment with logistics support. The company raised early / seed funding with participation from Qiming Venture Partners. Mucho has since shut down; its app is no longer distributed and the mucho.asia domain now resolves to a parked placeholder page with no product, API, or developer surface. This profile is retained as a defunct-company record surfaced through the Qiming portfolio graph.

providers.name: Muni
providers.description: Muni was a Latin American social-commerce and community group-buying platform founded in 2019 in Bogota, Colombia by Maria Echeverri Gomez, aiming to transform e-commerce across LATAM by letting community leaders aggregate neighborhood demand and buy everyday grocery and household items at prices up to 40 percent below competitors, with no added shipping or service fees. It raised a Series A from Lightspeed Venture Partners in 2021 and at its peak served over 15,000 communities across Colombia, Brazil, and Mexico. As of this enrichment pass the company's primary domain (munitienda.com) resolves to a parked GoDaddy lander with no active product, developer portal, or public API surface, so the profile remains a consumer-app portfolio lead with no discoverable API.

providers.name: Mybuys
providers.description: MyBuys was a San Mateo, California cross-channel retail personalization company founded in 2002 that delivered coordinated product recommendations and targeted offers across websites, email, and display advertising using a patented portfolio of real-time optimization algorithms and an Active Shopper Database. MyBuys merged with digital advertising firm Magnetic in 2015, and Magnetic sold the MyBuys merchandising/personalization business to Evergage in January 2018. The company is defunct as an independent entity; the mybuys.com domain resolves but serves no live product, and there is no developer portal, documentation, or public API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Myntra
providers.description: Myntra is one of India's largest fashion and lifestyle e-commerce platforms, offering apparel, footwear, accessories, and beauty products across its own and third-party brands. Founded in 2007 and headquartered in Bengaluru, Myntra was acquired by Flipkart (Walmart) in 2014 and operates a consumer marketplace at myntra.com. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Myntra does not publish a public developer API program; its developer/API hosts resolve behind Akamai but are not openly documented.

providers.name: MYSALE GROUP PLC
providers.description: MySale Group PLC is a former AIM-listed online retailer that operated flash-sale and outlet e-commerce marketplaces across Australia, New Zealand and Southeast Asia under brands including MySale, OzSale, BuyInvite and Cocosa. The group was delisted and its corporate operations wound down; the surviving consumer brand, OzSale (ozsale.com.au), now runs as a Shopify-hosted storefront. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public developer program, API, SDK, or webhook surface: the corporate domain mysalegroup.com no longer resolves and the remaining brand sites are consumer retail storefronts only. This record is retained as a portfolio-lead profile surfaced from the Insight Partners portfolio; it has no API artifacts to catalog.

providers.name: Na Kd
providers.description: Na Kd (NA-KD) is a Swedish online fashion retailer for women, selling clothing, shoes, and accessories direct-to-consumer through na-kd.com. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead, backed by Northzone and Partech. As of this enrichment pass NA-KD publishes no public developer API, SDK, MCP server, or /.well-known discovery surface; this profile captures the company identity and its live domain-security posture.

providers.name: Nexite
providers.description: Nexite is a retail technology company (website nexite.io) surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures. It operates in the connected-retail / IoT-for-physical-retail space. This profile was added as a stub lead and has been through one local enrichment pass: the public web presence is live but fully gated behind a bot / CAPTCHA challenge, and no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or discovery (/.well-known/) surface could be reached. No public API surface is catalogued at this time; the entry is retained as a company record pending a discoverable API.

providers.name: Onera (acquired by Lyniate in 2021)
providers.description: Onera, Inc. was a San Francisco-based retail technology company that built a real-time inventory availability and omnichannel order fulfillment platform. Its "Onera Decision Engine" connected inventory events across siloed retail systems into a single real-time source of inventory truth and used machine learning to determine optimal fulfillment locations for orders, serving retailers such as Gap, Old Navy, Torrid, rue21, and Zumiez. Founded circa 2014 and backed by Bain Capital Ventures and Founder's Collective, Onera was acquired by supply-chain planning and optimization vendor ToolsGroup in June 2022, where its real-time inventory and fulfillment capabilities were folded into the ToolsGroup retail platform. NOTE: the "acquired by Lyniate in 2021" in this record's slug/name is incorrect harvested metadata; the verified acquirer is ToolsGroup (2022). The company no longer operates a standalone public developer portal or API surface.

providers.name: Outfittery
providers.description: Outfittery is a European personal-shopping and personalized-fashion e-commerce service that curates and ships tailored outfits to customers based on a style questionnaire and human stylist recommendations. Headquartered in Berlin, Germany, it operates across the UK, Spain, France, Germany, Switzerland, Austria, Belgium, the Netherlands and Sweden. Surfaced as a portfolio company of HV Capital and Northzone and added to the API Evangelist network. An enrichment probe found a consumer web/e-commerce presence with no public developer portal, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: PatPat
providers.description: PatPat is a direct-to-consumer children's and family apparel retailer founded in 2014 by Albert Wang and Ken Gao, selling baby, toddler, and kids' clothing along with matching family outfits, shoes, women's clothing, bags, and accessories to consumers in more than 100 countries and regions. Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund 2, PatPat operates as an online marketplace and mobile-first shopping app, and is one of the largest direct-to-consumer players in the children's apparel segment. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of SoftBank Vision Fund and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; PatPat does not currently publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Pawdly
providers.description: Pawdly (포들리) is a South Korean pet e-commerce marketplace and mobile app operated by KCC I&C, offering pet product shopping across categories, saved/wishlist items, and pet-care service reservations, alongside pet-care tips and member benefits delivered through its app. KCC I&C operates as a payment intermediary and mail-order sales broker rather than the direct seller, with individual merchants fulfilling orders, shipping, and refunds. Pawdly was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. An enrichment pass found a consumer web/mobile marketplace with no public developer portal, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Pepperfry
providers.description: Pepperfry is an Indian online marketplace for furniture and home products, founded in 2011 and headquartered in Mumbai. It sells furniture, decor, lamps, kitchen and dining goods, furnishings, and modular home solutions to consumers across India through its website, mobile apps, and a network of physical studio showrooms. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-20 found no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/GraphQL specification, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface: the consumer site is fully bot-protected (HTTP 403) and there is no evidence of an externally documented API program. The one artifact captured is a live domain-security probe of pepperfry.com.

providers.name: Phia
providers.description: Phia is a personal shopping assistant that helps consumers build their closet and find the best prices instantly across the web. Co-founded by Phoebe Gates and Sophia Kianni, the product spans a mobile app and a browser extension that compares prices for a given item across new and resale marketplaces, tracking more than 700 fashion, beauty, and lifestyle brands. The public phia.com site is a consumer storefront (a brand directory plus editorial style edits) and exposes no developer API, documentation, or programmatic surface. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of GGV Capital and enriched from live probes of the public site.

providers.name: Philz Coffee
providers.description: Philz Coffee is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of cowboy-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: consumer. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Pinduoduo
providers.description: Pinduoduo is a China-focused social commerce and agriculture-first e-commerce marketplace operated by PDD Holdings (Nasdaq: PDD), the multinational commerce group that also runs the cross-border marketplace Temu. Pinduoduo pioneered the "team purchase" (group-buy) model, connecting hundreds of millions of consumers directly with farmers, manufacturers, and merchants at scale. For developers, Pinduoduo runs a merchant-facing Open Platform (open.pinduoduo.com) that exposes gateway-style APIs for goods, orders, logistics, promotions, and store management to ISVs and merchant tools; that platform is geo-restricted to mainland China and was not directly reachable for artifact capture in this pass. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Hongshan (formerly Sequoia Capital China) and enriched with verifiable corporate identity and domain security posture.

providers.name: Pointy
providers.description: Pointy was an Irish retail-technology startup (pointy.com), founded by Mark Cummins and Charles Bibby and backed by Seedcamp, that helped independent brick-and-mortar retailers put their in-store inventory online by connecting a simple barcode-scanning device or point-of-sale integration to a searchable online product page. Google acquired Pointy in 2020 and has since fully folded the product into Google's own tooling: pointy.com now redirects to Google Business Profile support, and the former Pointy app is now Google's Local Inventory app, which syncs in-store products to Google Search and Maps via POS systems such as Clover, Square, and Lightspeed. Pointy no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no standalone public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this API Evangelist profile is retained as a portfolio-lead record and historical marker rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Pomelo fashion
providers.description: Pomelo Fashion is an omnichannel fashion retailer headquartered in Bangkok, Thailand, selling women's apparel and accessories across Southeast Asia through its website and mobile app. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a consumer e-commerce storefront (pomelofashion.com, served via CloudFront) but exposes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, or /.well-known discovery surface (all probed paths returned HTTP 405). This profile therefore carries only probed domain-security signal; it remains a lead for revisiting should a developer program launch.

providers.name: Pop Mart
providers.description: Pop Mart International Group is a Chinese pop-culture and designer-toy company best known for its blind-box collectibles and character IP such as Labubu (The Monsters), Molly, Skullpanda and Dimoo. Headquartered in Beijing and listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, it operates retail stores, robot-shop vending machines, and a consumer e-commerce presence across China and international markets. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Hongshan (HongShan/Sequoia China). Consumer sector; no public developer API surface was found during enrichment (no developer portal, /.well-known documents, or llms.txt).

providers.name: Privalia
providers.description: Privalia is a members-only online outlet and flash-sales retailer offering time-limited private sales on fashion, footwear, accessories, sportswear, and home goods from major brands at discounts of up to 70 percent. Operating consumer storefronts across Spain, Italy, Mexico, and Brazil (es/it/mex/br.privalia.com), Privalia is part of the Veepee (vente-privee) group and was an early Insight Partners portfolio company. It runs as a business-to-consumer e-commerce brand and publishes no public developer or API program.

providers.name: Prodigy Software
providers.description: Prodigy Software was a San Francisco-based provider of cloud-based automotive retail software, offering a SaaS digital-retailing platform that let car dealerships move the sales process online (web-store services, deal structuring, and financing workflows). Founded in 2015 by Marty Hu and Michia Rohrssen, it raised seed funding from Battery Ventures, SV Angel, 8VC, and CrunchFund, and was acquired by Upstart Holdings in March 2021. The company no longer operates independently and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs; its former domain is parked.

providers.name: Quince
providers.description: Quince is a direct-to-consumer e-commerce retailer selling high-quality essentials at radical prices across apparel, home goods, bedding, furniture, accessories, jewelry, beauty, and travel. It uses a factory-direct model that bypasses traditional retail markups to offer affordable luxury. Quince was surfaced as a portfolio company of 8vc, GGV Capital, ICONIQ Capital, and Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As a consumer retail brand it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or .well-known discovery surface; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Ralph Lauren Corporation
providers.description: Ralph Lauren Corporation (NYSE: RL) is a global premium-lifestyle company founded by Ralph Lauren in 1967 and headquartered in New York City. The company designs, markets, and distributes apparel, accessories, home, and fragrances across a portfolio of brands including Polo Ralph Lauren, Ralph Lauren Collection, Ralph Lauren Purple Label, Double RL (RRL), Lauren Ralph Lauren, and Chaps, along with Polo Golf, RLX, Pink Pony, Ralph Lauren Home and Paint, Ralph Lauren Watches and Fine Jewelry, and Ralph Lauren Restaurants. Direct-to-consumer commerce runs on Adobe Commerce, and category-extension brands are operated through licensing partners (eyewear via Luxottica, fragrances via L'Oréal). The corporation operates retail stores in dozens of countries with no publicly documented developer APIs, partner program portal, affiliate API, or open OpenAPI/Postman/GraphQL surface as of the profiling date.

providers.name: Rasyonet
providers.description: Rasyonet is a Turkish fintech company providing integrated financial software solutions and capital markets data platforms for institutional clients, asset managers, and financial analysts. Founded in 2000 and headquartered at ITU ARI Teknopark in Istanbul, Rasyonet offers tools for analyzing global equity markets, economic indicators, mutual and pension funds, fixed-income securities, portfolio analytics, and automated financial reporting. Their flagship EquityRT platform delivers equity research, company valuation, and peer benchmarking capabilities via desktop and Excel integration. No public developer API or machine-readable specification has been documented at this time.

providers.name: Raw Apothecary
providers.description: Raw Apothecary is a Mexico-based consumer brand that operated a Shopify storefront at rawapothecary.mx (Spanish-language, powered-by Shopify), surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the storefront returns "Tienda no disponible" (HTTP 402, "Store Unavailable"), and the company publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, or machine-readable specification surface. This profile is retained as a company record; there is no API to enrich beyond a live domain-security probe of the storefront host.

providers.name: Retailigence
providers.description: Retailigence is a retail technology company that applies artificial intelligence and machine learning to category management and store operations. Its ML Engine powers an AI suite for assortment optimisation, space modelling, store clustering, customer segmentation, and an X-Ray control-tower hub (web and mobile) that tracks and helps remove in-store operational issues. The platform is delivered as a proof-of-concept engagement rather than a public self-serve developer API. Retailigence was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: RetailMeNot *
providers.description: RetailMeNot is a consumer savings destination that aggregates coupons, promo codes, cash-back offers, and deals from thousands of retailers and brands, helping shoppers in the United States save money when they buy online and in-store. It operates a website, mobile apps, and browser extensions that surface verified discount codes and cash-back at checkout, and it monetizes through retailer affiliate relationships rather than a self-serve developer platform. As of this profile RetailMeNot publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface; probing found no reachable developer portal or well-known discovery documents, and partner activity is handled through whitelabel affiliate infrastructure.

providers.name: Rothys
providers.description: Rothy's is a San Francisco-based direct-to-consumer footwear and accessories brand founded in 2012, known for washable shoes and bags 3D-knitted from recycled materials such as post-consumer plastic water bottles and marine plastics. Its catalog spans flats, loafers, sneakers, Mary Janes, clogs, sandals, heels, and boots for women, men, and kids, alongside totes, crossbody bags, wallets, and backpacks. The company ships to 40+ countries and emphasizes sustainable, seamless-knit manufacturing that reduces waste. Rothy's was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As a consumer retail brand it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface; this profile captures its identity and web presence for the catalog.

providers.name: Saks Global (fka Saks Fifth Avenue)
providers.description: Saks Global (fka Saks Fifth Avenue) is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of insight-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Saks OFF 5TH
providers.description: Saks OFF 5TH is an American off-price retailer of designer and luxury fashion, footwear, accessories, and home goods, historically operated as the discount banner of Saks Fifth Avenue and later folded into Saks Global (Hudson's Bay Company / HBC). It sold marked-down designer merchandise through outlet stores and an e-commerce site at saksoff5th.com. As of this enrichment pass the public website resolves to a shutdown notice with only a store-locations link, and the company publishes no developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface. It was surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub of Insight Partners in the consumer sector.

providers.name: Sampler
providers.description: Sampler (The Sampler App Inc., Toronto) was a digital product-sampling platform used by consumer packaged goods (CPG) and retail brands to run targeted sample-distribution campaigns, collect first-party consumer data and reviews, and measure the impact of sampling on purchase behavior. Founded in 2013, it acquired Abeo and AdMass in 2023 and served brands including Procter & Gamble, Unilever, L'Oreal, Nestle and PepsiCo. THE COMPANY IS DEFUNCT: it filed for bankruptcy on 2024-06-27 with CAD 12.9M in liabilities against roughly CAD 300K in assets, and ceased operations. As of 2026-08-12 the entire estate is decommissioned — sampler.io and www.sampler.io fail the TLS handshake outright, api.sampler.io retains stale DNS records whose hosts refuse all connections, and every documentation or developer subdomain is NXDOMAIN. Sampler never published a public developer API, developer portal, documentation host, OpenAPI, or machine discovery surface; the api.sampler.io/v1/ endpoints visible in archived crawls were the private backend of its consumer claim widget and admin console, not a documented developer product.

providers.name: Saturnbird Coffee
providers.description: Saturnbird Coffee (三顿半) is a Chinese specialty coffee company known for premium instant coffee made with its proprietary REPUS extraction technology (cold extraction plus intelligent drying) using 100% Arabica beans. Its numbered Number Series and Express Series products, a Red Dot Design Award winner and Specialty Coffee Association member, are sold direct-to-consumer online and through collaborations with roasters including April Coffee, Kurasu, Monogram Coffee, and Fritz Coffee Company. Backed by Hongshan (HSG), it was surfaced as a portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. It is a consumer packaged-goods e-commerce brand with no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Sears Hometown and Outlet Stores
providers.description: Sears Hometown and Outlet Stores, Inc. (NASDAQ: SHOS) was a national retailer of home appliances, lawn and garden equipment, tools and hardware, spun off from Sears Holdings in October 2012 and operating two segments: Sears Hometown and Hardware, a largely franchised network of smaller-format stores in rural and suburban markets, and Sears Outlet, which sold new, one-of-a-kind, out-of-carton, discontinued, obsolete, used, reconditioned, overstocked and scratch-and-dent merchandise. The company was acquired by Transform Holdco (Transformco) and ESL Investments in October 2019, at which point the Sears Outlet business was sold on to Franchise Group and rebranded American Freight. Sears Hometown filed for Chapter 11 in December 2022 and converted to a Chapter 7 liquidation in February 2023. The company is defunct: it never operated a public developer program, and its corporate domain shos.com is now a parked registrar page serving a wildcard *.hostgator.com certificate and a 404, so there is no API surface, documentation, or /.well-known/ document left to profile.

providers.name: Serena & Lily
providers.description: Serena & Lily is a home furnishings and design brand founded in 2003 and based in Sausalito, California, known for its coastal-inspired furniture, bedding, rugs, wallpaper, lighting, and home decor sold through its e-commerce site and a network of design shops. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As a direct-to-consumer retail and interior-design brand, Serena & Lily publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface at the time of this enrichment pass; this profile captures its identity and domain security posture only.

providers.name: Shelf Engine
providers.description: Shelf Engine was a Seattle-based technology company that used machine learning and AI-driven demand forecasting to help grocery retailers reduce food waste and optimize ordering of perishable and fresh food items. It offered a guaranteed-order model where its forecasting engine predicted demand and absorbed the risk of unsold inventory. Shelf Engine was acquired by / merged into Crisp (gocrisp.com), the retail data platform, and its independent brand is now defunct: shelfengine.com 301-redirects to gocrisp.com. No independent public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface is published under the Shelf Engine brand.

providers.name: ShoeDazzle
providers.description: ShoeDazzle is a California-based online fashion subscription retailer offering curated shoes, handbags, and accessories through a VIP membership model. Founded in March 2009 (early backers included Andreessen Horowitz and Lightspeed Venture Partners), it was acquired by JustFab in August 2013 and is now operated as a brand of TechStyle Fashion Group alongside Fabletics, JustFab, FabKids, and Savage X Fenty. ShoeDazzle is a direct-to-consumer e-commerce brand; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API documentation.

providers.name: Shoppr
providers.description: Shoppr was a Malaysia-based consumer fashion-discovery mobile app (launched May 2015, often described as the "Tinder of fashion") that let shoppers swipe through personalized clothing recommendations. The founding team, led by Kendrick Wong, subsequently pivoted the business into Omnilytics, a B2B fashion retail market-intelligence and analytics platform serving brands and retailers. As of this enrichment pass the associated domain omnilytics.co is a parked domain (nameservers lander.d.parity.domains) and neither Shoppr nor Omnilytics exposes any public developer API, documentation, SDK, or developer portal. This entry originated as a 500 Global portfolio lead and is retained for record; it has no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Skims
providers.description: SKIMS is an American shapewear, loungewear, and apparel brand co-founded in 2019 by Kim Kardashian with Jens and Emma Grede, headquartered in Los Angeles. It sells solutionwear, underwear, loungewear, swim, and ready-to-wear direct-to-consumer through skims.com and via wholesale partners, and is the official underwear partner of the NBA, WNBA, and USA Basketball. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Thrive Capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile. This consumer retail brand publishes no public developer API surface; the profile carries a live domain-security probe of its web infrastructure.

providers.name: Skinseoul Lab
providers.description: Skinseoul Lab operates skin-seoul.com, a direct-to-consumer Korean beauty (K-beauty) e-commerce brand selling skincare and cosmetics to international customers, backed by 500 Global. Its public presence is a Next.js storefront fronted by Cloudflare with an Express commerce backend; enrichment probing (2026-07-21) found no public developer API, documentation, developer portal, or /.well-known/ discovery surface. The api.skin-seoul.com host returns only a plaintext "OK" health response, indicating an internal storefront backend rather than a documented public API.

providers.name: Smilobaby
providers.description: Smilo (Smilobaby) is a direct-to-consumer baby and toddler products brand founded in 2016 and based in Boston, backed by Norwest Venture Partners. Products are developed by doctors, scientists and engineers and sold direct via smilobaby.com, spanning bottle feeding, pacifiers and teethers, pregnancy and nursing, nursery, mealtime and bath. Its hero products are a pediatric-dentist-designed pacifier that supports a baby's developing palate and a patented-nipple bottle with an extra-sensitive vent that simulates breastfeeding. This is a consumer e-commerce retail brand: it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI, so the enrichment pass records identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: SnapDeal
providers.description: Snapdeal is an Indian e-commerce marketplace founded in February 2010 by Kunal Bahl and Rohit Bansal and headquartered in Gurugram/New Delhi. It began as a daily-deals platform and grew into a value-focused online marketplace that connects third-party sellers with buyers across categories such as fashion, home and kitchen, electronics accessories, and general merchandise, primarily serving price-sensitive shoppers in India's smaller cities and towns. Sellers onboard and manage catalog, orders, and payouts through the Snapdeal seller portal (seller.snapdeal.com). Snapdeal has been backed by investors including SoftBank, Bessemer Venture Partners, Nexus Venture Partners, and Kalaari Capital. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners; enrichment found no public developer portal, no api.snapdeal.com or developer.snapdeal.com host, and no published API specification or well-known discovery surface — the seller portal is login-gated behind SSO.

providers.name: Socialee
providers.description: Socialee is a beauty shopping platform that blends social media with e-commerce, letting shoppers discover and buy products through shoppable videos, write reviews, and earn rewards as creators. Its catalog spans makeup, skincare, fragrance, haircare, and bath & body, with next-day delivery and 7-day returns. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; an enrichment pass on 2026-07-21 found no public API, developer portal, or .well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: Soldsie
providers.description: Soldsie was a social-commerce platform founded in 2012 in San Francisco by Chris Bennett and Arrel Gray that let retailers sell directly through social media: customers bought products by commenting "Sold" on a merchant's Facebook or Instagram post, while a backend dashboard handled invoicing, customer tracking, and waitlists. Backed by 500 Startups (now 500 Global) and e.ventures, it raised roughly $1M in seed funding and a $4M Series A (2014), and had processed over $25M in transactions across more than 1,000 merchants. The product is now defunct: the soldsie.com apex no longer resolves and www.soldsie.com returns a broken redirect, so there is no live developer portal, API, or documentation surface to enrich.

providers.name: Sole Society
providers.description: Sole Society is a women's footwear, handbags, jewelry, and accessories e-commerce brand, surfaced as a portfolio company of insight-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the standalone brand no longer operates its own storefront. The domain solesociety.com resolves to MarkMonitor-managed nameservers, its HTTPS endpoints do not respond, and http://solesociety.com redirects (HTTP 200) to https://www.dsw.com/, so the domain appears to have been folded into DSW / Designer Brands. No public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, MCP server, or other machine-readable API surface was found for this brand. This profile remains a lead-stage company record with no API artifacts.

providers.name: Spoke
providers.description: SPOKE (spoke-london.com) is a London-based direct-to-consumer men's fashion retailer specializing in tailored menswear engineered for precise fit, with the tagline "A flawless fit, delivered." Its range spans trousers, denim, shirts, knitwear, shorts, tailoring (suits and jackets) and accessories, sold through an e-commerce storefront with a "Fit Finder" sizing tool. Backed by Seedcamp and tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company. An enrichment pass found no public developer program, API, or developer documentation; the company operates a standard retail e-commerce storefront only.

providers.name: StackSocial
providers.description: StackSocial is a consumer e-commerce and daily-deals marketplace operated by StackCommerce, selling software, online courses, gadgets, and digital goods at discounted prices. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. The public surface is a bot-protected single-page storefront; enrichment probes found no publicly documented API, OpenAPI specification, SDK packages, MCP server, well-known metadata, or llms.txt on the stacksocial.com host as of this pass.

providers.name: Stailer
providers.description: Stailer (ステイラー) is a retail-commerce platform built by 10X, Inc. (株式会社10X) that lets Japanese supermarket, drugstore, and other retail chains vertically launch and operate their own branded e-commerce and online-grocery services. It provides the consumer storefront apps, order management, in-store picking and fulfillment, and delivery operations that let established brick-and-mortar retailers stand up online shopping quickly. Stailer is a B2B SaaS offering sold through direct enterprise engagement; as of this enrichment pass it exposes no public developer API, documentation portal, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: StalkBuyLove
providers.description: StalkBuyLove was an India-based online women's fashion e-commerce retailer, surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the brand appears defunct as an independent property, since the stalkbuylove.com domain now returns a 301 permanent redirect to styched.in (Styched, an unrelated Shopify-powered Indian youth-fashion retailer). No public developer portal, API, SDK, MCP server, changelog, or other machine-readable API surface could be found for StalkBuyLove on any registry or well-known path. The only honest signal available is the domain, DNS, and TLS security posture of the redirecting host, captured in the domain-security artifact.

providers.name: Studio Moderna
providers.description: Studio Moderna is one of the largest multichannel direct-to-consumer retailers across Central and Eastern Europe, the Middle East, and beyond, founded in 1992 and headquartered in Emmen, Switzerland, with major operations based in Ljubljana, Slovenia. The company reaches consumers through TV direct-response (Top Shop), e-commerce, print catalogs, call centers, and physical retail stores in roughly twenty countries. Its portfolio of house brands spans sleep and home (Dormeo), kitchenware (Delimano), footwear and wellness (Walkmaxx), and health and lifestyle products (Kosmodisk, Rovus, WellNeo). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; the company exposes no public developer or API surface at this time.

providers.name: StyleSage
providers.description: StyleSage was a fashion and retail market-intelligence startup (Techstars-backed) that applied computer vision and data science to track apparel pricing, assortment, discounting, and trend signals across e-commerce retailers. The stylesage.co domain now redirects to Centric Software, which acquired the product and folded it into its Centric Market Intelligence platform for fashion, footwear, home, and beauty brands. As of this enrichment pass no standalone public developer API, documentation, SDK, or well-known surface is published for StyleSage.

providers.name: StyleSaint
providers.description: StyleSaint is a Los Angeles-based direct-to-consumer luxury women's fashion brand, originally an a16z-backed social-commerce startup and now an independent e-commerce label selling silk, lace, and other luxury-fabric apparel that is handmade in LA, ethically made, and sustainably sourced. The storefront runs on Shopify. As of this enrichment pass StyleSaint publishes no public developer program, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or agent-facing surface of its own; it is catalogued here as an a16z portfolio company. Any programmable commerce capability would be provided by the underlying Shopify platform rather than by a first-party StyleSaint API.

providers.name: Styleup
providers.description: StyleUp was a Y Combinator (Winter 2013) fashion advisory startup that delivered personalized daily outfit recommendations tailored to the user's local weather and individual style preferences, learning from feedback to improve suggestions over time. It operated as a consumer styling service out of the San Francisco Bay Area rather than as an API or developer platform. The company is now defunct and no longer operates: its former domain (thestyleup.com) has been repurposed by an unrelated third party and serves a Turkish sports-streaming site, so there is no live product, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or API surface remaining to enrich. This profile is retained as a historical stub with no active API artifacts.

providers.name: SuperValu
providers.description: SuperValu was one of the largest grocery retail and wholesale distribution companies in the United States before being acquired by United Natural Foods (UNFI) in 2018 for $2.9 billion. SuperValu operated retail grocery stores under multiple banners and provided wholesale distribution services. The supervalu.com domain now redirects to UNFI's wholesale food distribution platform. Suppliers interact with UNFI/SuperValu distribution through EDI (Electronic Data Interchange) and the myUNFI supplier portal.

providers.name: Sweetgreen
providers.description: Sweetgreen is a fast-casual restaurant company (NYSE: SG) building healthy, plant-forward food through a network of company-owned locations and its digital ordering platform. It reaches customers primarily via its consumer website and mobile app for pickup, delivery, and its Sweetgreen Rewards loyalty program, and operates automated "Infinite Kitchen" locations. As of this enrichment pass, Sweetgreen publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specifications; this profile captures its public web presence and probed domain-security posture only. Backed by D1 Capital and True Ventures.

providers.name: Syrup
providers.description: Syrup (Syrup Tech) is an AI-powered inventory optimization and demand-forecasting platform for retail and apparel brands. Its machine-learning decision-support engine combines transactional, marketing, and inventory data with external signals such as social trends and weather to recommend how brands produce, buy, and allocate inventory across omnichannel commerce, reducing stockouts and overproduction. Founded in 2021 by James Theuerkauf and Ferdinand Stockmann, Syrup raised a $17.5M Series A led by Accel and was acquired by Anaplan in September 2025; syrup.tech now redirects to anaplan.com. Syrup exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: The Inside
providers.description: The Inside is a direct-to-consumer, made-to-order home furnishings brand founded in 2017 by Christiane Lemieux and Britt Bunn, offering customizable upholstered furniture — sofas, chairs, beds, headboards, and decor — in 100+ fabrics and patterns. Backed by Canaan Partners along with Corigin Ventures, Lerer Hippeau, Forerunner Ventures, and BAM Ventures, it was acquired by Havenly in February 2022. Surfaced as a VC-portfolio lead in the API Evangelist network; during enrichment no public developer API, OpenAPI, or well-known metadata surface was found — theinside.com serves an e-commerce storefront with no documented programmatic interface.

providers.name: The RealReal
providers.description: The RealReal is the world's largest online marketplace for authenticated, resale luxury goods, operating a managed consignment marketplace across women's and men's fashion, fine jewelry and watches, handbags, fine art, and home. Founded in 2011 and headquartered in San Francisco, the company employs in-house gemologists, horologists, art curators, and brand authenticators to verify every item, pairing that expertise with data-driven pricing and demand insights. The RealReal is a publicly traded company (NASDAQ: REAL) and has processed tens of millions of consigned items. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass The RealReal publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Theres Camping
providers.description: Theres (데얼스, Theres Co., Ltd.) is a South Korean e-commerce marketplace for outdoor and camping gear, where customers buy both new and second-hand equipment in one place. The platform aggregates brands and vendors (Grape Box, Camping Khan, Ridge Mountain Gear, Matador, and others), offering product search, a shopping cart, deal notifications, a community section, and vendor/product listing tools. Based in Seoul (Seocho-gu), Theres is a portfolio company of 500 Global. The company publishes a consumer web/app storefront and does not currently expose a public developer API, documentation, or integration surface.

providers.name: ThirdLove
providers.description: ThirdLove is a San Francisco-based direct-to-consumer women's intimate apparel brand best known for its online Fit Finder quiz and half-cup bra sizing, selling bras, underwear, and loungewear direct to consumers through its e-commerce site. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of a16z and Felicis. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-21 found no public developer or API surface — no developer subdomain, no documented API, no /.well-known/ discovery documents, and no security.txt or trust-center program. Only a domain-security probe of thirdlove.com yielded real data (TLS 1.3, HSTS, SPF, DMARC).

providers.name: Thread
providers.description: Thread (thread.com) was a UK-based fashion technology company that combined AI with human expert stylists to deliver personalized clothing recommendations for men and women. Founded by Kieran O'Neill and Ben Phillips and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Balderton Capital, Thread's brand, technology and data were acquired by Marks & Spencer. The company subsequently entered administration and has ceased trading; its site now serves only a shutdown notice. Enrichment found no public API, developer portal, documentation, or event surface. This profile is retained as a network record of a defunct portfolio company.

providers.name: Three Squirrels
providers.description: Three Squirrels (三只松鼠) is a Chinese consumer snack company founded in 2012 by Zhang Liaoyuan and headquartered in Wuhu, Anhui Province. Positioned as one of China's first internet-native food brands, it sells nuts, seeds, dried fruits, baked goods, and other leisure snacks primarily through e-commerce channels (Tmall, JD.com, and its own storefronts) alongside a growing offline retail footprint. The company is publicly listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange ChiNext board (stock code 300783). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment; as a consumer packaged-goods retailer it does not publish a public developer API, open platform, or API documentation. Sector: consumer.

providers.name: Ticketmonster
providers.description: Ticketmonster (TMON) is a South Korean e-commerce and social-commerce platform founded in 2010 as "Ticket Monster." Operating primarily at tmon.co.kr (the legacy ticketmonster.co.kr brand), TMON sells deals, daily bargains, fashion, travel, and a broad retail catalog to Korean consumers via web and mobile apps. It grew into one of Korea's leading online marketplaces and was later brought under the Qoo10 group. TMON is a consumer-facing retail/marketplace business; it does not publish a public developer program, API portal, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or documented API surface. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-linked company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline, which confirmed the absence of any public API surface.

providers.name: To Summer
providers.description: To Summer (观夏 / Guanxia) is a Chinese premium home-fragrance and lifestyle brand founded in Beijing, known for its Eastern-inspired scented candles, incense, diffusers, perfumes, and bath and body products. Positioned as a direct-to-consumer scent brand, it sells primarily through its own website, WeChat mini-program, Tmall flagship store, and a growing footprint of physical concept stores across China. To Summer is backed by IDG Capital and was surfaced through the API Evangelist venture-portfolio pipeline. As a consumer retail brand it exposes a customer-facing e-commerce experience rather than a public developer API; this profile captures its identity and the outcome of an enrichment probe that found no public API surface.

providers.name: Toasty
providers.description: Toasty (toasty.family, published by Wenose) is a French consumer mobile application for responsible, sustainable, and ethical shopping. The app curates committed brands and makes conscious consumption engaging through a gamified experience of daily private sales, quizzes, challenges, gifts, and rewards. It reports a 4.9-star rating across the app stores and more than 400,000 downloads. Toasty is a business-to-consumer mobile product with no public developer program, API, or documentation surface at this time; it was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. This profile captures its public identity and a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: Toolsvilla
providers.description: Toolsvilla is an India-based e-commerce marketplace for machinery, tools, and equipment, positioning itself as one of India's largest online stores for industrial, agricultural, and power tools serving small businesses, farmers, and trade buyers. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. No public developer API, documentation, or SDKs were found during this enrichment pass; the site's internal backend at api.toolsvilla.com is undocumented and returns a bare JSON response.

providers.name: Tops Friendly Markets
providers.description: Tops Friendly Markets is a regional supermarket chain headquartered in Amherst, New York operating 152 grocery stores and 58 gas station and convenience stores across upstate New York, northern Pennsylvania, and Vermont. In November 2021 Tops Holding II merged with Price Chopper / Market 32 to form Northeast Grocery Inc, a roughly 300-store regional alliance under common ownership. The Tops consumer brand continues to operate an e-commerce platform with online grocery pickup and DoorDash delivery, the BonusPlus loyalty card program with digital coupons and gas rewards, the MoolahVille cash back rewards program, in-store pharmacies, gift cards, and iOS and Android mobile apps. Vendor and supplier engagement is handled through Northeast Shared Services. No public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, webhook, EDI portal, status page, RSS feed, or changelog is published for the Tops brand.

providers.name: Tractor Supply
providers.description: Tractor Supply Company is the largest rural lifestyle retailer in the United States, providing products to support recreational farming, ranching, and country lifestyles. Tractor Supply integrates with suppliers and vendors via EDI and vendor portal systems, enabling order management, invoice processing, and shipment notifications. The company operates through its vendor transaction portal for supplier collaboration and EDI-based supply chain integrations.

providers.name: Treat.co
providers.description: Treat.co was a consumer gifting e-commerce startup surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. As of this enrichment pass the treat.co domain is controlled by Mars, Incorporated: it resolves to an AWS Application Load Balancer presenting a certificate for alb-redirect.mars.com and returns HTTP 403 on every probed path (homepage, /.well-known/security.txt, /api, /developers), with no MX record for email. The company therefore exposes no public website, developer portal, documentation, or API surface today; it appears dormant or absorbed following acquisition. This profile records the domain-security probe and is retained as a network lead pending any revived or successor developer surface.

providers.name: TryTry (穿穿)
providers.description: TryTry (穿穿, trytrytw.com) was a Taiwanese women's fashion e-commerce brand ("是妳，決定了這件衣服的表情" — "It's you who decides the expression of this dress"), active around 2015-2016 and surfaced as a Qiming portfolio company. The business appears defunct — as of 2026-07-21 trytrytw.com is domain-squatted (wildcard DNS to a parked Chinese web-design page, serving an expired TLS certificate issued for an unrelated host) and no developer, API, or documentation surface exists.

providers.name: TSM
providers.description: TSM (Team SoloMid) is a North American esports and gaming lifestyle organization, surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners in the consumer sector. Its public web presence at tsm.gg redirects to the official TSM Store (tsmshop.com), a Shopify-hosted storefront selling TSM apparel and accessories. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-21 found no first-party developer API surface: no developer portal, no API documentation, no OpenAPI, no resolving developer/api/docs subdomains, and no real /.well-known/ discovery documents (every probed path returned the storefront catch-all page). This profile is retained as a consumer-brand lead with only domain-security signals captured.

providers.name: Tundra
providers.description: Tundra is a business-to-business wholesale marketplace that connects independent retailers with brands and suppliers, letting shop owners discover, source, and order wholesale products across categories online. Backed by Redpoint Ventures, the company operates in the ecommerce sector. As of this enrichment pass Tundra exposes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface: live probes of tundra.com found no developer/api/docs subdomains and no /.well-known discovery documents, and the public www.tundra.com storefront was reachable but served an expired TLS certificate.

providers.name: Virgio
providers.description: Virgio is an India-based direct-to-consumer sustainable fashion brand delivering trend-driven, eco-conscious womens apparel built around circular fashion, recycled and natural fabrics (recycled polyester, organic cotton, viscose, modal, lyocell), ethical production, and zero-waste packaging. It operates as an online-first retail marketplace with a consumer web storefront and mobile app. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and Prosus Ventures; an enrichment probe found a consumer e-commerce presence but no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: Vue
providers.description: Vue (Vue Technology) was an item-level RFID hardware and software company based in Lake Forest, California, backed by Canaan Partners at Series A. Its product family combined RFID readpoints and networking devices with a software platform for real-time, item-level inventory monitoring and tracking, with notable retail rollouts including American Apparel. Tyco's Sensormatic Electronics acquired Vue Technology in October 2008 for approximately $43M, so the company no longer operates as an independent entity. It surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Canaan Partners portfolio lead; enrichment finds no active developer portal, public API, or first-party artifacts to catalog.

providers.name: wantful
providers.description: Wantful was a personalized online gift-giving service founded in 2011 by John Poisson, based in San Francisco and New York City, that let shoppers assemble curated gift books of design-forward products which recipients could browse and redeem for the item they most wanted. Backed by Slow Ventures and others (roughly $5.5M raised) and partnered with Nordstrom, the company shut down in September 2013 after failing to secure follow-on funding. It is defunct — wantful.com resolves (Route53 NS) but serves no live product, and there is no API, documentation, or developer surface to enrich.

providers.name: Wonder Brands
providers.description: Wonder Brands is a Latin American digital-first e-commerce company that builds and operates a portfolio of 15+ consumer product brands (including AlebriPets, Tropical Heal, Somos Reyes, Kingsman, KingsHouse, and KingsPort) spanning mattresses and bedroom furniture, sports equipment, home appliances, travel gear, tools, home and garden furniture, pet and baby products, and personal care. Operating an online-first omnichannel model across Uruguay, Mexico, Colombia, and Chile, it fulfills over 2 million annual orders from 25,000+ square meters of warehouse space, backed by proprietary technology for product optimization, marketing, pricing, and demand forecasting. Backed by QED Investors. The company exposes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Wonderbly *
providers.description: Wonderbly is an online publisher that makes personalized books and gifts for kids and adults. Founded in 2013 (originally as Lost My Name), it lets customers design and buy books customized with a recipient's name, themes, and occasion, and has delighted over 10 million readers worldwide. The consumer e-commerce site operates across 40+ language and regional storefronts (US, UK, AU, CA, DE, FR, NL, IT, ES). Backed by GV. No public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation was found during enrichment; this remains a company profile lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Yunji
providers.description: Yunji (云集) is a leading membership-based social e-commerce platform in China, founded in Hangzhou in May 2015. Yunji curates a wide range of consumer products across health food, beauty, personal care, digital devices, and apparel, and uses a member-driven model in which members earn rewards by sharing products with their social contacts. The company applies big data and artificial intelligence to optimize the shopping experience and incentivize social promotion. Yunji listed on the Nasdaq Stock Exchange (ticker YJ) in May 2019 as the first membership-based Chinese e-commerce firm to do so. Yunji was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass, Yunji operates as a consumer mobile-app commerce platform and publishes no public developer or open API program.

providers.name: Zapp
providers.description: Zapp is a London-based premium quick-commerce (q-commerce) business that delivers daily essentials such as snacks, drinks, groceries, household items and pharmacy needs across central London in minutes, 24/7. Founded in 2020 by Navid Hadzaad and Joe Falter, the company operates a network of micro-fulfilment "dark stores" and a consumer mobile app (iOS and Android) rather than a public developer platform. Zapp is a venture-backed company whose investors include Lightspeed Venture Partners. As of this profile, Zapp exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; it is a business-to-consumer delivery brand surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a company lead.

providers.name: Zappli
providers.description: Zappli was an early mobile-commerce startup, maker of the myShopanion iPhone shopping app, which let consumers browse and shop retail products and share their finds and purchases across social networks such as Facebook and Twitter to get real-time feedback from friends and family. Backed by 500 Global (500 Startups), Founders' Co-op, Techstars, and the Webb Investment Network, Zappli was acquired by Connexity in July 2013 and is no longer operating. It publishes no public API, developer portal, or API documentation, and the zappli.com domain no longer serves a live website.

providers.name: Boxy (ex-Storelift)
providers.description: Boxy, operated by the French company SAS Storelift (founded 2018 in Ivry-sur-Seine by David Gabai and Tom Hayat), built unstaffed 24/7 convenience stores inside 15-20 square metre shipping containers, using computer vision, weight-sensing shelves and an on-site compute node so a shopper could unlock the door with a QR code from the Boxy mobile app, take products off the shelf and walk out to be invoiced automatically. The company raised roughly 5M EUR in 2020 and a 25M EUR Series A in February 2022 led by Serena with CapHorn and LocalGlobe, targeting 1,000 stores. It shut its entire store estate by the end of April 2024, and SAS Storelift entered liquidation judiciaire on 6 November 2024 after sauvegarde and redressement procedures earlier that year; the store containers were auctioned in early 2025. The getboxy.co domain is now parked and returns HTTP 410 Gone on every path, and no developer program, API documentation or machine-readable contract was ever published. This profile records that absence.

providers.name: Brandless
providers.description: Brandless is an American direct-to-consumer e-commerce retailer of own-label food, beauty, personal care and household goods, founded in 2016 by Tina Sharkey and Ido Leffler and launched in July 2017. SoftBank-backed, it ceased operations on 10 February 2020; its assets were bought in June 2020 by Clarke Capital Partners and Ikonifi and the brand relaunched that summer under Utah-based ownership, later led by Cydni Tetro and then Tiffany Vail. The storefront ran on Shopify and sold physical consumer packaged goods only — Brandless never operated a developer program, public API, SDK or webhook surface of its own. As of this profile the brandless.com domain no longer resolves and the site is parked, so there is no live company surface to profile.

providers.name: Builders FirstSource
providers.description: Builders FirstSource (NYSE: BLDR) is the nation's largest supplier and manufacturer of structural building products, value-added components, and construction services to the professional market for single-family and multi-family construction. The company operates approximately 570 locations across 43 states with 28,000 team members, headquartered in Irving, Texas. Its product portfolio includes lumber, manufactured components, doors, windows, millwork, cabinets, and roofing, complemented by digital procurement and project management tools through the myBLDR platform.

providers.name: CaaStle
providers.description: CaaStle Inc. was a New York based business-to-business "Clothing-as-a-Service" company that built white-label clothing rental, subscription and resale infrastructure for apparel retailers, operating tenant-branded storefronts and reverse-logistics for partner brands rather than selling directly to consumers. The company collapsed in 2025: its board confirmed financial distress and furloughed staff in April 2025, and it filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy in the District of Delaware on 20 June 2025 (case 25-11187), electing liquidation over reorganization. Founder and chief executive Christine Hunsicker resigned amid allegations of fabricated financial disclosures and later pleaded guilty to a fraud scheme prosecutors valued in the hundreds of millions of dollars. CaaStle never operated a public developer program, and the caastle.com domain has since passed out of the company's control.

providers.name: Tailored Brands
providers.description: Tailored Brands is a leading specialty retailer of menswear operating the Men's Wearhouse, Jos. A. Bank, K&G Superstores, Moores Clothing for Men, and Joseph Abboud brands. The company operates over 1,000 retail locations across North America and e-commerce platforms at menswearhouse.com, josbank.com, and kgstores.com. Tailored Brands is preparing for an IPO in 2026 following its 2020 restructuring. No public developer API is currently available.

providers.name: Techstyle Fashion Group
providers.description: TechStyle Fashion Group is the El Segundo, California holding company founded in March 2010 by Don Ressler and Adam Goldenberg as JustFab Inc. and renamed TechStyle Fashion Group in August 2016. It builds and operates direct-to-consumer membership fashion brands on a shared, proprietary commerce and personalization platform once marketed as TechStyle OS — Fabletics (with the Yitty shapewear line), Savage X Fenty, JustFab, ShoeDazzle and FabKids — selling apparel, footwear, activewear, intimates and accessories through a VIP membership subscription that gives members monthly credits, member pricing and a monthly skip window. The group reported more than five million paying VIP members and roughly $800 million in revenue as of 2019, and has since reorganized so that Fabletics, Savage X Fenty and the Global Fashion Brands unit (JustFab, ShoeDazzle, FabKids) run as standalone operating companies on the shared supply chain, fulfillment and technology stack. The TechStyle corporate identity itself has been retired: both techstyle.com and techstyleos.com now redirect to a Gandi domain-parking page at techstylefashiongroup.com that answers on plain HTTP only, so the group publishes no corporate site, no developer program, no API reference and no machine-readable contract of its own. The live API surface belongs to the operating brands, which are profiled separately in this network.

providers.name: Academy Sports and Outdoors
providers.description: Academy Sports + Outdoors is a Fortune 500 sporting goods and outdoor recreation retailer headquartered in Katy, Texas. The company operates retail stores across the United States and an e-commerce platform offering sporting equipment, apparel, footwear, hunting and fishing gear, camping supplies, and outdoor recreation products. This repository captures any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts associated with Academy Sports + Outdoors. No public developer APIs or documentation portal have been identified at this time.

providers.name: FirstCash Holdings
providers.description: FirstCash Holdings is a leading international operator of pawn stores and a major provider of retail point-of-sale payment solutions. The company operates pawn store locations across the United States and Latin America, offering pawn loans, retail merchandise sales, and lease-to-own financing through its American First Finance subsidiary. No public developer API or technical documentation portal is currently available.

providers.name: Gap
providers.description: Gap Inc. is a Fortune 500 American clothing and accessories retailer operating brands including Gap, Old Navy, Banana Republic, and Athleta. Gap does not publish a public developer API; this repository tracks the company, its public web presence, and any partner or technical artifacts that surface over time.

providers.name: Hanesbrands
providers.description: Hanesbrands is a global consumer apparel company designing, manufacturing, and selling everyday basic apparel under brands including Hanes, Champion, Bali, Maidenform, and Bonds. In 2025 Hanesbrands was acquired by Gildan, with both companies continuing to operate as a combined apparel leader.

providers.name: Inditex
providers.description: A Spanish multinational fashion group and the world's largest apparel retailer operating brands including Zara, Massimo Dutti, and Pull&Bear. Known for its fast-fashion model with rapid design-to-store turnaround times. No public developer portal or open API catalogue was located on inditex.com.

providers.name: Macy's
providers.description: Macy's, Inc. is one of the nation's premier omnichannel retailers, operating department stores, websites, and apps under the Macy's, Bloomingdale's, and Bluemercury brands. This repository tracks any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable artifacts that are made publicly available by Macy's.

providers.name: Neiman Marcus Group
providers.description: Neiman Marcus Group is an American chain of luxury department stores selling designer apparel, accessories, jewelry, beauty, home, and gifts under the Neiman Marcus, Bergdorf Goodman, and Last Call banners.

providers.name: QVC
providers.description: QVC is a multinational corporation specializing in televised home shopping owned by Qurate Retail Group, broadcasting to millions of households worldwide and offering products through television, mobile apps, and websites.

providers.name: Office Depot
providers.description: Office Depot is a leading provider of business products and services delivering workplace solutions through retail stores, e-commerce sites, and a dedicated business-to-business sales organization.

providers.name: Crocs
providers.description: Crocs, Inc. is a global designer, manufacturer, and retailer of casual footwear known for its iconic molded clog. The company sells through e-commerce, owned retail, and wholesale channels worldwide and also owns the HEYDUDE casual footwear brand. Crocs does not publish a public developer API portal.

providers.name: Dollar General
providers.description: Dollar General is a Fortune 500 discount retailer operating more than 20,000 stores across the United States. Vendor and supplier integration is handled through the DG Partners portal and RangeMe for new vendor onboarding. Dollar General does not currently publish a public REST API.

providers.name: G-III Apparel Group
providers.description: G-III Apparel Group is a designer, manufacturer, and marketer of branded apparel, accessories, and team sports products owning and licensing brands such as DKNY, Donna Karan, Calvin Klein, Tommy Hilfiger, and Karl Lagerfeld Paris.

providers.name: Genesco
providers.description: Genesco is a specialty retailer and branded company selling footwear, apparel, and accessories through more than 1,400 retail stores and e-commerce sites under banners including Journeys, Schuh, Johnston & Murphy, and Genesco Brands.

providers.name: Guess
providers.description: Guess? is a global lifestyle brand that designs, markets, distributes, and licenses a leading lifestyle collection of contemporary apparel and accessories for men, women, and children.
